text:
【任务】BK7258 DevKit（openvela/NuttX，仓 contest2026_098_zhanshangxingguang，分支 dev-ai-contest-2026）功耗优化：修复"摄像头/LCD 命令用完不彻底下电"导致的待机电流偏高。

【实测事实】串表法（UT181A 串电池正极、纯电池供电、拔掉 Type-C）：
- 复位进 NSH、不跑任何命令的干净待机 = ~16mA（正常）。
- 跑 camera velapet 后按 Enter 退出、回到 NSH = ~102mA（多了 ~86mA）。
- 结论：命令退出时没关掉摄像头电源/MCLK 和 LCD LDO_3V3。

【根因（已定位，board/contest_board/src/）】
- bk7258_gc9d01.c 的 bk7258_lcd_preview_deinit() 只关背光(P25)，注释保留 LDO_3V3(P52)。
- bk7258_camera.c 的 bk7258_camera_velapet() 退出路径(stop_lcd/stop_stream)只调 preview_deinit + dvp_ctrl_deconfig()，未做摄像头下电(PWR 置无效 + 关 MCLK)。
- 对照：camera id 的清理里已有完整下电序列（dvp_ctrl_deconfig + dvp_module_clk_disable + 关 MCLK gate + PWR 置无效，日志 "[camera] Cleanup done - pins restored"），可抽成公共函数复用。

【要做】
1. 抽公共函数 camera_power_off()：dvp_module_clk_disable() + 关 MCLK 门 + 摄像头 PWR 置无效(按 CONFIG_CAMERA_PWR_ACTIVE_HIGH 取反) + PWDN 进 standby；幂等、可重复调用。
2. 所有用摄像头/DVP 的命令退出都调用它：velapet、hr、track、buf、preview，以及各 cleanup_ctrl 分支。
3. LCD：先确认 P52(LDO_3V3) 是否只供 LCD（查原理图/代码，必要时上板实测关掉后是否影响别的功能）。确认只供 LCD 就在退出时关 LDO_3V3；不确定则做成宏/参数、默认关、可保留。
4. camera init 里 "MCLK/power left ON for oscilloscope verification" 仅作调试用，不影响正常命令退出下电；正常命令退出必须下电。
5. 不破坏：控制台、各命令可重复运行(退出下电后再跑要能重新上电初始化)、既有功能(心率/眼神/手势)。

【验证（必须上板实测，串表法）】
- reset→NSH→拔 Type-C，基线应 ~16mA。
- 跑 camera velapet → Enter 退出 → 电流应从 ~102mA 回落到 ~16mA。
- 同样验证 camera hr、lcdtest oeye 退出后回落到 ~16mA。
- 每个命令再重复跑一次，确认功能正常(能重新点屏/出图/测心率)。
- 把优化前后电流记录到 docs/续航压测_SOP.md 与 docs/技术报告.md 3.5 的功耗表("velapet 退出后" 102→~16)。

【约束】小步改、每步可编译；以真机串口+串表电流为准；不确定 3.3V 是否共用就做成可开关、别贸然关导致别的功能挂掉。

263	 * Actual SPI clock = 26 MHz / (div + 1).
264	 * Range: 0..255 (CTRL register bits[8:15]).
265	 *
266	 * Measured (51200-byte blit, burst=32, BYTE_INTERVAL=0):
267	 *   div=12 (2.0 MHz) → 740ms / 67 KB/s   (burst=1)
268	 *   div=3  (6.5 MHz) → 120ms / 416 KB/s  (burst=32)
269	 *   div=1  (13 MHz)  →  50ms / 1000 KB/s (burst=32) ← default
270	 *   div=0  (26 MHz)  →  50ms / 1000 KB/s (no gain, polling ceiling)
271	 */
272	
273	static uint32_t g_spi_clk_div = 3;   /* was CONFIG (1); 6.5MHz for
274	                                       * signal integrity under load */
275	
276	/* Runtime-adjustable SPI burst write count.
277	 * Default = CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_BURST (from Kconfig, default 32).
278	 * "lcdtest burst <n>" sets this.  Accepted values: 1, 16, 32.
279	 *
280	 * burst=1: classic per-byte polling via tx_fifo_wr_ready (INT_STATUS bit1).
281	 * burst=16/32: uses tx_fifo_int_level (CTRL bits[1:0]) to set the FIFO
282	 *   interrupt threshold, then polls tx_fifo_int (INT_STATUS bit8) which
283	 *   asserts when the FIFO occupancy <= level.  After the poll, writes
284	 *   N bytes to the FIFO in a tight loop (no per-byte ready check).
285	 *
286	 * Measured (51200-byte blit, lcdtest chunk 4094 sram multi):
287	 *   2.0 MHz  burst=1  →  740ms /   67 KB/s
288	 *   6.5 MHz  burst=1  →  390ms /  128 KB/s
289	 *   6.5 MHz  burst=16 →  120ms /  416 KB/s
290	 *   6.5 MHz  burst=32 →  120ms /  416 KB/s
291	 *   13  MHz  burst=32 →   50ms / 1000 KB/s  ← default combo
292	 *   26  MHz  burst=32 →   50ms / 1000 KB/s  (no further gain)
293	 *   burst=48 → FAIL (FIFO overflow, see below)
294	 *
295	 * The 4 hardware tx_fifo_int levels map to CTRL bits[1:0]:
296	 *   level 0 → occupancy ≤ 0  (burst=1, uses bit1 polling instead)
297	 *   level 1 → occupancy ≤ 16 (empty ≥ 48, safe to write 16)
298	 *   level 2 → occupancy ≤ 32 (empty ≥ 32, safe to write 32)
299	 *   level 3 → occupancy ≤ 48 (empty ≥ 16, safe to write only 16!)
300	 *
301	 * FIFO depth is 64, NOT 48.  The value 48 comes from ARMino's
302	 * SPI_FIFO_INT_LEVEL_48 enum which defines interrupt *thresholds*, not
303	 * capacity.  Safe write count = FIFO_DEPTH (64) - level:
304	 *   level=16 → safe=48, write 16 → OK
305	 *   level=32 → safe=32, write 32 → OK (exactly fits)
306	 *   level=48 → safe=16, write 48 → OVERFLOW (writes 32 extra bytes)
307	 *
308	 * IMPORTANT: tx_fifo_int (bit8) is write-1-to-clear.  It must be cleared
309	 * before each re-poll; otherwise a stale assertion causes an immediate
310	 * pass and the FIFO overflows.
311	 */
312	
313	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_BURST
314	static uint32_t g_spi_burst = CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_BURST;
315	#else
316	static uint32_t g_spi_burst = 32;
317	#endif
318	
319	/* Convert burst count (1/16/32) to CTRL tx_fifo_int_level field (0/1/2/3).
320	 * burst=1 → level 0 (not used for int polling, but valid for register).
321	 * burst=48 is intentionally NOT supported: level=3 only guarantees 16
322	 * empty slots (FIFO_DEPTH=64 minus level=48), but burst=48 writes 48.
323	 */
324	
325	static uint32_t burst_to_fifo_level(uint32_t burst)
326	{
327	  if (burst >= 32) return 2;
328	  if (burst >= 16) return 1;
329	  return 0;
330	}
331	
332	/* Convert CTRL tx_fifo_int_level register value (0/1/2/3) back to the
333	 * byte count that level represents.  NOT the same as the level number!
334	 *   level 0 →  1 byte  (burst=1, per-byte mode)
335	 *   level 1 → 16 bytes
336	 *   level 2 → 32 bytes
337	 *   level 3 → 48 bytes
338	 *
339	 * This mapping is the inverse of the CTRL bits[1:0] encoding.
340	 * Common mistake: using the level number directly as a byte count
341	 * (e.g. level=2 → 2 bytes instead of 32).  See DEBUG_JOURNAL §5.
342	 */
343	
344	static uint32_t fifo_level_to_bytes(uint32_t level)
345	{
346	  switch (level)
347	    {
348	      case 0:  return 1;
349	      case 1:  return 16;
350	      case 2:  return 32;
351	      case 3:  return 48;
352	      default: return 1;
353	    }
354	}
355	
356	/* INT_STATUS bits (spi_struct.h: int_status, REG_0x06) */
357	
358	#define SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_WR_READY     (1u << 1)
359	#define SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_INT          (1u << 8)
360	#define SPI_INT_TX_UNDERFLOW         (1u << 11)
361	#define SPI_INT_TX_FINISH            (1u << 13)
362	#define SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_CLR          (1u << 16)
363	#define SPI_INT_RX_FIFO_CLR          (1u << 17)
364	
365	/* System clock enable register for SPI1 */
366	
367	#define BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG    (BK7258_SYS_BASE + 0x0c * 4)
368	#define SPI1_CLK_ENABLE_BIT          (1u << 9)
369	
370	/* SPI clock source select register (ARMino: sys_hal_spi_select_clock).
371	 * Register: SYS_REG_0x0A at SYS_BASE + 0x0a * 4 = 0x44010028.
372	 *   bit4 = clksel_spi0 (0 = XTAL 26 MHz, 1 = APLL)
373	 *   bit5 = clksel_spi1 (0 = XTAL 26 MHz, 1 = APLL)
374	 */
375	
376	#define BK7258_SYS_CLK_DIV_REG       (BK7258_SYS_BASE + 0x0a * 4)
377	#define SPI1_CLKSEL_BIT              (1u << 5)
378	
379	/* SPI clock: XTAL 26 MHz / (clk_rate + 1).
380	 * CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_CLK_DIV sets the clk_rate field (0-255).
381	 * Default=12 → 26/(12+1) = 2 MHz (conservative for bring-up).
382	 */
383	
384	#define SPI1_CLK_RATE  CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_CLK_DIV
385	
386	/* SPI FIFO depth (bytes).
387	 *
388	 * IMPORTANT: The FIFO is 64 bytes deep, NOT 48.
389	 *
390	 * The value 48 comes from ARMino's SPI_FIFO_INT_LEVEL_48 enum (the largest
391	 * tx_fifo_int_level setting), which was mistakenly copied as the FIFO depth
392	 * in earlier versions.  The ARMino enum defines interrupt *thresholds*, not
393	 * capacity.
394	 *
395	 * Empirical proof (BK7258, clk_div=3 / 6.5 MHz, lcdtest chunk 4094 sram):
396	 *   tx_fifo_int_level=16  → safe to write 16 bytes  (FIFO empty ≥ 48)
397	 *   tx_fifo_int_level=32  → safe to write 32 bytes  (FIFO empty ≥ 32)
398	 *   tx_fifo_int_level=48  → OVERFLOW at write 48     (FIFO empty only ≥ 16)
399	 *
400	 * This only makes sense if FIFO depth = 64:
401	 *   tx_fifo_int asserts when FIFO *occupancy* ≤ level (empty ≥ 64 - level).
402	 *   level=16 → empty ≥ 48, write 16 → safe
403	 *   level=32 → empty ≥ 32, write 32 → safe (exactly fits)
404	 *   level=48 → empty ≥ 16, write 48 → overwrites 32 bytes → corruption
405	 *
406	 * ARMino's FIFO depth is documented as "≥48" (spi_ll.h comment), which is
407	 * consistent with 64 but was read as "exactly 48".  The actual depth is 64.
408	 *
409	 * Safe write count per level: safe = FIFO_DEPTH - level
410	 *   level 16 → safe = 48
411	 *   level 32 → safe = 32
412	 *   level 48 → safe = 16  (NOT enough for burst=48, hence the failure)
413	 */
414	
415	#define SPI_FIFO_DEPTH               64
416	
417	/* Tile buffer size for lcd_fill_rect() HW SPI path.
418	 * Configurable via CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_TILE_BYTES (default 1024).
419	 * Must be ≤4095 (tx_trans_len 12-bit field) and even (RGB565 pixel pairs).
420	 */
421	
422	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
423	#  define SPI_TILE_BYTES  CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_TILE_BYTES
424	#else
425	#  define SPI_TILE_BYTES  SPI_FIFO_DEPTH
426	#endif
427	
428	/* Timeout for SPI status polling loops.
429	 * Max chunk = 4095 bytes @ 2 MHz ≈ 16.4 ms.  Each poll iteration is a
430	 * single getreg32 (~2-3 bus cycles @ 26 MHz CPU) ≈ 0.1 μs.
431	 * 500,000 iterations ≈ 50 ms, which is ~3× the max transfer time.
432	 */
433	
434	#define SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT             500000u
435	
436	/* Minimum data length to use hardware SPI.
437	 * BK7258 SPI does NOT assert tx_finish_int when tx_trans_len == 1
438	 * (observed empirically: all len=1 transfers timeout with
439	 * INT_STATUS=0x00000003, while len>=2 always gets bit13).
440	 * Panel init commands are mostly 1-byte, so routing them through HW SPI
441	 * wastes ~3 ms timeout per byte.  Bit-bang is faster for short writes.
442	 * Set via CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HWSPI_MIN_LEN (default 8).
443	 */
444	
445	#define SPI_HWSPI_MIN_LEN  CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HWSPI_MIN_LEN
446

449	 ****************************************************************************/

451	static bool g_hw_spi_capable;     /* SPI1 initialized successfully */
452	static bool g_pins_in_spi_mode;   /* false=GPIO, true=SPI peripheral */
453	static uint32_t g_saved_sys_clk_en;
454	static uint32_t g_saved_sys_clk_div;  /* SPI clock source select register */

464	  return g_hw_spi_capable && g_active_pins == &g_lcd_left;
465	#else
466	  return false;
467	#endif
468	}

483	/****************************************************************************
484	 * Name: gpio_set_output
485	 ****************************************************************************/
486	
487	static void gpio_set_output(int pin)
488	{
489	  uint32_t cfg = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
490	
491	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;  /* GPIO mode (bit6 = 0) */
492	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;    /* output enable (bit3 active-low: 0 = on) */
493	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_INPUT_EN;     /* input off (bit2: 0=off) */
494	  putreg32(cfg, BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
495	}
496	
497	/****************************************************************************
498	 * Name: gpio_write
499	 ****************************************************************************/
500	
501	static void gpio_write(int pin, int val)
502	{
503	  uint32_t cfg = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
504	
505	  if (val)
506	    {
507	      cfg |= GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT;
508	    }
509	  else
510	    {
511	      cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT;
512	    }
513	
514	  putreg32(cfg, BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
515	}
516	
517	/****************************************************************************
518	 * Name: gpio_set_output_cached
519	 *
520	 * Description:
521	 *   Configure pin as GPIO output and cache the CFG register values
522	 *   for fast putreg32-only writes (no getreg32 read needed later).
523	 *
524	 ****************************************************************************/
525	
526	static void gpio_set_output_cached(int pin, gpio_cache_t *c)
527	{
528	  uint32_t cfg;
529	
530	  c->addr = BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin);
531	  cfg = getreg32(c->addr);
532	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;
533	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;
534	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_INPUT_EN;
535	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT;   /* output = 0 */
536	  putreg32(cfg, c->addr);
537	  c->base_lo = cfg;            /* OUTPUT=0 */
538	  c->base_hi = cfg | GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT; /* OUTPUT=1 */
539	}
540	
541	/****************************************************************************
542	 * Name: gpio_write_fast
543	 *
544	 * Description:
545	 *   Set pin via cached values — no read-modify-write, just a single
546	 *   putreg32.  ~2x faster than gpio_write().
547	 *
548	 ****************************************************************************/
549	
550	static inline void gpio_write_fast(const gpio_cache_t *c, int val)
551	{
552	  putreg32(val ? c->base_hi : c->base_lo, c->addr);
553	}

555	/****************************************************************************
556	 * Name: gpio_set_second_func
557	 *
558	 * Description:
559	 *   Configure a GPIO pin for peripheral (second) function.
560	 *
561	 ****************************************************************************/
562	
563	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
564	
565	static void gpio_set_second_func(int pin, int func_sel)
566	{
567	  uint32_t cfg;
568	  uintptr_t func_reg;
569	  uint32_t shift;
570	  uint32_t val;
571	
572	  cfg = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
573	  cfg |= GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;    /* second function mode (bit6=1) */
574	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;     /* ENABLE GPIO output (active-low: bit3=0=on) */
575	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_INPUT_EN;      /* disable input (bit2=0) */
576	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_PULL_EN;       /* disable pull (bit5=0) */
577	
578	  /* Set drive capacity to 1 for SCK pins (matches ARMino SPI_SET_PIN).
579	   * GPIO capacity is bits[8:9], max=3.  SCK needs stronger drive.
580	   * MOSI uses default capacity=0.
581	   */
582	
583	  if (pin == g_lcd_left.sclk)
584	    {
585	      cfg &= ~(0x3u << 8);        /* clear capacity bits */
586	      cfg |= (1u << 8);           /* capacity=1 for SCK */
587	    }
588	
589	  putreg32(cfg, BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
590	
591	  func_reg = BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(pin);
592	  shift = BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_SHIFT(pin);
593	  val = getreg32(func_reg);
594	  val &= ~(BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_MASK << shift);
595	  val |= ((uint32_t)(func_sel & BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_MASK) << shift);
596	  putreg32(val, func_reg);
597	}

599	/****************************************************************************
600	 * Name: lcd_spi_init
601	 *
602	 * Description:
603	 *   Initialize BK7258 SPI1 for left-screen LCD data transfers.
604	 *   Returns 0 on success, negative errno on failure.
605	 *   On failure, g_hw_spi_capable stays false — caller falls back to bit-bang.
606	 *
607	 *   Init sequence (matching ARMino spi_id_init_common + spi_hal_init
608	 *     + spi_hal_configure + spi_hal_start_common):
609	 *     1. Enable SPI1 module clock, verify by read-back
610	 *     2. Soft-reset (NO CLK_GATE_BYPASS — ARMino doesn't use it)
611	 *     3. Configure CTRL: master, enable, mode 0, 8-bit, MSB first,
612	 *        byte_interval=1, rx_sample_edge=1, interrupt enables
613	 *     4. Configure CFG: TX enable, TX/RX finish int enable
614	 *     5. Clear all interrupt status
615	 *     6. Clear FIFOs
616	 *
617	 ****************************************************************************/
618	
619	static int lcd_spi_init(const lcd_pins_t *pins)
620	{
621	  uint32_t ctrl_val;
622	  uint32_t cfg_val;
623	  uint32_t readback;
624	  uint32_t cfg2;
625	  uint32_t cfg4;
626	  uint32_t func2;
627	  uint32_t func4;
628	  uintptr_t func_reg;
629	  uint32_t shift;
630	
631	  if (pins->sclk != 2 || pins->cs != 3 || pins->mosi != 4)
632	    {
633	      g_hw_spi_capable = false;
634	      return -EINVAL;
635	    }
636	
637	  /* Step 1: Enable SPI1 module clock, verify by read-back */
638	
639	  g_saved_sys_clk_en = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG);
640	  putreg32(g_saved_sys_clk_en | SPI1_CLK_ENABLE_BIT,
641	           BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG);
642	
643	  readback = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG);
644	
645	  if (!(readback & SPI1_CLK_ENABLE_BIT))
646	    {
647	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
648	             "[lcd] SPI1 clock enable FAILED: wrote 0x%08lx, "
649	             "read 0x%08lx\n",
650	             (unsigned long)(g_saved_sys_clk_en | SPI1_CLK_ENABLE_BIT),
651	             (unsigned long)readback);
652	      g_hw_spi_capable = false;
653	      return -EIO;
654	    }
655	
656	  /* Step 1b: Select XTAL as SPI1 clock source.
657	   * ARMino: sys_hal_spi_select_clock(SPI_ID_1, SPI_CLK_XTAL)
658	   * Register 0x44010028 bit5: 0 = XTAL 26 MHz, 1 = APLL.
659	   * Without this, SPI1 may have no clock source and never runs.
660	   */
661	
662	  g_saved_sys_clk_div = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_DIV_REG);
663	  putreg32(g_saved_sys_clk_div & ~SPI1_CLKSEL_BIT,
664	           BK7258_SYS_CLK_DIV_REG);
665	
666	  /* Step 2: Soft-reset (ARMino spi_ll_init — NO CLK_GATE_BYPASS) */
667	
668	  putreg32(SPI_SOFT_RESET, SPI_REG_GLOBAL_CTRL(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
669	
670	  /* Step 3: Configure CTRL — match ARMino spi_ll_init + spi_hal_configure
671	   *
672	   * spi_ll_init sets:
673	   *   soft_reset → byte_interval=1 → rx_sample_edge=1 → fifo_levels=0
674	   *
675	   * spi_hal_configure sets:
676	   *   tx_udf_int_en=1 → rx_ovf_int_en=1 → tx_fifo_int_en=0
677	   *   → rx_fifo_int_en=1 → clk_rate → bit_width → bit_order
678	   *   → cpol → cpha → master → wire3_en=0 → slave_release_int_en=0
679	   *   → tx_finish_int_en=1 → rx_finish_int_en=1 → clear_int_status
680	   *
681	   * spi_hal_start_common (LAST): enable=1
682	   *
683	   * CTRL REG_0x04 layout (spi_struct.h):
684	   *   bit[0:1]   tx_fifo_int_level   = 0
685	   *   bit[2:3]   rx_fifo_int_level   = 0
686	   *   bit[4]     tx_udf_int_en       = 1
687	   *   bit[5]     rx_ovf_int_en       = 1
688	   *   bit[6]     tx_fifo_int_en      = 0
689	   *   bit[7]     rx_fifo_int_en      = 1
690	   *   bit[8:15]  clk_rate            = CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_CLK_DIV
691	   *   bit[16]    slave_release_int_en= 0
692	   *   bit[17]    wire3_en            = 0
693	   *   bit[18]    bit_width           = 0 (8-bit)
694	   *   bit[19]    lsb_first_en        = 0 (MSB first)
695	   *   bit[20]    cpol                = 0
696	   *   bit[21]    cpha                = 0
697	   *   bit[22]    master_en           = 1
698	   *   bit[23]    enable              = 1
699	   *   bit[24:29] byte_interval       = 1
700	   *   bit[30:31] rx_sample_edge      = 1
701	   */
702	
703	  /* tx_fifo_int_level (CTRL bits[1:0]) and tx_fifo_int_en (bit6) are set
704	   * when g_spi_burst > 1.  tx_fifo_int_en gates the tx_fifo_int status bit.
705	   */
706	
707	  uint32_t fifo_lvl = burst_to_fifo_level(g_spi_burst);
708	  uint32_t fifo_int_en = (g_spi_burst > 1) ? (1u << 6) : 0; /* tx_fifo_int_en */
709	
710	  ctrl_val = (1u << 4)  |   /* tx_udf_int_en */
711	             (1u << 5)  |   /* rx_ovf_int_en */
712	             (1u << 7)  |   /* rx_fifo_int_en */
713	             fifo_int_en  |  /* tx_fifo_int_en (when burst>1) */
714	             (fifo_lvl << SPI_CTRL_TX_FIFO_INT_LVL_SHIFT) |
715	             (g_spi_clk_div << SPI_CTRL_CLK_RATE_SHIFT) |
716	             SPI_CTRL_MASTER_BIT |
717	             SPI_CTRL_ENABLE_BIT |
718	             ((uint32_t)CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_BYTE_INTERVAL
719	                       << SPI_CTRL_BYTE_INTERVAL_SHIFT) |
720	             (1u << 30);     /* rx_sample_edge=1 (spi_ll_set_rx_sample_edge) */
721	
722	  putreg32(ctrl_val, SPI_REG_CTRL(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
723	
724	  /* Step 4: Configure CFG — TX enable, TX/RX finish int enable
725	   * (matches spi_hal_configure: tx_en, tx_finish_int_en, rx_finish_int_en)
726	   */
727	
728	  cfg_val = SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT |
729	            SPI_CFG_TX_FINISH_INT_EN_BIT |
730	            SPI_CFG_RX_FINISH_INT_EN_BIT;
731	  putreg32(cfg_val, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
732	
733	  /* Step 5: Clear interrupt status (matches spi_hal_configure last step) */
734	
735	  putreg32(0xFFFFFFFF, SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
736	
737	  /* Step 6: Clear FIFOs */
738	
739	  putreg32(SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_CLR | SPI_INT_RX_FIFO_CLR,
740	           SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
741	
742	  /* Verify CTRL was accepted + check SPI mode config */
743	
744	  readback = getreg32(SPI_REG_CTRL(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
745	
746	  if (!(readback & SPI_CTRL_ENABLE_BIT))
747	    {
748	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
749	             "[lcd] SPI1 CTRL enable FAILED: wrote 0x%08lx, "
750	             "read 0x%08lx\n",
751	             (unsigned long)ctrl_val, (unsigned long)readback);
752	      g_hw_spi_capable = false;
753	      return -EIO;
754	    }
755	
756	  /* Verify SPI controller config matches GC9D01 requirements:
757	   *   mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0), MSB first, 8-bit, master
758	   */
759	
760	  if (readback & SPI_CTRL_CPHA_BIT)
761	    {
762	      syslog(LOG_WARNING,
763	             "[lcd] WARNING: CPHA=1 (expected 0 for mode 0)\n");
764	    }
765	
766	  if (readback & SPI_CTRL_CPOL_BIT)
767	    {
768	      syslog(LOG_WARNING,
769	             "[lcd] WARNING: CPOL=1 (expected 0 for mode 0)\n");
770	    }
771	
772	  if (readback & SPI_CTRL_LSB_FIRST_BIT)
773	    {
774	      syslog(LOG_WARNING,
775	             "[lcd] WARNING: LSB first (expected MSB first)\n");
776	    }
777	
778	  if (readback & SPI_CTRL_BIT_WIDTH_BIT)
779	    {
780	      syslog(LOG_WARNING,
781	             "[lcd] WARNING: bit_width=1 (expected 0 for 8-bit)\n");
782	    }
783	
784	  g_hw_spi_capable = true;
785	  g_pins_in_spi_mode = false;
786	
787	  /* Mux readback diagnostics: print GPIO CFG and func select once.
788	   * Do this here (not per-frame) to avoid syslog overhead.
789	   */
790	
791	  lcd_spi_pins_to_spi();
792	
793	  cfg2 = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(g_lcd_left.sclk));
794	  cfg4 = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(g_lcd_left.mosi));
795	
796	  func_reg = BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(g_lcd_left.sclk);
797	  shift = BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_SHIFT(g_lcd_left.sclk);
798	  func2 = (getreg32(func_reg) >> shift) & BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_MASK;
799	
800	  func_reg = BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(g_lcd_left.mosi);
801	  shift = BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_SHIFT(g_lcd_left.mosi);
802	  func4 = (getreg32(func_reg) >> shift) & BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_MASK;
803	
804	  /* Restore to GPIO mode — pins stay GPIO until data transfer time */
805	
806	  lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
807	
808	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
809	         "[lcd] SPI1 init OK: clk_div=%d (~%d.%d MHz), "
810	         "byte_interval=%d, CTRL=0x%08lX CFG=0x%08lX\n"
811	         "[lcd]   mux: P%d cfg=0x%05lX func=%lu, "
812	         "P%d cfg=0x%05lX func=%lu\n"
813	         "[lcd]   mode: %s, %s, %s, enable=%d\n"
814	         "[lcd]   clk: en_reg=0x%08lX div_reg=0x%08lX "
815	         "(SPI1_en=%d clksel=%s)\n",
816	         (int)g_spi_clk_div,
817	         26 / (int)(g_spi_clk_div + 1),
818	         (26 * 10 / (int)(g_spi_clk_div + 1)) % 10,
819	         CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_BYTE_INTERVAL,
820	         (unsigned long)readback,
821	         (unsigned long)getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE)),
822	         g_lcd_left.sclk, (unsigned long)cfg2, (unsigned long)func2,
823	         g_lcd_left.mosi, (unsigned long)cfg4, (unsigned long)func4,
824	         (readback & SPI_CTRL_CPHA_BIT) ? "CPHA=1" : "CPHA=0",
825	         (readback & SPI_CTRL_CPOL_BIT) ? "CPOL=1" : "CPOL=0",
826	         (readback & SPI_CTRL_LSB_FIRST_BIT) ? "LSB first" : "MSB first",
827	         !!(readback & SPI_CTRL_ENABLE_BIT),
828	         (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG),
829	         (unsigned long)getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_DIV_REG),
830	         !!(getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG) & SPI1_CLK_ENABLE_BIT),
831	         (getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_DIV_REG) & SPI1_CLKSEL_BIT)
832	           ? "APLL" : "XTAL");
833	
834	  return 0;
835	}

837	/****************************************************************************
838	 * Name: lcd_spi_deinit
839	 ****************************************************************************/
840	
841	static void lcd_spi_deinit(void)
842	{
843	  uint32_t val;
844	
845	  if (!g_hw_spi_capable)
846	    {
847	      return;
848	    }
849	
850	  putreg32(0, SPI_REG_CTRL(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
851	
852	  if (g_pins_in_spi_mode)
853	    {
854	      gpio_set_output_cached(g_active_pins->sclk, &g_cache_sclk);
855	      gpio_set_output_cached(g_active_pins->mosi, &g_cache_mosi);
856	      gpio_set_output_cached(g_active_pins->cs,   &g_cache_cs);
857	      g_pins_in_spi_mode = false;
858	    }
859	
860	  /* Restore only the SPI1-related bits in shared clock registers.
861	   * 0x44010030 bit9 = SPI1 module clock enable
862	   * 0x44010028 bit5 = SPI1 clock source select (CLKSEL)
863	   * DVP camera also uses 0x44010028 for its own clock fields.
864	   * Full-word write with the init-time snapshot would clobber DVP bits.
865	   */
866	
867	  val = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG);
868	  val &= ~SPI1_CLK_ENABLE_BIT;               /* clear SPI1 clock enable */
869	  val |= (g_saved_sys_clk_en & SPI1_CLK_ENABLE_BIT);  /* restore original */
870	  putreg32(val, BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE_REG);
871	
872	  val = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_DIV_REG);
873	  val &= ~SPI1_CLKSEL_BIT;                   /* clear SPI1 CLKSEL */
874	  val |= (g_saved_sys_clk_div & SPI1_CLKSEL_BIT);     /* restore original */
875	  putreg32(val, BK7258_SYS_CLK_DIV_REG);
876	
877	  g_hw_spi_capable = false;
878	}

880	/****************************************************************************
881	 * Name: lcd_spi_pins_to_spi / lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio
882	 *
883	 * Description:
884	 *   Only SCLK (P2) and MOSI (P4) are muxed to SPI1 peripheral.
885	 *   CS (P3) and DC (P5) STAY as GPIO outputs — software controls them.
886	 *
887	 *   Why CS stays GPIO: SPI1_CSN is auto-toggled by the controller
888	 *   per byte/transfer.  GC9D01 requires CS low across the entire
889	 *   command+data sequence.  Auto-toggling CS resets the panel state
890	 *   machine and all commands are lost.
891	 *
892	 ****************************************************************************/
893	
894	static void lcd_spi_pins_to_spi(void)
895	{
896	  /* Hardware SPI1 is only wired to the left screen (P2/P4).
897	   * If the active panel is not the left one, do nothing — the caller
898	   * must not attempt HW SPI on the right screen.
899	   */
900	
901	  if (g_pins_in_spi_mode)
902	    {
903	      return;
904	    }
905	
906	  if (g_active_pins != &g_lcd_left)
907	    {
908	      return;
909	    }
910	
911	  /* Only SCLK and MOSI → SPI1 peripheral.  CS stays GPIO. */
912	
913	  gpio_set_second_func(g_active_pins->sclk, 0);  /* SPI1_SCK  func0 */
914	  gpio_set_second_func(g_active_pins->mosi, 0);  /* SPI1_MOSI func0 */
915	
916	  g_pins_in_spi_mode = true;
917	}
918	
919	static void lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio(void)
920	{
921	  if (!g_pins_in_spi_mode)
922	    {
923	      return;
924	    }
925	
926	  /* Restore SCLK and MOSI to GPIO output mode using the ACTIVE panel's
927	   * pins, not hardcoded g_lcd_left.  This prevents corrupting the GPIO
928	   * cache when the active panel has changed since to_spi() was called.
929	   */
930	
931	  gpio_set_output_cached(g_active_pins->sclk, &g_cache_sclk);
932	  gpio_set_output_cached(g_active_pins->mosi, &g_cache_mosi);
933	
934	  g_pins_in_spi_mode = false;
935	}

937	/****************************************************************************
938	 * Name: lcd_spi_write
939	 *
940	 * Description:
941	 *   Write data bytes via hardware SPI1 with timeout-protected polling.
942	 *   Returns 0 on success, -ETIMEDOUT if FIFO stalls.
943	 *   If sent_out is non-NULL, *sent_out receives the number of bytes
944	 *   successfully written before return (0 on success = full len).
945	 *
946	 * HARDWARE NOTE 1: BK7258 SPI does NOT assert tx_finish_int (bit13) when
947	 *   tx_trans_len == 1.  Observed empirically: all len=1 transfers timeout
948	 *   with INT_STATUS=0x00000003, while len>=2 always get bit13.
949	 *   Callers should route len < SPI_HWSPI_MIN_LEN through bit-bang instead.
950	 *
951	 * HARDWARE NOTE 2: tx_en rising edge latches trans_len.
952	 *   The controller loads tx_trans_len into its internal counter on the
953	 *   rising edge of tx_en (0→1).  If tx_en stays 1 across chunks, the
954	 *   new trans_len is never loaded and the FIFO stalls after ~70 bytes.
955	 *   Therefore each chunk MUST: (1) clear tx_en, (2) set trans_len,
956	 *   (3) set tx_en (rising edge).  At the end of each chunk, tx_en must
957	 *   be cleared again so the next chunk gets a fresh rising edge.
958	 *   ARMino reference: spi_driver.c spi_hal_enable_tx() is always a
959	 *   separate register write after spi_hal_set_tx_trans_len().
960	 *
961	 ****************************************************************************/
962	
963	static int lcd_spi_write(const uint8_t *data, size_t len,
964	                         size_t *sent_out)
965	{
966	  size_t remaining = len;
967	  const uint8_t *p = data;
968	  uint32_t cfg;
969	
970	  /* Guard: HW SPI only works with left screen pins (P2/P3/P4).
971	   * If caches point to right screen, CS/DC would go to P23/P7 —
972	   * left screen ignores all data, right screen gets no clock.
973	   */
974	
975	  if (g_cached_pins != &g_lcd_left)
976	    {
977	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
978	             "[lcd] lcd_spi_write called with wrong pins "
979	             "(cached=%s, need left)\n",
980	             g_cached_pins ? "right" : "none");
981	      return -EINVAL;
982	    }
983	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_VERIFY
984	  size_t bytes_written = 0;
985	  size_t chunks_sent = 0;
986	#endif
987	
988	  if (sent_out != NULL)
989	    {
990	      *sent_out = 0;
991	    }
992	
993	  while (remaining > 0)
994	    {
995	      size_t chunk = remaining;
996	      uint32_t poll_cnt;
997	      uint32_t st;
998	
999	      if (chunk > g_spi_max_chunk)
1000	        {
1001	          chunk = g_spi_max_chunk;
1002	        }
1003	
1004	      /* [A] Clear TX/RX FIFO (bit16, bit17).
1005	       * ARMino: spi_hal_clear_tx_fifo → spi_ll_clear_tx_fifo (bit16=1)
1006	       */
1007	
1008	      putreg32(SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_CLR | SPI_INT_RX_FIFO_CLR,
1009	               SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1010	
1011	      /* [A2] Clear status bits 8..14 only (write-1-to-clear).
1012	       * Do NOT write 0xFFFFFFFF — that would pulse bit16/17 (FIFO clear)
1013	       * again, which is unnecessary and could disturb the FIFO state.
1014	       * Bits: 8=tx_fifo_int, 9=rx_fifo_int, 10=rx_finish,
1015	       *       11=tx_underflow, 12=tx_finish, 13=rx_underflow, 14=cs_done
1016	       */
1017	
1018	      putreg32(0x7F00u, SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1019	
1020	      /* [B] Set TX transfer length with tx_en = 0.
1021	       * This must be a SEPARATE step from [C] — the controller latches
1022	       * trans_len on the tx_en rising edge.  If we set trans_len and
1023	       * tx_en=1 in the same write, there is no rising edge for the
1024	       * second chunk (tx_en was already 1 from the previous chunk).
1025	       *
1026	       * ARMino: spi_hal_set_tx_trans_len(size) — only touches trans_len
1027	       *         field, tx_en is left as-is (0 at this point).
1028	       */
1029	
1030	      cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1031	      cfg &= ~SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT;  /* tx_en = 0 — prerequisite for rising edge */
1032	      cfg &= ~(SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_MASK << SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_SHIFT);
1033	      cfg |= (chunk << SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_SHIFT);
1034	      cfg |= SPI_CFG_TX_FINISH_INT_EN_BIT; /* preserve bit2 */
1035	      putreg32(cfg, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1036	
1037	      /* [C] Enable TX — rising edge (0→1) latches trans_len.
1038	       * This MUST be a separate putreg32 from [B].
1039	       * ARMino: spi_hal_enable_tx() — separate register write.
1040	       */
1041	
1042	      cfg |= SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT;
1043	      putreg32(cfg, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1044	
1045	      /* [D] Feed FIFO.
1046	       *
1047	       * g_spi_burst=1 (default): per-byte polling via tx_fifo_wr_ready
1048	       *   (INT_STATUS bit1).  Matches ARMino spi_id_write_bytes_common.
1049	       *
1050	       * g_spi_burst=16/32: uses tx_fifo_int (INT_STATUS bit8).
1051	       *   CTRL bits[1:0] = level (1→16, 2→32).
1052	       *   tx_fifo_int asserts when FIFO occupancy <= level
1053	       *   (i.e. empty >= FIFO_DEPTH(64) - level).
1054	       *   bit8 is write-1-to-clear: must clear before each re-poll,
1055	       *   otherwise a stale assertion causes immediate pass → overflow.
1056	       *
1057	       *   burst=48 is NOT supported: level=3 only guarantees 16 empty
1058	       *   slots, writing 48 overflows.  See SPI_FIFO_DEPTH comment.
1059	       */
1060	
1061	      size_t i;
1062	
1063	      for (i = 0; i < chunk; )
1064	        {
1065	          size_t burst = chunk - i;
1066	          size_t b;
1067	
1068	          if (burst > g_spi_burst)
1069	            {
1070	              burst = g_spi_burst;
1071	            }
1072	
1073	          if (g_spi_burst <= 1)
1074	            {
1075	              /* ---- burst=1: per-byte tx_fifo_wr_ready polling ---- */
1076	
1077	              poll_cnt = SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT;
1078	
1079	              while (!(getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE)) &
1080	                       SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_WR_READY))
1081	                {
1082	                  if (--poll_cnt == 0)
1083	                    {
1084	                      size_t done = (size_t)(p - data) + i;
1085	
1086	                      st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(
1087	                                      BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1088	
1089	                      syslog(LOG_ERR,
1090	                             "[lcd] SPI TX FIFO timeout, "
1091	                             "INT_STATUS=0x%08lx sent=%lu/%lu "
1092	                             "total_done=%lu/%lu\n",
1093	                             (unsigned long)st,
1094	                             (unsigned long)i,
1095	                             (unsigned long)chunk,
1096	                             (unsigned long)done,
1097	                             (unsigned long)len);
1098	                      cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1099	                      cfg &= ~SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT;
1100	                      putreg32(cfg, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1101	                      lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1102	                      if (sent_out != NULL)
1103	                        {
1104	                          *sent_out = done;
1105	                        }
1106	
1107	                      return -ETIMEDOUT;
1108	                    }
1109	                }
1110	
1111	              putreg32(p[i], SPI_REG_DATA(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1112	              i++;
1113	            }
1114	          else
1115	            {
1116	              /* ---- burst>1: tx_fifo_int level polling ---- */
1117	
1118	              /* Clear tx_fifo_int (write-1-to-clear bit8) BEFORE polling.
1119	               * A stale assertion from a previous iteration would cause an
1120	               * immediate pass and FIFO overflow.
1121	               */
1122	
1123	              putreg32(SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_INT,
1124	                       SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1125	
1126	              poll_cnt = SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT;
1127	
1128	              while (!(getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE)) &
1129	                       SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_INT))
1130	                {
1131	                  if (--poll_cnt == 0)
1132	                    {
1133	                      size_t done = (size_t)(p - data) + i;
1134	
1135	                      st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(
1136	                                      BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1137	
1138	                      syslog(LOG_ERR,
1139	                             "[lcd] SPI TX FIFO INT timeout, "
1140	                             "INT_STATUS=0x%08lx sent=%lu/%lu "
1141	                             "total_done=%lu/%lu burst=%lu\n",
1142	                             (unsigned long)st,
1143	                             (unsigned long)i,
1144	                             (unsigned long)chunk,
1145	                             (unsigned long)done,
1146	                             (unsigned long)len,
1147	                             (unsigned long)g_spi_burst);
1148	                      cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1149	                      cfg &= ~SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT;
1150	                      putreg32(cfg, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1151	                      lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1152	                      if (sent_out != NULL)
1153	                        {
1154	                          *sent_out = done;
1155	                        }
1156	
1157	                      return -ETIMEDOUT;
1158	                    }
1159	                }
1160	
1161	              /* Write burst bytes to FIFO (no per-byte ready check).
1162	               * The FIFO has >= burst empty slots at this point.
1163	               */
1164	
1165	              for (b = 0; b < burst; b++)
1166	                {
1167	                  putreg32(p[i + b], SPI_REG_DATA(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1168	                }
1169	
1170	              i += burst;
1171	            }
1172	        }
1173	
1174	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_VERIFY
1175	      bytes_written += chunk;
1176	      chunks_sent++;
1177	#endif
1178	
1179	      /* [E] Wait for TX finish (bit13) — the controller has clocked out
1180	       * all tx_trans_len bytes.
1181	       * ARMino: ISR checks spi_ll_is_tx_finish_int_triggered(status, BIT(13)),
1182	       *         then calls bk_spi_clr_tx → disable_tx.
1183	       * We poll bit13 directly.  Also accept bit11 (tx_underflow) as a
1184	       * secondary indicator — it fires when the FIFO drains faster than
1185	       * expected, which is benign and means data was sent.
1186	       *
1187	       * CRITICAL: do NOT clear INT_STATUS between feeding and waiting.
1188	       */
1189	
1190	      poll_cnt = SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT;
1191	
1192	      for (;;)
1193	        {
1194	          st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1195	
1196	          if (st & (SPI_INT_TX_FINISH | SPI_INT_TX_UNDERFLOW))
1197	            {
1198	              break;
1199	            }
1200	
1201	          if (--poll_cnt == 0)
1202	            {
1203	              size_t done = (size_t)(p - data) + chunk;
1204	
1205	              syslog(LOG_ERR,
1206	                     "[lcd] SPI TX finish timeout, "
1207	                     "INT_STATUS=0x%08lx sent=%lu/%lu "
1208	                     "total_done=%lu/%lu\n",
1209	                     (unsigned long)st,
1210	                     (unsigned long)chunk,
1211	                     (unsigned long)chunk,
1212	                     (unsigned long)done,
1213	                     (unsigned long)len);
1214	              cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1215	              cfg &= ~SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT;
1216	              putreg32(cfg, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1217	              lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1218	              if (sent_out != NULL)
1219	                {
1220	                  *sent_out = done;
1221	                }
1222	
1223	              return -ETIMEDOUT;
1224	            }
1225	        }
1226	
1227	      /* tx_finish_int (bit13) fires when the last byte enters the shift
1228	       * register, NOT when it has fully shifted out.  The final 8 clocks
1229	       * (4 μs @ 2 MHz) may still be in progress.  Disabling tx_en
1230	       * immediately truncates that byte, causing cumulative byte
1231	       * misalignment — visible as diagonal seams on structured content.
1232	       *
1233	       * Cost: 10 μs × 50 tiles/frame = 0.5 ms per frame @ tile=1024,
1234	       * which is 0.24% of 206 ms frame time.  Negligible.  DO NOT
1235	       * remove this delay again without scope-verifying the MOSI line.
1236	       */
1237	
1238	      up_udelay(10);
1239	
1240	      /* [F] Clear completion bits (write-1-to-clear) and disable tx_en.
1241	       *
1242	       * tx_en MUST be cleared here — it is the prerequisite for the next
1243	       * chunk's rising edge.  Without this, the next iteration's
1244	       * [B]+[C] cannot produce a 0→1 transition, and the new trans_len
1245	       * is never latched.  This was previously removed as "redundant"
1246	       * and caused multi-chunk stalls (INT_STATUS=0, sent=70).
1247	       * ARMino: spi_hal_disable_tx() is called after every chunk.
1248	       */
1249	
1250	      putreg32(st & (SPI_INT_TX_FINISH | SPI_INT_TX_UNDERFLOW),
1251	               SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1252	
1253	      cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1254	      cfg &= ~SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT;
1255	      putreg32(cfg, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1256	
1257	      p += chunk;
1258	      remaining -= chunk;
1259	    }
1260	
1261	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_SPI_VERIFY
1262	  if (bytes_written != len)
1263	    {
1264	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
1265	             "[lcd] SPI VERIFY FAIL: requested=%zu written=%zu "
1266	             "delta=%zd chunks=%zu\n",
1267	             len, bytes_written,
1268	             (ssize_t)len - (ssize_t)bytes_written,
1269	             chunks_sent);
1270	    }
1271	#endif
1272	
1273	  if (sent_out != NULL)
1274	    {
1275	      *sent_out = len;
1276	    }
1277	
1278	  return 0;
1279	}
1280	
1281	#endif /* CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI */

1283	/****************************************************************************
1284	 * Name: lcd_spidiag
1285	 *
1286	 * Description:
1287	 *   Minimal SPI1 diagnostic: send 1 cmd byte + 4 data bytes, printing
1288	 *   register snapshots at every decision point.  Invoked as "lcd spidiag".
1289	 *
1290	 ****************************************************************************/
1291	
1292	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
1293	
1294	static void spidiag_decode_ctrl(uint32_t ctrl)
1295	{
1296	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1297	         "[spidiag]   master=%d enable=%d cpol=%d cpha=%d "
1298	         "clk_rate=%lu tx_udf_int_en=%d\n",
1299	         !!(ctrl & SPI_CTRL_MASTER_BIT),
1300	         !!(ctrl & SPI_CTRL_ENABLE_BIT),
1301	         !!(ctrl & SPI_CTRL_CPOL_BIT),
1302	         !!(ctrl & SPI_CTRL_CPHA_BIT),
1303	         (unsigned long)((ctrl >> SPI_CTRL_CLK_RATE_SHIFT) & SPI_CTRL_CLK_RATE_MASK),
1304	         !!(ctrl & (1u << 4)));
1305	}
1306	
1307	static void spidiag_decode_cfg(uint32_t cfg)
1308	{
1309	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1310	         "[spidiag]   tx_en=%d rx_en=%d tx_finish_int_en=%d "
1311	         "rx_finish_int_en=%d tx_trans_len=%lu\n",
1312	         !!(cfg & SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT),
1313	         !!(cfg & SPI_CFG_RX_EN_BIT),
1314	         !!(cfg & SPI_CFG_TX_FINISH_INT_EN_BIT),
1315	         !!(cfg & SPI_CFG_RX_FINISH_INT_EN_BIT),
1316	         (unsigned long)((cfg >> SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_SHIFT) & SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_MASK));
1317	}
1318	
1319	static int lcd_spidiag(void)
1320	{
1321	  uint32_t ctrl;
1322	  uint32_t cfg;
1323	  uint32_t st;
1324	  uint32_t poll_cnt;
1325	  uint32_t cfg_before;
1326	  uint32_t cfg_after;
1327	  uint32_t func_before;
1328	  uint32_t func_after;
1329	  uintptr_t func_reg;
1330	  uint32_t shift;
1331	  int i;
1332	
1333	  static const uint8_t diag_data[4] = {0xaa, 0x55, 0x33, 0xcc};
1334	
1335	  /* Self-contained: ensure left screen pins + SPI1 are initialized.
1336	   * lcd_setup_pins is idempotent (skips if already done for this panel).
1337	   * This allows running "lcdtest spidiag" without a prior "lcdtest go".
1338	   * We only init pins+SPI, NOT the panel display sequence.
1339	   */
1340	
1341	  lcd_setup_pins(&g_lcd_left);
1342	
1343	  if (!g_hw_spi_capable)
1344	    {
1345	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "[spidiag] HW SPI not capable, abort\n");
1346	      return -ENODEV;
1347	    }
1348	
1349	  /* [F-before] GPIO pin state BEFORE mux */
1350	
1351	  cfg_before = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(g_lcd_left.sclk));
1352	  func_reg = BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(g_lcd_left.sclk);
1353	  shift = BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_SHIFT(g_lcd_left.sclk);
1354	  func_before = (getreg32(func_reg) >> shift) & BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_MASK;
1355	
1356	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1357	         "[spidiag] GPIO BEFORE mux: P%d cfg=0x%05lX func=%lu\n",
1358	         g_lcd_left.sclk, (unsigned long)cfg_before,
1359	         (unsigned long)func_before);
1360	
1361	  /* Mux to SPI */
1362	
1363	  lcd_spi_pins_to_spi();
1364	
1365	  /* [F-after] GPIO pin state AFTER mux */
1366	
1367	  cfg_after = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(g_lcd_left.sclk));
1368	  func_reg = BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(g_lcd_left.sclk);
1369	  shift = BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_SHIFT(g_lcd_left.sclk);
1370	  func_after = (getreg32(func_reg) >> shift) & BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_MASK;
1371	
1372	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1373	         "[spidiag] GPIO AFTER  mux: P%d cfg=0x%05lX func=%lu\n",
1374	         g_lcd_left.sclk, (unsigned long)cfg_after,
1375	         (unsigned long)func_after);
1376	
1377	  /* [A] Post-init register dump */
1378	
1379	  ctrl = getreg32(SPI_REG_CTRL(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1380	  cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1381	  st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1382	
1383	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1384	         "[spidiag] [A] post-init: CTRL=0x%08lX CFG=0x%08lX "
1385	         "INT_STATUS=0x%08lX\n",
1386	         (unsigned long)ctrl, (unsigned long)cfg, (unsigned long)st);
1387	  spidiag_decode_ctrl(ctrl);
1388	  spidiag_decode_cfg(cfg);
1389	
1390	  /* --- Start a minimal transfer: 4 data bytes --- */
1391	
1392	  /* Clear FIFO + interrupts */
1393	
1394	  putreg32(SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_CLR | SPI_INT_RX_FIFO_CLR,
1395	           SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1396	  putreg32(0xFFFFFFFF, SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1397	
1398	  /* Set trans_len via read-modify-write */
1399	
1400	  cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1401	  cfg &= ~(SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_MASK << SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_SHIFT);
1402	  cfg |= (4u << SPI_CFG_TX_TRANS_LEN_SHIFT);
1403	  cfg |= SPI_CFG_TX_EN_BIT;
1404	  cfg |= SPI_CFG_TX_FINISH_INT_EN_BIT;
1405	  putreg32(cfg, SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1406	
1407	  /* [B] Post-translen CFG */
1408	
1409	  cfg = getreg32(SPI_REG_CFG(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1410	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1411	         "[spidiag] [B] after set trans_len: CFG=0x%08lX\n",
1412	         (unsigned long)cfg);
1413	  spidiag_decode_cfg(cfg);
1414	
1415	  /* Assert CS (DC=1 for data) */
1416	
1417	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 1);
1418	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
1419	
1420	  /* [C] Feed 4 bytes one at a time */
1421	
1422	  for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)
1423	    {
1424	      poll_cnt = SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT;
1425	
1426	      while (!(getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE)) &
1427	               SPI_INT_TX_FIFO_WR_READY))
1428	        {
1429	          if (--poll_cnt == 0)
1430	            {
1431	              st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1432	              syslog(LOG_ERR,
1433	                     "[spidiag] FIFO timeout at byte %d, "
1434	                     "INT_STATUS=0x%08lX\n",
1435	                     i, (unsigned long)st);
1436	              gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1437	              lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1438	              return -ETIMEDOUT;
1439	            }
1440	        }
1441	
1442	      putreg32(diag_data[i], SPI_REG_DATA(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1443	    }
1444	
1445	  /* [C] After last byte written */
1446	
1447	  st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1448	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1449	         "[spidiag] [C] after last byte: INT_STATUS=0x%08lX\n",
1450	         (unsigned long)st);
1451	
1452	  /* [D] Poll for tx_finish, printing status up to 5 times */
1453	
1454	  {
1455	    int prints = 0;
1456	    poll_cnt = SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT;
1457	
1458	    for (;;)
1459	      {
1460	        st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1461	
1462	        if (st & (SPI_INT_TX_FINISH | SPI_INT_TX_UNDERFLOW))
1463	          {
1464	            break;
1465	          }
1466	
1467	        if (prints < 5)
1468	          {
1469	            syslog(LOG_INFO,
1470	                   "[spidiag] [D] polling: INT_STATUS=0x%08lX\n",
1471	                   (unsigned long)st);
1472	            prints++;
1473	          }
1474	
1475	        if (--poll_cnt == 0)
1476	          {
1477	            st = getreg32(SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1478	            syslog(LOG_ERR,
1479	                   "[spidiag] [E] TIMEOUT: INT_STATUS=0x%08lX "
1480	                   "polls=%lu\n",
1481	                   (unsigned long)st,
1482	                   (unsigned long)SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT);
1483	            gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1484	            lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1485	            return -ETIMEDOUT;
1486	          }
1487	      }
1488	
1489	    /* [E] Success */
1490	
1491	    syslog(LOG_INFO,
1492	           "[spidiag] [E] OK: INT_STATUS=0x%08lX polls=%lu\n",
1493	           (unsigned long)st,
1494	           (unsigned long)(SPI_POLL_TIMEOUT - poll_cnt));
1495	  }
1496	
1497	  /* Clear completion bits */
1498	
1499	  putreg32(st & (SPI_INT_TX_FINISH | SPI_INT_TX_UNDERFLOW),
1500	           SPI_REG_INT_STATUS(BK7258_SPI1_BASE));
1501	
1502	  /* Deassert CS, restore pins */
1503	
1504	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1505	  lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1506	
1507	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[spidiag] done — 4 bytes sent successfully\n");
1508	  return 0;
1509	}

1513	/****************************************************************************
1514	 * Name: lcd_set_pins / lcd_setup_pins
1515	 ****************************************************************************/
1516	
1517	static void lcd_set_pins(const lcd_pins_t *pins)
1518	{
1519	  g_active_pins = pins;
1520	
1521	  /* Rebuild GPIO caches so g_cache_cs/dc/sclk/mosi point to this panel's
1522	   * GPIOs.  Without this, bit-bang writes (spi_write_byte, lcd_send_cmd,
1523	   * lcd_send_data) target the PREVIOUS panel's pins after a switch.
1524	   * This caused: blit using left SPI path but right CS/DC (black screen),
1525	   * and four earlier bugs where g_active_pins was used as a guard but
1526	   * didn't reflect the actual cache state.
1527	   */
1528	
1529	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->sclk, &g_cache_sclk);
1530	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->mosi, &g_cache_mosi);
1531	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->cs,   &g_cache_cs);
1532	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->dc,   &g_cache_dc);
1533	  g_cached_pins = pins;
1534	}
1535	
1536	static void lcd_setup_pins(const lcd_pins_t *pins)
1537	{
1538	  lcd_set_pins(pins);
1539	  gpio_set_output(pins->rst);
1540	
1541	  /* Always set up GPIO mode first — needed for command bit-bang */
1542	
1543	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->sclk, &g_cache_sclk);
1544	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->mosi, &g_cache_mosi);
1545	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->cs,   &g_cache_cs);
1546	  gpio_set_output_cached(pins->dc,   &g_cache_dc);
1547	
1548	  /* Initial idle state: CS=HIGH, DC=HIGH, SCLK=LOW, MOSI=LOW */
1549	
1550	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs,   1);
1551	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc,   1);
1552	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_sclk, 0);
1553	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_mosi, 0);
1554	
1555	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
1556	  /* Initialize SPI1 for left screen — ONCE.  The SPI1 peripheral config
1557	   * (clock, CTRL, reset) persists across panel switches; the right panel
1558	   * bit-bangs its own pins (P22-24) and never touches SPI1.  Re-running
1559	   * the full init on every panel switch (i.e. every eye redraw) was the
1560	   * source of the per-frame "[lcd] SPI1 init OK" spam and frame drops.
1561	   * lcd_spi_deinit() clears g_hw_spi_capable, so the next session
1562	   * re-inits once.  Pins stay GPIO until transfer time (lcd_spi_write
1563	   * mux's them per write).  Failure is non-fatal — falls back to bit-bang.
1564	   */
1565	
1566	  if (pins->sclk == 2 && !g_hw_spi_capable)
1567	    {
1568	      int ret = lcd_spi_init(pins);
1569	
1570	      if (ret < 0)
1571	        {
1572	          syslog(LOG_ERR,
1573	                 "[lcd] SPI1 init failed (%d), using bit-bang\n", ret);
1574	        }
1575	    }
1576	#endif
1577	}

1579	/****************************************************************************
1580	 * Name: spi_write_byte
1581	 *
1582	 * Description:
1583	 *   Bit-bang one byte, MSB-first, SPI mode 0.
1584	 *   Uses cached GPIO values (no getreg32 read).
1585	 *   spi_delay() after each SCLK edge adds timing margin that
1586	 *   prevents window corruption when PSRAM/DVP bus traffic
1587	 *   stalls the CPU mid-transfer.
1588	 *
1589	 ****************************************************************************/
1590	
1591	static void spi_write_byte(uint8_t byte)
1592	{
1593	  int bit;
1594	
1595	  for (bit = 7; bit >= 0; bit--)
1596	    {
1597	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_mosi, (byte >> bit) & 1);
1598	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_sclk, 1);
1599	      spi_delay();
1600	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_sclk, 0);
1601	      spi_delay();
1602	    }
1603	}
1604	
1605	/****************************************************************************
1606	 * Name: lcd_send_cmd / lcd_send_data / lcd_send_cmd_data
1607	 ****************************************************************************/
1608	
1609	static void lcd_send_cmd(uint8_t cmd)
1610	{
1611	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
1612	  /* Commands always use bit-bang — ensure GPIO mode */
1613	
1614	  if (lcd_hw_spi_usable())
1615	    {
1616	      lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1617	    }
1618	#endif
1619	
1620	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 0);
1621	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
1622	  spi_write_byte(cmd);
1623	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1624	}
1625	
1626	static void lcd_send_data(const uint8_t *data, int len)
1627	{
1628	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
1629	  /* Use hardware SPI for data when available (left screen).
1630	   * Switch pins to SPI mode, send, switch back to GPIO.
1631	   * Falls back to bit-bang on timeout.
1632	   */
1633	
1634	  if (lcd_hw_spi_usable() && len >= SPI_HWSPI_MIN_LEN)
1635	    {
1636	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 1);
1637	
1638	      /* Mux SCLK+MOSI to SPI1 peripheral BEFORE asserting CS.
1639	       * Previous code asserted CS first, then muxed — the mux switch
1640	       * can glitch SCLK while CS is low, confusing the panel.
1641	       * After mux, SCLK is driven by SPI1 in mode 0 (CPOL=0) → idle low.
1642	       */
1643	
1644	      lcd_spi_pins_to_spi();
1645	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
1646	
1647	      if (lcd_spi_write(data, len, NULL) == 0)
1648	        {
1649	          gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1650	          lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1651	          return;
1652	        }
1653	
1654	      /* Timeout — fallback to bit-bang */
1655	
1656	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1657	      lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1658	    }
1659	#endif
1660	
1661	  /* Bit-bang fallback */
1662	
1663	  int i;
1664	
1665	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 1);
1666	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
1667	  for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
1668	    {
1669	      spi_write_byte(data[i]);
1670	    }
1671	
1672	  gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1673	}
1674	
1675	static void lcd_send_cmd_data(uint8_t cmd, const uint8_t *data, int len)
1676	{
1677	  lcd_send_cmd(cmd);
1678	  if (len > 0)
1679	    {
1680	      lcd_send_data(data, len);
1681	    }
1682	}

1684	/****************************************************************************
1685	 * Name: lcd_init_sequence
1686	 *
1687	 * Description:
1688	 *   Full GC9D01 init sequence from ARMINO lcd_spi_gc9d01.c.
1689	 *   If display_on is true, sends 0x29 (display on) at the end;
1690	 *   otherwise leaves the display off so the caller can fill the
1691	 *   framebuffer first (avoids flash of uninitialised GRAM).
1692	 *
1693	 *   WARNING: a caller passing display_on=false MUST issue
1694	 *   lcd_display_on() (or lcd_send_cmd(0x29)) itself once the frame is
1695	 *   ready.  Forgetting it yields a lit backlight over a black screen,
1696	 *   which is easily mistaken for a data-path failure — and is masked
1697	 *   whenever an earlier command has already turned the display on, so
1698	 *   it only shows up on a cold boot.  Never rely on display state left
1699	 *   behind by a previous command.
1700	 *
1701	 ****************************************************************************/
1702	
1703	static void lcd_init_sequence(bool display_on)
1704	{
1705	  lcd_send_cmd(0xfe);
1706	  lcd_send_cmd(0xef);
1707	
1708	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x80, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1709	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x81, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1710	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x82, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1711	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x83, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1712	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x84, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1713	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x85, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1714	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x86, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1715	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x87, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1716	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x88, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1717	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x89, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1718	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x8a, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1719	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x8b, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);

1721	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x8d, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1722	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x8e, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1723	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x8f, (const uint8_t *)"\xff", 1);
1724	
1725	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x3a, (const uint8_t *)"\x05", 1);
1726	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xec, (const uint8_t *)"\x01", 1);
1727	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x74,
1728	    (const uint8_t *)"\x02\x0e\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00", 7);
1729	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x98, (const uint8_t *)"\x3e\x99\x3e", 3);
1730	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xb5, (const uint8_t *)"\x0d\x0d", 2);
1731	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x60,
1732	    (const uint8_t *)"\x38\x0f\x79\x67", 4);
1733	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x61,
1734	    (const uint8_t *)"\x38\x11\x79\x67", 4);
1735	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x64,
1736	    (const uint8_t *)"\x38\x17\x71\x5f\x79\x67", 6);
1737	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x65,
1738	    (const uint8_t *)"\x38\x13\x71\x5b\x79\x67", 6);
1739	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x6a, (const uint8_t *)"\x00\x00", 2);
1740	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x6c,
1741	    (const uint8_t *)"\x22\x02\x22\x02\x22\x22\x50", 7);
1742	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x6e,
1743	    (const uint8_t *)"\x03\x03\x01\x01\x00\x00"
1744	                     "\x0f\x0f\x0d\x0d\x0b\x0b"
1745	                     "\x09\x09\x00\x00\x00\x00"
1746	                     "\x0a\x0a\x0c\x0c\x0e\x0e"
1747	                     "\x10\x10\x00\x00\x02\x02"
1748	                     "\x04\x04", 32);
1749	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xbf, (const uint8_t *)"\x01", 1);
1750	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xf9, (const uint8_t *)"\x40", 1);
1751	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x9b, (const uint8_t *)"\x3b", 1);
1752	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x93, (const uint8_t *)"\x33\x7f\x00", 3);
1753	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x7e, (const uint8_t *)"\x30", 1);
1754	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x70,
1755	    (const uint8_t *)"\x0d\x02\x08\x0d\x02\x08", 6);
1756	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x71,
1757	    (const uint8_t *)"\x0d\x02\x08", 3);
1758	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x91, (const uint8_t *)"\x0e\x09", 2);
1759	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xc3, (const uint8_t *)"\x18", 1);
1760	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xc4, (const uint8_t *)"\x18", 1);
1761	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xc9, (const uint8_t *)"\x3c", 1);
1762	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xf0,
1763	    (const uint8_t *)"\x13\x15\x04\x05\x01\x38", 6);
1764	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xf2,
1765	    (const uint8_t *)"\x13\x15\x04\x05\x01\x34", 6);
1766	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xf1,
1767	    (const uint8_t *)"\x4b\xb8\x7b\x34\x35\xef", 6);
1768	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0xf3,
1769	    (const uint8_t *)"\x47\xb4\x72\x34\x35\xda", 6);
1770	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x36, (const uint8_t *)"\x00", 1);
1771	
1772	  lcd_send_cmd(0x34);  /* tearing effect off */
1773	  lcd_send_cmd(0x11);  /* sleep out */
1774	  up_mdelay(120);
1775	
1776	  if (display_on)
1777	    {
1778	      lcd_send_cmd(0x29);  /* display on */
1779	    }
1780	}

1797	 *
1798	 * Description:

1803	
1804	static void lcd_fill_rect(uint16_t x0, uint16_t y0,
1805	                          uint16_t x1, uint16_t y1,
1806	                          uint16_t color)
1807	{
1808	  uint8_t ca[4];
1809	  uint8_t ra[4];
1810	  int npix = (int)(x1 - x0 + 1) * (int)(y1 - y0 + 1);
1811	
1812	  /* CASET */
1813	
1814	  ca[0] = (x0 >> 8) & 0xff;
1815	  ca[1] = x0 & 0xff;
1816	  ca[2] = (x1 >> 8) & 0xff;
1817	  ca[3] = x1 & 0xff;
1818	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2a, ca, 4);
1819	
1820	  /* RASET */
1821	
1822	  ra[0] = (y0 >> 8) & 0xff;
1823	  ra[1] = y0 & 0xff;
1824	  ra[2] = (y1 >> 8) & 0xff;
1825	  ra[3] = y1 & 0xff;
1826	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2b, ra, 4);
1827	
1828	  /* RAMWR + pixel data — use HW SPI for bulk fill when available */
1829	
1830	  lcd_send_cmd(0x2c);
1831	
1832	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
1833	  if (lcd_hw_spi_usable())
1834	    {
1835	      /* Static tile buffer — avoids large stack allocation.
1836	       * SPI_TILE_BYTES defaults to 1024 (configurable up to 4095).
1837	       * At 1024: 51200 bytes / 1024 = 50 SPI transactions per frame
1838	       * (vs 800 at the 64-byte FIFO_DEPTH).
1839	       */
1840	
1841	      static uint8_t tile[SPI_TILE_BYTES];
1842	      uint8_t hi = (color >> 8) & 0xff;
1843	      uint8_t lo = color & 0xff;
1844	      int i;
1845	
1846	      for (i = 0; i < SPI_TILE_BYTES; i += 2)
1847	        {
1848	          tile[i]     = hi;
1849	          tile[i + 1] = lo;
1850	        }
1851	
1852	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 1);
1853	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
1854	      lcd_spi_pins_to_spi();
1855	
1856	      while (npix > 0)
1857	        {
1858	          int batch = npix;
1859	
1860	          if (batch > SPI_TILE_BYTES / 2)
1861	            {
1862	              batch = SPI_TILE_BYTES / 2;
1863	            }
1864	
1865	          if (lcd_spi_write(tile, batch * 2, NULL) != 0)
1866	            {
1867	              goto fill_bb_fallback;
1868	            }
1869	
1870	          npix -= batch;
1871	        }
1872	
1873	      lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1874	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1875	      return;
1876	    }
1877	
1878	fill_bb_fallback:
1879	  /* Restore GPIO mode if HW SPI failed mid-transfer */
1880	
1881	  if (g_pins_in_spi_mode)
1882	    {
1883	      lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1884	    }
1885	#endif
1886	
1887	  /* Bit-bang fallback */
1888	
1889	  {
1890	    uint8_t hi = (color >> 8) & 0xff;
1891	    uint8_t lo = color & 0xff;
1892	    int i;
1893	
1894	    gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 1);
1895	    gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
1896	
1897	    for (i = 0; i < npix; i++)
1898	      {
1899	        spi_write_byte(hi);
1900	        spi_write_byte(lo);
1901	      }
1902	
1903	    gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1904	  }
1905	}

1907	/****************************************************************************
1908	 * Name: bk7258_lcd_blit_rgb565
1909	 *
1910	 * Description:
1911	 *   Blit a full RGB565 framebuffer to the LCD.
1912	 *   Sends CASET/RASET/RAMWR then streams pixel data in rows.
1913	 *
1914	 *   panel: 0=left (SPI1 HW), 1=right (bit-bang), other=left
1915	 *
1916	 ****************************************************************************/
1917	
1918	void bk7258_lcd_blit_rgb565(int panel,
1919	                             uint16_t x0, uint16_t y0,
1920	                             uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
1921	                             const uint8_t *rgb565)
1922	{
1923	  uint8_t ca[4];
1924	  uint8_t ra[4];
1925	  uint16_t x1 = x0 + w - 1;
1926	  uint16_t y1 = y0 + h - 1;
1927	
1928	  /* Auto-switch panel if different from current */
1929	
1930	  if (panel == 1 && g_active_pins != &g_lcd_right)
1931	    {
1932	      lcd_set_pins(&g_lcd_right);
1933	      lcd_setup_pins(&g_lcd_right);
1934	    }
1935	  else if (panel != 1 && g_active_pins != &g_lcd_left)
1936	    {
1937	      lcd_set_pins(&g_lcd_left);
1938	      lcd_setup_pins(&g_lcd_left);
1939	    }
1940	
1941	  /* CASET */
1942	
1943	  ca[0] = (x0 >> 8) & 0xff;
1944	  ca[1] = x0 & 0xff;
1945	  ca[2] = (x1 >> 8) & 0xff;
1946	  ca[3] = x1 & 0xff;
1947	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2a, ca, 4);
1948	
1949	  /* RASET */
1950	
1951	  ra[0] = (y0 >> 8) & 0xff;
1952	  ra[1] = y0 & 0xff;
1953	  ra[2] = (y1 >> 8) & 0xff;
1954	  ra[3] = y1 & 0xff;
1955	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2b, ra, 4);
1956	
1957	  /* RAMWR — CS must stay LOW for entire pixel transfer (GC9D01 datasheet).
1958	   * lcd_spi_write() internally chunks by SPI_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES (1024)
1959	   * without touching CS, so a single call for the whole frame is safe.
1960	   */
1961	
1962	  lcd_send_cmd(0x2c);
1963	
1964	#ifdef CONFIG_LCD_GC9D01_HW_SPI
1965	  /* Use HW SPI for pixel data when available (left screen only) */
1966	
1967	  if (lcd_hw_spi_usable())
1968	    {
1969	      int total = (int)w * (int)h * 2;
1970	      size_t sent = 0;
1971	
1972	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 1);
1973	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
1974	      lcd_spi_pins_to_spi();
1975	
1976	      if (lcd_spi_write(rgb565, total, &sent) != 0)
1977	        {
1978	          /* HW SPI timeout mid-frame.
1979	           * RAMWR pointer has advanced by 'sent' bytes — we cannot
1980	           * reliably resume or resend.  Abort cleanly: raise CS to
1981	           * terminate RAMWR, restore GPIO, log and return.
1982	           * A partially-drawn frame is better than a garbled one.
1983	           */
1984	
1985	          gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1986	          syslog(LOG_ERR,
1987	                 "[blit] HW SPI timeout, abort frame "
1988	                 "(sent=%lu/%d)\n",
1989	                 (unsigned long)sent, total);
1990	          return;
1991	        }
1992	
1993	      lcd_spi_pins_to_gpio();
1994	      gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
1995	      return;
1996	    }
1997	#endif
1998	
1999	  /* Bit-bang fallback (right screen, or HW SPI not compiled in).
2000	   * CS stays LOW for the entire transfer — same as lcd_fill_rect() and
2001	   * lcdtest_pat().  Each pixel is 2 bytes (RGB565 big-endian).
2002	   */
2003	
2004	  {
2005	    int i;
2006	    int total = (int)w * (int)h;
2007	
2008	    gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_dc, 1);
2009	    gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 0);
2010	
2011	    for (i = 0; i < total; i++)
2012	      {
2013	        spi_write_byte(rgb565[0]);
2014	        spi_write_byte(rgb565[1]);
2015	        rgb565 += 2;
2016	      }
2017	
2018	    gpio_write_fast(&g_cache_cs, 1);
2019	  }
2020	}

2023	 * Name: bk7258_lcd_preview_init
2024	 *
2025	 * Description:
2026	 *   Initialize the left-screen LCD for camera preview use.
2027	 *   Enables LDO_3V3 (P52), backlight (P25), configures SPI pins,
2028	 *   resets GC9D01, runs init sequence, turns display on, fills
2029	 *   with black to confirm screen is alive.
2030	 *
2031	 *   Reuses the same static functions that lcdtest uses — no
2032	 *   duplicated init sequence.
2033	 *
2034	 *   Safe to call even if lcdtest has previously run — pin setup
2035	 *   is idempotent (gpio_set_output + cached values).
2036	 *
2037	 * Returns:
2038	 *   0 on success.
2039	 *
2040	 ****************************************************************************/
2041	
2042	int bk7258_lcd_preview_init(void)
2043	{
2044	  /* LCD 3.3V power supply — P52 enables U3 (ME6211C33 LDO) */
2045	
2046	  gpio_set_output(LCD_PIN_LDO33_EN);
2047	  gpio_write(LCD_PIN_LDO33_EN, 1);
2048	  up_mdelay(50);
2049	
2050	  /* Backlight on */
2051	
2052	  gpio_set_output(LCD_PIN_BL);
2053	  gpio_write(LCD_PIN_BL, 1);
2054	
2055	  /* --- Left screen (P2/P3/P4/P5/P45) --- */
2056	
2057	  lcd_setup_pins(&g_lcd_left);
2058	
2059	  gpio_write(g_lcd_left.rst, 0);
2060	  up_mdelay(15);
2061	  gpio_write(g_lcd_left.rst, 1);
2062	  up_mdelay(120);
2063	
2064	  lcd_init_sequence(true);
2065	  lcd_fill_rect(0, 0, LCD_WIDTH - 1, LCD_HEIGHT - 1, 0x0000);
2066	
2067	  /* --- Right screen (P22/P23/P24/P7/P6) — bit-bang only --- */
2068	
2069	  lcd_setup_pins(&g_lcd_right);
2070	
2071	  gpio_write(g_lcd_right.rst, 0);
2072	  up_mdelay(15);
2073	  gpio_write(g_lcd_right.rst, 1);
2074	  up_mdelay(120);
2075	
2076	  lcd_init_sequence(true);
2077	  lcd_fill_rect(0, 0, LCD_WIDTH - 1, LCD_HEIGHT - 1, 0x0000);
2078	
2079	  /* Switch back to left as default active panel */
2080	
2081	  lcd_set_pins(&g_lcd_left);
2082	
2083	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
2084	         "[lcd] dual-screen init done, HW SPI %s\n",
2085	         lcd_hw_spi_usable() ? "ON (left screen)" : "OFF (bit-bang)");
2086	
2087	  return 0;
2088	}

2109	/****************************************************************************
2110	 * Name: sqrt_int — integer square root (Newton's method)
2111	 ****************************************************************************/
2112	
2113	static int16_t sqrt_int(int32_t val)
2114	{
2115	  int32_t guess;
2116	  int32_t next;
2117	  int i;
2118	
2119	  if (val <= 0)
2120	    {
2121	      return 0;
2122	    }
2123	
2124	  guess = val;
2125	
2126	  for (i = 0; i < 10; i++)
2127	    {
2128	      next = (guess + val / guess) / 2;
2129	
2130	      if (next >= guess)
2131	        {
2132	          break;
2133	        }
2134	
2135	      guess = next;
2136	    }
2137	
2138	  return (int16_t)guess;
2139	}

2141	/****************************************************************************
2142	 * Name: lcd_fill_circle
2143	 *
2144	 * Description:
2145	 *   Fill a circle centred at (cx,cy) with radius r using scanline
2146	 *   rendering.  Each scanline is a 1px-high lcd_fill_rect call.
2147	 *
2148	 ****************************************************************************/
2149	
2150	static void lcd_fill_circle(int16_t cx, int16_t cy, int16_t r,
2151	                            uint16_t color)
2152	{
2153	  int16_t y;
2154	  int16_t dx;
2155	  int16_t x0;
2156	  int16_t x1;
2157	  int32_t r2 = (int32_t)r * r;
2158	
2159	  for (y = cy - r; y <= cy + r; y++)
2160	    {
2161	      int32_t dy  = (int32_t)(y - cy);
2162	      int32_t rem = r2 - dy * dy;
2163	
2164	      if (rem < 0)
2165	        {
2166	          continue;
2167	        }
2168	
2169	      dx = sqrt_int(rem);
2170	      x0 = cx - dx;
2171	      x1 = cx + dx;
2172	
2173	      if (x0 < 0)
2174	        {
2175	          x0 = 0;
2176	        }
2177	
2178	      if (x1 >= LCD_WIDTH)
2179	        {
2180	          x1 = LCD_WIDTH - 1;
2181	        }
2182	
2183	      if (y < 0 || y >= LCD_HEIGHT)
2184	        {
2185	          continue;
2186	        }
2187	
2188	      lcd_fill_rect(x0, y, x1, y, color);
2189	    }
2190	}

2192	/****************************************************************************
2193	 * Name: lcd_fill_round_rect
2194	 *
2195	 * Description:
2196	 *   Fill a rounded rectangle centred at (cx,cy), width w, height h,
2197	 *   corner radius r.  Built from one inner rect + four corner circles.
2198	 *
2199	 ****************************************************************************/
2200	
2201	static void lcd_fill_round_rect(int16_t cx, int16_t cy,
2202	                                int16_t w, int16_t h,
2203	                                int16_t r, uint16_t color)
2204	{
2205	  int16_t x0 = cx - w / 2;
2206	  int16_t y0 = cy - h / 2;
2207	  int16_t x1 = cx + w / 2;
2208	  int16_t y1 = cy + h / 2;
2209	
2210	  /* Horizontal centre strip (full width, reduced height) */
2211	
2212	  lcd_fill_rect(x0, y0 + r, x1, y1 - r, color);
2213	
2214	  /* Vertical centre strip (reduced width, full height) */
2215	
2216	  lcd_fill_rect(x0 + r, y0, x1 - r, y1, color);
2217	
2218	  /* Four corner circles */
2219	
2220	  lcd_fill_circle(x0 + r, y0 + r, r, color);
2221	  lcd_fill_circle(x1 - r, y0 + r, r, color);
2222	  lcd_fill_circle(x0 + r, y1 - r, r, color);
2223	  lcd_fill_circle(x1 - r, y1 - r, r, color);
2224	}

2292	/****************************************************************************
2293	 * Name: eye_move_pupil
2294	 *
2295	 * Description:
2296	 *   Stream-based local update: composite one bounding-box region into
2297	 *   a RAM buffer (highlight > pupil > iris > background), then blast
2298	 *   it to the LCD in a single CASET/RASET/RAMWR sequence.
2299	 *   Eliminates the per-circle command storm that caused horizontal
2300	 *   tearing when DVP interrupts preempted mid-draw.
2301	 *
2302	 ****************************************************************************/
2303	
2304	static void eye_move_pupil(int old_dx, int new_dx)
2305	{
2306	  static uint8_t buf[128 * 52 * 2];
2307	  int old_cx = EYE_CX + old_dx;
2308	  int new_cx = EYE_CX + new_dx;
2309	  int hx = new_cx - 8;
2310	  int hy = EYE_CY - 10;
2311	  int x0;
2312	  int x1;
2313	  int y0;
2314	  int y1;
2315	  int w;
2316	  int h;
2317	  int x;
2318	  int y;
2319	  int idx;
2320	  uint8_t ca[4];
2321	  uint8_t ra[4];
2322	
2323	  /* Bounding box covering old + new pupil + highlight, with 2px pad */
2324	
2325	  x0 = (old_cx < new_cx ? old_cx : new_cx) - EYE_PUPIL_R - 2;
2326	  x1 = (old_cx > new_cx ? old_cx : new_cx) + EYE_PUPIL_R + 2;
2327	  y0 = EYE_CY - EYE_PUPIL_R - 2;
2328	  y1 = EYE_CY + EYE_PUPIL_R + 2;
2329	
2330	  /* Clamp to iris circle and screen bounds */
2331	
2332	  if (x0 < EYE_CX - EYE_IRIS_R) x0 = EYE_CX - EYE_IRIS_R;
2333	  if (x1 > EYE_CX + EYE_IRIS_R) x1 = EYE_CX + EYE_IRIS_R;
2334	  if (x0 < 0) x0 = 0;
2335	  if (y0 < 0) y0 = 0;
2336	  if (x1 > LCD_WIDTH  - 1) x1 = LCD_WIDTH  - 1;
2337	  if (y1 > LCD_HEIGHT - 1) y1 = LCD_HEIGHT - 1;
2338	
2339	  w = x1 - x0 + 1;
2340	  h = y1 - y0 + 1;
2341	  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0 || w * h * 2 > (int)sizeof(buf)) return;
2342	
2343	  /* Per-pixel composite: highlight(white) > pupil(black) >
2344	   * iris(cyan) > background(black)
2345	   */
2346	
2347	  idx = 0;
2348	  for (y = y0; y <= y1; y++)
2349	    {
2350	      int dyp = y - EYE_CY;
2351	      int dyh = y - hy;
2352	
2353	      for (x = x0; x <= x1; x++)
2354	        {
2355	          int dxp = x - new_cx;
2356	          int dxh = x - hx;
2357	          int dxi = x - EYE_CX;
2358	          int dyi = y - EYE_CY;
2359	          uint16_t c;
2360	
2361	          if (dxh * dxh + dyh * dyh <=
2362	              EYE_HIGHLIGHT_R * EYE_HIGHLIGHT_R)
2363	            {
2364	              c = 0xffff;
2365	            }
2366	          else if (dxp * dxp + dyp * dyp <=
2367	                   EYE_PUPIL_R * EYE_PUPIL_R)
2368	            {
2369	              c = 0x0000;
2370	            }
2371	          else if (dxi * dxi + dyi * dyi <=
2372	                   EYE_IRIS_R * EYE_IRIS_R)
2373	            {
2374	              c = 0x07ff;
2375	            }
2376	          else
2377	            {
2378	              c = 0x0000;
2379	            }
2380	
2381	          buf[idx++] = (uint8_t)((c >> 8) & 0xff);
2382	          buf[idx++] = (uint8_t)(c & 0xff);
2383	        }
2384	    }
2385	
2386	  /* Single window open + one data stream, no per-row commands */
2387	
2388	  ca[0] = (uint8_t)((x0 >> 8) & 0xff);
2389	  ca[1] = (uint8_t)(x0 & 0xff);
2390	  ca[2] = (uint8_t)((x1 >> 8) & 0xff);
2391	  ca[3] = (uint8_t)(x1 & 0xff);
2392	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2a, ca, 4);
2393	
2394	  ra[0] = (uint8_t)((y0 >> 8) & 0xff);
2395	  ra[1] = (uint8_t)(y0 & 0xff);
2396	  ra[2] = (uint8_t)((y1 >> 8) & 0xff);
2397	  ra[3] = (uint8_t)(y1 & 0xff);
2398	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2b, ra, 4);
2399	
2400	  lcd_send_cmd(0x2c);
2401	  lcd_send_data(buf, w * h * 2);
2402	}

2404	/****************************************************************************
2405	 * Name: eye_compose_full
2406	 *
2407	 * Description:
2408	 *   Full-eye single-window stream render.  Composites iris, pupil,
2409	 *   highlight, and optional upper eyelid into a RAM buffer, then
2410	 *   blasts it to the LCD in one CASET/RASET/RAMWR sequence.
2411	 *
2412	 *   Priority: highlight(white) > eyelid(black) > pupil(black) >
2413	 *             iris(cyan) > background(black).
2414	 *
2415	 ****************************************************************************/
2416	
2417	static void eye_compose_full(int gaze_dx, int pupil_r,
2418	                              int lid_top_y, int lid_bot_y)
2419	{
2420	  static uint8_t buf[120 * 120 * 2]; /* ~28 KB, covers full iris */
2421	  int pcx = EYE_CX + gaze_dx;
2422	  int hx = pcx - 8;
2423	  int hy = EYE_CY - 10;
2424	  int x0 = EYE_CX - EYE_IRIS_R;
2425	  int x1 = EYE_CX + EYE_IRIS_R;
2426	  int y0 = EYE_CY - EYE_IRIS_R;
2427	  int y1 = EYE_CY + EYE_IRIS_R;
2428	  int w;
2429	  int h;
2430	  int x;
2431	  int y;
2432	  int idx;
2433	  int ir2 = EYE_IRIS_R * EYE_IRIS_R;
2434	  int pr2 = pupil_r * pupil_r;
2435	  int hr2 = EYE_HIGHLIGHT_R * EYE_HIGHLIGHT_R;
2436	  uint8_t ca[4];
2437	  uint8_t ra[4];
2438	
2439	  if (x0 < 0) x0 = 0;
2440	  if (y0 < 0) y0 = 0;
2441	  if (x1 > LCD_WIDTH  - 1) x1 = LCD_WIDTH  - 1;
2442	  if (y1 > LCD_HEIGHT - 1) y1 = LCD_HEIGHT - 1;
2443	
2444	  w = x1 - x0 + 1;
2445	  h = y1 - y0 + 1;
2446	  if (w <= 0 || h <= 0 || w * h * 2 > (int)sizeof(buf)) return;
2447	
2448	  idx = 0;
2449	  for (y = y0; y <= y1; y++)
2450	    {
2451	      int dyi = y - EYE_CY;
2452	      int dyh = y - hy;
2453	      int dyp = y - EYE_CY;
2454	
2455	      for (x = x0; x <= x1; x++)
2456	        {
2457	          int dxi = x - EYE_CX;
2458	          int dxh = x - hx;
2459	          int dxp = x - pcx;
2460	          uint16_t c;
2461	
2462	          if (dxi * dxi + dyi * dyi > ir2)
2463	            {
2464	              /* Outside iris: background black */
2465	
2466	              c = 0x0000;
2467	            }
2468	          else if (y < lid_top_y || y > lid_bot_y)
2469	            {
2470	              /* Eyelid (upper or lower): black */
2471	
2472	              c = 0x0000;
2473	            }
2474	          else if (dxh * dxh + dyh * dyh <= hr2)
2475	            {
2476	              /* Highlight: white */
2477	
2478	              c = 0xffff;
2479	            }
2480	          else if (dxp * dxp + dyp * dyp <= pr2)
2481	            {
2482	              /* Pupil: black */
2483	
2484	              c = 0x0000;
2485	            }
2486	          else
2487	            {
2488	              /* Iris: cyan */
2489	
2490	              c = 0x07ff;
2491	            }
2492	
2493	          buf[idx++] = (uint8_t)((c >> 8) & 0xff);
2494	          buf[idx++] = (uint8_t)(c & 0xff);
2495	        }
2496	    }
2497	
2498	  ca[0] = (uint8_t)((x0 >> 8) & 0xff);
2499	  ca[1] = (uint8_t)(x0 & 0xff);
2500	  ca[2] = (uint8_t)((x1 >> 8) & 0xff);
2501	  ca[3] = (uint8_t)(x1 & 0xff);
2502	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2a, ca, 4);
2503	
2504	  ra[0] = (uint8_t)((y0 >> 8) & 0xff);
2505	  ra[1] = (uint8_t)(y0 & 0xff);
2506	  ra[2] = (uint8_t)((y1 >> 8) & 0xff);
2507	  ra[3] = (uint8_t)(y1 & 0xff);
2508	  lcd_send_cmd_data(0x2b, ra, 4);
2509	
2510	  lcd_send_cmd(0x2c);
2511	  lcd_send_data(buf, w * h * 2);
2512	}

2564	/****************************************************************************
2565	 * Name: eye_blink
2566	 *
2567	 * Description:
2568	 *   Quick blink: fill iris area black, pause, then redraw fully.
2569	 *
2570	 ****************************************************************************/
2571	
2572	static void eye_blink(int gaze_dx)
2573	{
2574	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[eye] blink (gaze_dx=%d)\n", gaze_dx);
2575	
2576	  /* Closed eye: lid pushed below iris → entire iris disc goes black.
2577	   * Uses eye_compose_full rasterization — same boundary as open eye,
2578	   * pixel-perfect, no residual ring, single-window stream.
2579	   */
2580	
2581	  eye_compose_full(gaze_dx, EYE_PUPIL_R,
2582	                    EYE_CY + EYE_IRIS_R + 1,   /* lid_top below iris → all black */
2583	                    EYE_CY - EYE_IRIS_R - 1);  /* lid_bot above iris → all black */
2584	  up_mdelay(120);
2585	
2586	  /* Open eye: normal, no eyelid */
2587	
2588	  eye_compose_full(gaze_dx, EYE_PUPIL_R, EYE_CY - EYE_IRIS_R,
2589	                    EYE_CY + EYE_IRIS_R + 1);
2590	}
