2592	/****************************************************************************
2593	 * Name: bk7258_lcd_eye_expr
2594	 *
2595	 * Description:
2596	 *   Draw a full eye with expression on the specified panel.
2597	 *   Uses single-window stream rendering (eye_compose_full).
2598	 *
2599	 *   EYE_EXPR_NEUTRAL: normal eye, pupil r=22, no eyelid
2600	 *   EYE_EXPR_SLEEPY:  half-closed, pupil r=22, lid at EYE_CY
2601	 *   EYE_EXPR_WAKE:    surprised, pupil r=30, no eyelid
2602	 *   EYE_EXPR_HAPPY:   squinting, pupil r=22, top/bottom lid narrow strip
2603	 *
2604	 ****************************************************************************/
2605	
2606	void bk7258_lcd_eye_expr(int panel, int expr, int gaze_dx)
2607	{
2608	  int pupil_r;
2609	  int lid_top_y;
2610	  int lid_bot_y;
2611	
2612	  /* Switch panel */
2613	
2614	  if (panel == 1 && g_active_pins != &g_lcd_right)
2615	    {
2616	      lcd_set_pins(&g_lcd_right);
2617	      lcd_setup_pins(&g_lcd_right);
2618	    }
2619	  else if (panel != 1 && g_active_pins != &g_lcd_left)
2620	    {
2621	      lcd_set_pins(&g_lcd_left);
2622	      lcd_setup_pins(&g_lcd_left);
2623	    }
2624	
2625	  /* Map expression to parameters */
2626	
2627	  switch (expr)
2628	    {
2629	      case EYE_EXPR_SLEEPY:
2630	        pupil_r = EYE_PUPIL_R;
2631	        lid_top_y = EYE_CY;               /* upper half covered */
2632	        lid_bot_y = EYE_CY + EYE_IRIS_R + 1; /* no lower lid */
2633	        break;
2634	
2635	      case EYE_EXPR_WAKE:
2636	        pupil_r = 30;                      /* dilated, surprised */
2637	        lid_top_y = EYE_CY - EYE_IRIS_R;  /* no upper lid */
2638	        lid_bot_y = EYE_CY + EYE_IRIS_R + 1; /* no lower lid */
2639	        break;
2640	
2641	      case EYE_EXPR_HAPPY:
2642	        pupil_r = EYE_PUPIL_R;
2643	        lid_top_y = EYE_CY - 18;          /* upper lid pressed down */
2644	        lid_bot_y = EYE_CY + 18;          /* lower lid raised up */
2645	        break;                             /* → squinting happy strip */
2646	
2647	      case EYE_EXPR_NEUTRAL:
2648	      default:
2649	        pupil_r = EYE_PUPIL_R;
2650	        lid_top_y = EYE_CY - EYE_IRIS_R;  /* no upper lid */
2651	        lid_bot_y = EYE_CY + EYE_IRIS_R + 1; /* no lower lid */
2652	        break;
2653	    }
2654	
2655	  eye_compose_full(gaze_dx, pupil_r, lid_top_y, lid_bot_y);
2656	}

2763	 * Official-website-style eye: white bg + blue iris + black eyelids
2764	 *
2765	 * Color palette (RGB565):
2766	 *   0xFFFF  white  (background)
2767	 *   0x02DF  sky-blue (iris) — try 0x001F for deeper blue
2768	 *   0x0000  black  (pupil, eyelids)
2769	 *   0xFFFF  white  (highlight)

2773	#define OEYE_IRIS      0x02DF  /* sky-blue */
2774	#define OEYE_PUPIL     0x0000  /* black */
2775	#define OEYE_HL        0xFFFF  /* white highlight */
2776	#define OEYE_LID       0x0000  /* black eyelid */
2777	
2778	#define OEYE_IRIS_R    56     /* blue iris with visible white border */
2779	#define OEYE_PUPIL_R   28     /* black pupil */
2780	#define OEYE_HL1_R     10     /* primary highlight upper-left */
2781	#define OEYE_HL1_X     68     /* primary highlight centre */
2782	#define OEYE_HL1_Y     68
2783	#define OEYE_HL2_R     4      /* secondary highlight lower-right */
2784	#define OEYE_HL2_X     92     /* secondary highlight centre */
2785	#define OEYE_HL2_Y     92

2787	/* Iris bounding box — the only region we redraw per frame.
2788	 * iris at (80,80) r56 → x,y ∈ [24,136].
2789	 */

2791	#define OEYE_BOX_L     24
2792	#define OEYE_BOX_R     136
2793	#define OEYE_BOX_T     24
2794	#define OEYE_BOX_B     136

2796	/* Eyelid Y boundaries for each expression */
2797	
2798	#define OEYE_NEUTRAL_TOP  16   /* neutral: upper lid covers y 0..16 */
2799	#define OEYE_NEUTRAL_BOT  143  /* neutral: lower lid covers y 143..159 */
2800	#define OEYE_HALF_TOP     50   /* half: upper lid covers y 0..50 */
2801	#define OEYE_HALF_BOT     110  /* half: lower lid covers y 110..159 */
2802	#define OEYE_BLINK_TOP    70   /* blink: black arc top edge */
2803	#define OEYE_BLINK_BOT    90   /* blink: black arc bottom edge */

2823	 * Description:

21	/****************************************************************************
22	 * GC2145 Phase 1 - DVP IO + sensor init + PSRAM framebuf
23	 *
24	 * Phase 0: "camera id" - reads GC2145 chip ID via SCCB bit-bang
25	 * Phase 1: DVP data pin mux (P29-P39), GC2145 init, PSRAM buffer
26	 *
27	 * BK7258 GPIO CFG register (per-pin, at AON_GPIO_BASE + pin*4):
28	 *   bit[0]   gpio_input     (RO) - reads pin level
29	 *   bit[1]   gpio_output    (RW) - OUTPUT VALUE: 0=low, 1=high
30	 *   bit[2]   input_enable   (RW) - 1=enable input buffer
31	 *   bit[3]   output_enable  (RW, active-low) - 0=output enabled
32	 *   bit[4]   pull_mode      (RW) - 1=pull-up
33	 *   bit[5]   pull_enable    (RW) - 1=enable pull
34	 *   bit[6]   second_func    (RW) - 1=peripheral function, 0=GPIO
35	 *
36	 * Open-drain SCCB:
37	 *   Drive low  = output_enable=0, output_value=0, second_func=0
38	 *   Release    = output_enable=1(disabled), input_enable=1
39	 *
40	 * DVP data pins (P29-P39):
41	 *   Function select = 0 (JPEG_PCLK/HSYNC/VSYNC/PXDATA0-7)
42	 *   CFG: output_dis, input_dis, pull_dis, second_func=1
43	 *
44	 * GC2145 init table:
45	 *   Ported from ARMino dvp_gc2145.c (Apache-2.0, Galois Inc)
46	 *   Output format: reg 0x84 = 0x02, 640x480
47	 *   Actual PSRAM byte order: VYUY (V Y0 U Y1, color-target verified)
48	 *
49	 ****************************************************************************/

74	/****************************************************************************
75	 * Pre-processor Definitions
76	 ****************************************************************************/
77	
78	/* CIS Controller (YUV_BUF) Register Base Address
79	 * From ARMino yuv_buf_reg.h: SOC_YUV_BUF_REG_BASE = 0x48020000
80	 * SOC_ADDR_OFFSET = 0 for non-secure world.
81	 */
82	
83	#define YUV_BUF_REG_BASE          0x48020000u
84	
85	/* Register offsets (word-addressed, multiply by 4 for byte offset) */
86	
87	#define YUV_BUF_REG_0x04          (YUV_BUF_REG_BASE + 0x04 * 4)  /* CTRL */
88	#define YUV_BUF_REG_0x05          (YUV_BUF_REG_BASE + 0x05 * 4)  /* PIXEL */
89	#define YUV_BUF_REG_0x08          (YUV_BUF_REG_BASE + 0x08 * 4)  /* EM_BASE_ADDR */
90	#define YUV_BUF_REG_0x09          (YUV_BUF_REG_BASE + 0x09 * 4)  /* INT_EN */
91	#define YUV_BUF_REG_0x0a          (YUV_BUF_REG_BASE + 0x0a * 4)  /* INT_STATUS */
92	
93	/* CTRL register (0x04) bit fields */

203	/* Skin-tone detection thresholds (Cr/Cb domain).
204	 *
205	 * Calibration data (2026-08-21, 20 frames each, 4800 samples/frame,
206	 * zoom range [80,208]):
207	 *
208	 *                  Face      White wall   Wood photo
209	 *   Cr >= 154     29.2%      0.30%        5.95%
210	 *   Cr >= 158     18.6%      0.00%        1.29%   <- selected
211	 *   Cr >= 162     10.8%      0.00%        0.17%
212	 *
213	 * Cb has no discriminative power (face mean 93.3 / wall 89.7, nearly
214	 * identical distributions) and drifts 30-50 levels across sessions,
215	 * so it is used only as a loose gate.  Y < 50 renders chrominance
216	 * unreliable (occlusion test: 98% of samples collapse to neutral).
217	 */
218	
219	#define SKIN_Y_LO    50    /* below this, chrominance is noise */
220	#define SKIN_Y_HI    230   /* above this, likely saturated */
221	#define SKIN_CB_LO   40    /* loose Cb gate (no discriminative power) */
222	#define SKIN_CB_HI   150
223	#define SKIN_CR_LO   152   /* skin vs wood-board separation, empirical
224	                            * (per-surface uvhist, zoom 96..176):
225	                            *   white wall  : Cr <= 138
226	                            *   wood board  : Cr mass <= 149, tail to ~154,
227	                            *                 but < 25 samples >= 152
228	                            *   frontal face: ~670 samples in Cr 152..165
229	                            * WB is low-saturation so skin and wood overlap
230	                            * below 150; they only separate in the skin
231	                            * tail.  152 + DETECT_MIN_HITS(96) keeps wood
232	                            * under the detection floor while a frontal
233	                            * face clears it ~7x.  (142 was wrong: wood
234	                            * has ~1376 samples >= 142.) */
235	#define SKIN_CR_HI   200
236	#define SKIN_CR_CEIL 166   /* face Cr tops ~164; orange wires >=175
237	                             * are non-skin red, clamp them here */
238	
239	/* Adaptive skin threshold (demo scene has no wood, lighting is
240	 * uncontrolled).  The neutral background Cr peak is stable ~127
241	 * across all captures; skin is always the reddish tail above it.
242	 * Threshold = background_Cr_mode + margin, clamped.  This tracks
243	 * lighting/white-balance drift instead of using a fixed value.
244	 */
245	#define SKIN_CR_MARGIN  16   /* skin sits >= this above neutral peak */
246	#define SKIN_CR_LO_MIN  140  /* floor: neutral wall topped out at 138 */
247	#define SKIN_CR_LO_MAX  156  /* ceiling: skin tops ~167, cap prevents
248	                              * adaptive threshold from killing face */

250	/* Minimum hit count to report a direction.
251	 * Empty scenes test 0-29 hits; 60 rejects those while
252	 * recovering face frames in the 60-95 range that the
253	 * previous 96 threshold missed during motion.

1066	/****************************************************************************
1067	 * GPIO Helpers
1068	 *
1069	 * register: CFG = AON_GPIO_BASE + pin*4
1070	 *   bit[1] = output value (0=low, 1=high)
1071	 *   bit[3] = output enable (active-low: 0=enabled)
1072	 *   bit[2] = input enable
1073	 *   bit[6] = second function
1074	 ****************************************************************************/
1075	
1076	static inline bool gpio_is_valid(int pin)
1077	{
1078	  return pin >= CAMERA_GPIO_MIN && pin <= CAMERA_GPIO_MAX;
1079	}
1080	
1081	static void gpio_save_state(int pin, gpio_state_t *s)
1082	{
1083	  int shift;
1084	  uint32_t func_raw;
1085	
1086	  s->pin       = pin;
1087	  s->cfg_addr  = BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin);
1088	  s->func_addr = BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(pin);
1089	  s->cfg       = getreg32(s->cfg_addr);
1090	
1091	  /* Save only this pin's 4-bit function field */
1092	
1093	  func_raw = getreg32(s->func_addr);
1094	  shift    = (pin & 7) * 4;
1095	  s->func  = (func_raw >> shift) & 0xFu;
1096	}
1097	
1098	static void gpio_restore_state(const gpio_state_t *s)
1099	{
1100	  int shift;
1101	  uint32_t func_val;
1102	
1103	  putreg32(s->cfg, s->cfg_addr);
1104	
1105	  /* Read-modify-write: only restore this pin's 4-bit function field */
1106	
1107	  shift    = (s->pin & 7) * 4;
1108	  func_val = getreg32(s->func_addr);
1109	  func_val &= ~(0xFu << shift);
1110	  func_val |= (s->func & 0xFu) << shift;
1111	  putreg32(func_val, s->func_addr);
1112	}

1114	/****************************************************************************
1115	 * Name: gpio_drive_low
1116	 *   Output value=0, output enabled, GPIO mode.
1117	 ****************************************************************************/
1118	
1119	static void gpio_drive_low(int pin)
1120	{
1121	  uintptr_t addr = BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin);
1122	  uint32_t cfg = getreg32(addr);
1123	
1124	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;  /* bit6=0: GPIO mode */
1125	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT;       /* bit1=0: output value = LOW */
1126	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;    /* bit3=0: output enabled (active-low) */
1127	
1128	  putreg32(cfg, addr);
1129	}

1131	/****************************************************************************
1132	 * Name: gpio_set_output_high
1133	 *   Output value=1, output enabled, GPIO mode.
1134	 ****************************************************************************/
1135	
1136	static void gpio_set_output_high(int pin)
1137	{
1138	  uintptr_t addr = BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin);
1139	  uint32_t cfg = getreg32(addr);
1140	
1141	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;  /* bit6=0: GPIO mode */
1142	  cfg |=  GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT;       /* bit1=1: output value = HIGH */
1143	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;    /* bit3=0: output enabled (active-low) */
1144	
1145	  putreg32(cfg, addr);
1146	}

1148	/****************************************************************************
1149	 * Name: gpio_release
1150	 *   Output disabled, input enabled, GPIO mode (high-Z).
1151	 ****************************************************************************/
1152	
1153	static void gpio_release(int pin)
1154	{
1155	  uintptr_t addr = BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin);
1156	  uint32_t cfg = getreg32(addr);
1157	
1158	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;  /* bit6=0: GPIO mode */
1159	  cfg &= ~GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT;       /* bit1=0: value=0 (irrelevant when out dis) */
1160	  cfg |=  GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;    /* bit3=1: output DISABLED (active-low) */
1161	  cfg |=  GPIO_CFG_INPUT_EN;     /* bit2=1: input enabled */
1162	
1163	  putreg32(cfg, addr);
1164	}

1171	/****************************************************************************
1172	 * SCCB Bit-Bang
1173	 ****************************************************************************/
1174	
1175	static void sccb_sda_low(void)     { gpio_drive_low(g_cam_sda_pin); }
1176	static void sccb_sda_release(void) { gpio_release(g_cam_sda_pin); }
1177	static void sccb_scl_low(void)     { gpio_drive_low(g_cam_scl_pin); }
1178	static void sccb_scl_release(void) { gpio_release(g_cam_scl_pin); }
1179	static bool sccb_sda_read(void)    { return gpio_read_input(g_cam_sda_pin); }
1180	
1181	static int sccb_scl_wait_high(void)
1182	{
1183	  int timeout = SCCB_TIMEOUT_ITER;
1184	  while (timeout-- > 0)
1185	    {
1186	      if (gpio_read_input(g_cam_scl_pin)) return 0;
1187	      up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1188	    }
1189	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] SCL stuck low\n");
1190	  return -ETIMEDOUT;
1191	}
1192	
1193	static int sccb_start(void)
1194	{
1195	  int ret;
1196	
1197	  sccb_sda_release();
1198	  sccb_scl_release();
1199	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1200	
1201	  /* Bus-free check */
1202	
1203	  if (!gpio_read_input(g_cam_scl_pin))
1204	    {
1205	      ret = sccb_scl_wait_high();
1206	      if (ret < 0) return ret;
1207	    }
1208	
1209	  if (!gpio_read_input(g_cam_sda_pin))
1210	    {
1211	      /* SDA stuck low - 9-clock recovery */
1212	
1213	      int i;
1214	      for (i = 0; i < 9; i++)
1215	        {
1216	          sccb_scl_low();
1217	          up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1218	          sccb_scl_release();
1219	          ret = sccb_scl_wait_high();
1220	          if (ret < 0) return ret;
1221	          up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1222	          if (gpio_read_input(g_cam_sda_pin)) break;
1223	        }
1224	      if (!gpio_read_input(g_cam_sda_pin))
1225	        {
1226	          syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] SDA stuck low - recovery failed\n");
1227	          return -EIO;
1228	        }
1229	    }
1230	
1231	  /* START: SDA falls while SCL high */
1232	
1233	  sccb_sda_low();
1234	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1235	  sccb_scl_low();
1236	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1237	
1238	  return 0;
1239	}
1240	
1241	static int sccb_stop(void)
1242	{
1243	  int ret;
1244	
1245	  sccb_sda_low();
1246	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1247	
1248	  sccb_scl_release();
1249	  ret = sccb_scl_wait_high();
1250	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
1251	
1252	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1253	
1254	  sccb_sda_release();
1255	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1256	
1257	  return 0;
1258	}
1259	
1260	static int sccb_write_byte(uint8_t byte)
1261	{
1262	  int i, ret;
1263	  bool ack;
1264	
1265	  for (i = 7; i >= 0; i--)
1266	    {
1267	      if ((byte >> i) & 1) sccb_sda_release();
1268	      else                 sccb_sda_low();
1269	
1270	      up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1271	
1272	      sccb_scl_release();
1273	      ret = sccb_scl_wait_high();
1274	      if (ret < 0) return ret;
1275	      up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1276	
1277	      sccb_scl_low();
1278	      up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1279	    }
1280	
1281	  /* ACK clock */
1282	
1283	  sccb_sda_release();
1284	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1285	
1286	  sccb_scl_release();
1287	  ret = sccb_scl_wait_high();
1288	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
1289	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1290	
1291	  ack = !sccb_sda_read();
1292	
1293	  sccb_scl_low();
1294	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1295	
1296	  return ack ? 0 : -EIO;
1297	}
1298	
1299	static int sccb_read_byte(bool ack)
1300	{
1301	  uint8_t byte = 0;
1302	  int i, ret;
1303	
1304	  sccb_sda_release();
1305	
1306	  for (i = 7; i >= 0; i--)
1307	    {
1308	      up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1309	      sccb_scl_release();
1310	      ret = sccb_scl_wait_high();
1311	      if (ret < 0) return ret;
1312	      up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1313	
1314	      if (sccb_sda_read()) byte |= (1u << i);
1315	
1316	      sccb_scl_low();
1317	      up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1318	    }
1319	
1320	  if (ack) sccb_sda_low();
1321	  else     sccb_sda_release();
1322	
1323	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1324	
1325	  sccb_scl_release();
1326	  ret = sccb_scl_wait_high();
1327	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
1328	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1329	
1330	  sccb_scl_low();
1331	  up_udelay(SCCB_HALF_PERIOD_US);
1332	  sccb_sda_release();
1333	
1334	  return (int)byte;
1335	}
1336	
1337	static int sccb_read_reg(uint8_t reg_addr)
1338	{
1339	  int ret, value, stop_ret;
1340	
1341	  /* Phase 1: write address */
1342	
1343	  ret = sccb_start();
1344	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
1345	
1346	  ret = sccb_write_byte((uint8_t)(GC2145_SCCB_ADDR << 1) | 0);
1347	  if (ret < 0) goto stop_fail;
1348	
1349	  ret = sccb_write_byte(reg_addr);
1350	  if (ret < 0) goto stop_fail;
1351	
1352	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
1353	  if (stop_ret < 0) return stop_ret;
1354	
1355	  /* Phase 2: read value */
1356	
1357	  ret = sccb_start();
1358	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
1359	
1360	  ret = sccb_write_byte((uint8_t)(GC2145_SCCB_ADDR << 1) | 1);
1361	  if (ret < 0) goto stop_fail;
1362	
1363	  value = sccb_read_byte(false);
1364	  if (value < 0) { ret = value; goto stop_fail; }
1365	
1366	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
1367	  if (stop_ret < 0) return stop_ret;
1368	
1369	  return value;
1370	
1371	stop_fail:
1372	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
1373	  return (stop_ret < 0) ? stop_ret : ret;
1374	}
1375	
1376	/****************************************************************************
1377	 * Name: sccb_write_reg
1378	 *   Write a single 8-bit value to a GC2145 register via SCCB.
1379	 *   Same error handling quality as sccb_read_reg().
1380	 ****************************************************************************/
1381	
1382	static int sccb_write_reg(uint8_t reg_addr, uint8_t val)
1383	{
1384	  int ret, stop_ret;
1385	
1386	  ret = sccb_start();
1387	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
1388	
1389	  ret = sccb_write_byte((uint8_t)(GC2145_SCCB_ADDR << 1) | 0);
1390	  if (ret < 0) goto stop_fail;
1391	
1392	  ret = sccb_write_byte(reg_addr);
1393	  if (ret < 0) goto stop_fail;
1394	
1395	  ret = sccb_write_byte(val);
1396	  if (ret < 0) goto stop_fail;
1397	
1398	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
1399	  if (stop_ret < 0) return stop_ret;
1400	
1401	  return 0;
1402	
1403	stop_fail:
1404	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
1405	  return (stop_ret < 0) ? stop_ret : ret;
1406	}

1408	/****************************************************************************
1409	 * MCLK
1410	 *
1411	 * mclk_enable_24mhz modifies 4 registers:
1412	 *   1. GPIO FUNC (shared P24-P31) - only P27 bits
1413	 *   2. P27 GPIO CFG - set second_func=1 (bit6)
1414	 *   3. CLK DIV - cksel + ckdiv
1415	 *   4. CLK EN - enable gate
1416	 *
1417	 * Restore uses read-modify-write on shared registers.
1418	 ****************************************************************************/
1419	
1420	static void mclk_save_state(mclk_state_t *ms)
1421	{
1422	  uint32_t val;
1423	
1424	  /* Save only the MCLK-relevant bit fields from shared registers */
1425	
1426	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_DIV_REG);
1427	  ms->clk_div = val & ((CAMERA_CKSEL_MASK << CAMERA_CKSEL_POS) |
1428	                        (CAMERA_CKDIV_MASK << CAMERA_CKDIV_POS));
1429	
1430	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1431	  ms->clk_en = val & CAMERA_CIS_AUXS_CKEN_BIT;
1432	
1433	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_GPIO_FUNC_REG);
1434	  ms->func2431 = val & (CAMERA_P27_FUNC_MASK << CAMERA_P27_FUNC_SHIFT);
1435	
1436	  ms->p27_cfg = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(CAMERA_MCLK_REQUIRED_PIN));
1437	  ms->valid   = true;
1438	}
1439	
1440	static void mclk_restore_state(const mclk_state_t *ms)
1441	{
1442	  uint32_t val;
1443	
1444	  if (!ms->valid) return;
1445	
1446	  /* 1. Gate OFF first - avoid glitch while source/divider changes */
1447	
1448	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1449	  val &= ~CAMERA_CIS_AUXS_CKEN_BIT;
1450	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1451	
1452	  /* 2. Restore cksel/ckdiv - read-modify-write, safe while gate off */
1453	
1454	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_DIV_REG);
1455	  val &= ~((CAMERA_CKSEL_MASK << CAMERA_CKSEL_POS) |
1456	            (CAMERA_CKDIV_MASK << CAMERA_CKDIV_POS));
1457	  val |= ms->clk_div;
1458	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_DIV_REG);
1459	
1460	  /* 3. Restore P27 function select - read-modify-write FUNC reg */
1461	
1462	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_GPIO_FUNC_REG);
1463	  val &= ~(CAMERA_P27_FUNC_MASK << CAMERA_P27_FUNC_SHIFT);
1464	  val |= ms->func2431;
1465	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_GPIO_FUNC_REG);
1466	
1467	  /* 4. Restore P27 GPIO CFG (direction/latch/pull) - per-pin, safe */
1468	
1469	  putreg32(ms->p27_cfg, BK7258_GPIO_CFG(CAMERA_MCLK_REQUIRED_PIN));
1470	
1471	  /* 5. Restore saved gate state - read-modify-write CLK_EN */
1472	
1473	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1474	  val &= ~CAMERA_CIS_AUXS_CKEN_BIT;
1475	  val |= ms->clk_en;
1476	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1477	}
1478	
1479	static void mclk_enable_24mhz(void)
1480	{
1481	  uint32_t val;
1482	
1483	  /* 1. Gate OFF - avoid glitch while source/divider changes */
1484	
1485	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1486	  val &= ~CAMERA_CIS_AUXS_CKEN_BIT;
1487	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1488	
1489	  /* 2. Unmap P27 - clear function select (ARMino: gpio_dev_unmap) */
1490	
1491	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_GPIO_FUNC_REG);
1492	  val &= ~(CAMERA_P27_FUNC_MASK << CAMERA_P27_FUNC_SHIFT);
1493	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_GPIO_FUNC_REG);
1494	
1495	  /* 3. Remap P27 -> CIS AUXS clock (ARMino: gpio_dev_map) */
1496	
1497	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_GPIO_FUNC_REG);
1498	  val |= (CAMERA_P27_FUNC_CIS_CLK << CAMERA_P27_FUNC_SHIFT);
1499	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_GPIO_FUNC_REG);
1500	
1501	  /* 4. Prep P27 GPIO: disable output/input/pull before switching function
1502	   *    (ARMino: gpio_hal_func_map -> gpio_hal_set_pull/ output_dis / input_dis)
1503	   *    Saved in mclk_save_state(), restored in mclk_restore_state().
1504	   */
1505	
1506	  val = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(CAMERA_MCLK_REQUIRED_PIN));
1507	  val |=  GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;    /* bit3=1: output DISABLED (active-low) */
1508	  val &= ~GPIO_CFG_INPUT_EN;     /* bit2=0: input disabled */
1509	  val &= ~GPIO_CFG_PULL_EN;      /* bit5=0: pull disabled */
1510	  val |=  GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;  /* bit6=1: peripheral function */
1511	  putreg32(val, BK7258_GPIO_CFG(CAMERA_MCLK_REQUIRED_PIN));
1512	
1513	  /* 5. Set clock source and divider - read-modify-write
1514	   *    (ARMino: sys_drv_set_auxs_cis(3, 19))
1515	   */
1516	
1517	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_DIV_REG);
1518	  val &= ~((CAMERA_CKSEL_MASK << CAMERA_CKSEL_POS) |
1519	           (CAMERA_CKDIV_MASK << CAMERA_CKDIV_POS));
1520	  val |= (CAMERA_CKSEL_AUXS_CIS << CAMERA_CKSEL_POS);
1521	  val |= (CAMERA_CKDIV_24MHZ    << CAMERA_CKDIV_POS);
1522	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_DIV_REG);
1523	
1524	  /* 6. Enable clock gate - read-modify-write
1525	   *    (ARMino: sys_drv_set_cis_auxs_clk_en(1))
1526	   */
1527	
1528	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1529	  val |= CAMERA_CIS_AUXS_CKEN_BIT;
1530	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1531	}

1590	/****************************************************************************
1591	 * DVP Data Pin Mux (P29-P39)
1592	 *
1593	 * Configure 11 DVP data pins for camera use:
1594	 *   P29=PCLK, P30=HSYNC, P31=VSYNC, P32-P39=PXDATA[0:7]
1595	 *
1596	 * Each pin:
1597	 *   1. Save full CFG + 4-bit function field (for restore)
1598	 *   2. Set function select = 0 (JPEG/DVP function)
1599	 *   3. Set CFG: output_dis, input_dis, pull_dis, second_func=1
1600	 *
1601	 * Function select register layout (shared per 8 pins):
1602	 *   P24-P31: SYS_BASE + 0xCC  (P27=MCLK uses func=1, others=0)
1603	 *   P32-P39: SYS_BASE + 0xD0  (all use func=0)
1604	 ****************************************************************************/
1605	
1606	static int dvp_io_config(void)
1607	{
1608	  int i;
1609	  uint32_t val;
1610	
1611	  for (i = 0; i < DVP_PIN_COUNT; i++)
1612	    {
1613	      int pin = DVP_PIN_FIRST + i;
1614	
1615	      /* Save CFG + function field for restore */
1616	
1617	      gpio_save_state(pin, &g_dvp_state[i]);
1618	
1619	      /* Set function select = 0 via field-level RMW */
1620	
1621	      val = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(pin));
1622	      val &= ~(0xFu << ((pin & 7) * 4));  /* clear function field */
1623	      putreg32(val, BK7258_SYS_GPIO_FUNC(pin));
1624	
1625	      /* Set CFG: disable output, disable input, disable pull, enable
1626	       * second function (ARMino gpio_hal_func_map prep sequence).
1627	       */
1628	
1629	      val = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
1630	      val |=  GPIO_CFG_OUTPUT_EN;    /* bit3=1: output DISABLED (active-low) */
1631	      val &= ~GPIO_CFG_INPUT_EN;     /* bit2=0: input disabled */
1632	      val &= ~GPIO_CFG_PULL_EN;      /* bit5=0: pull disabled */
1633	      val |=  GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC;  /* bit6=1: peripheral function */
1634	      putreg32(val, BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
1635	    }
1636	
1637	  g_dvp_pins_configed = true;
1638	  return 0;
1639	}
1640	
1641	static void dvp_io_deconfig(void)
1642	{
1643	  int i;
1644	
1645	  if (!g_dvp_pins_configed) return;
1646	
1647	  /* Restore in reverse order */
1648	
1649	  for (i = DVP_PIN_COUNT - 1; i >= 0; i--)
1650	    {
1651	      gpio_restore_state(&g_dvp_state[i]);
1652	    }
1653	
1654	  g_dvp_pins_configed = false;
1655	}

1657	/****************************************************************************
1658	 * GC2145 Write Table
1659	 *
1660	 * Write a register table to GC2145 via SCCB.
1661	 * Reports NACK with register address and entry index for debugging.
1662	 ****************************************************************************/
1663	
1664	static int gc2145_write_table(const uint8_t (*table)[2], int count)
1665	{
1666	  int i, ret;
1667	
1668	  for (i = 0; i < count; i++)
1669	    {
1670	      ret = sccb_write_reg(table[i][0], table[i][1]);
1671	      if (ret < 0)
1672	        {
1673	          syslog(LOG_ERR,
1674	                 "[camera] table[%d] reg 0x%02X NACK (err=%d)\n",
1675	                 i, table[i][0], ret);
1676	          return ret;
1677	        }
1678	    }
1679	
1680	  return 0;
1681	}

1683	/****************************************************************************
1684	 * PSRAM Frame Buffer
1685	 *
1686	 * Allocate two ping-pong frame buffers in PSRAM at 0x60000000.
1687	 * Each buffer is 640 * 480 * 2 = 614400 bytes (VYUY).
1688	 ****************************************************************************/
1689	
1690	static int camera_framebuf_alloc(void)
1691	{
1692	  int ret;
1693	
1694	  if (g_framebuf_allocated)
1695	    {
1696	      syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] Framebuf already allocated\n");
1697	      return 0;
1698	    }
1699	
1700	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
1701	  if (ret < 0)
1702	    {
1703	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] PSRAM init failed: %d\n", ret);
1704	      return ret;
1705	    }
1706	
1707	  g_camera_buf[0] = (volatile uint8_t *)(CAMERA_PSRAM_BASE);

1726	/****************************************************************************
1727	 * DVP Module Clock and Interrupt Enable
1728	 *
1729	 * From ARMino yuv_buf_driver.c:yuv_buf_init_common():
1730	 *   1. Enable YUV_BUF power (PM voting - skipped, assume always on)
1731	 *   2. Enable H264 clock (bit[0] of CLK_EN_REG) - needed for bus
1732	 *   3. Enable YUV_BUF clock (bit[3] of CLK_EN_REG)
1733	 *   4. Enable system interrupt (bit[26] of INT_32_63_EN_REG)
1734	 *   5. Init global control (soft reset + clock gate bypass)
1735	 *
1736	 * All register writes use field-level RMW on shared registers.
1737	 ****************************************************************************/
1738	
1739	typedef struct
1740	{
1741	  uint32_t clk_en;       /* CLK_EN_REG bits we modify */
1742	  uint32_t int_en;       /* INT_32_63_EN_REG bits we modify */
1743	  uint32_t global_ctrl;  /* YUV_BUF REG_0x02 value */
1744	  bool     valid;
1745	} dvp_module_state_t;
1746	
1747	static dvp_module_state_t g_dvp_module_saved = { .valid = false };
1748	static bool g_dvp_module_enabled = false;
1749	
1750	static int dvp_module_clk_enable(void)
1751	{
1752	  uint32_t val;
1753	
1754	  if (g_dvp_module_enabled)
1755	    {
1756	      return 0;
1757	    }
1758	
1759	  /* Save register values for restore - only bits we modify */
1760	
1761	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1762	  g_dvp_module_saved.clk_en = val & (CAMERA_H264_CLKEN_BIT |
1763	                                      CAMERA_YUV_BUF_CLKEN_BIT);
1764	
1765	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_SYS_INT_32_63_REG);
1766	  g_dvp_module_saved.int_en = val & CAMERA_YUVB_INT_EN_BIT;
1767	
1768	  g_dvp_module_saved.global_ctrl = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x02);
1769	  g_dvp_module_saved.valid = true;
1770	
1771	  /* Step 1: Enable H264 clock - needed for YUV_BUF internal bus
1772	   * From ARMino sys_drv_set_h264_clk_en(1)
1773	   */
1774	
1775	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1776	  val |= CAMERA_H264_CLKEN_BIT;
1777	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1778	
1779	  /* Step 2: Enable YUV_BUF clock
1780	   * From ARMino sys_drv_set_yuv_buf_clk_en(1)
1781	   */
1782	
1783	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1784	  val |= CAMERA_YUV_BUF_CLKEN_BIT;
1785	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1786	
1787	  /* Step 3: Enable system interrupt for YUV_BUF
1788	   * From ARMino sys_drv_int_group2_enable(YUV_BUF_INTERRUPT_CTRL_BIT)
1789	   * YUV_BUF_INTERRUPT_CTRL_BIT = (1 << 26)
1790	   */
1791	
1792	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_SYS_INT_32_63_REG);
1793	  val |= CAMERA_YUVB_INT_EN_BIT;
1794	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_SYS_INT_32_63_REG);
1795	
1796	  /* Step 4: Init global control - soft reset + clock gate bypass
1797	   * From ARMino yuv_buf_ll_init():
1798	   *   hw->global_ctrl.soft_reset = 0;    // assert reset
1799	   *   hw->global_ctrl.soft_reset = 1;    // deassert reset
1800	   *   hw->global_ctrl.clk_gate_bypass = 1; // bypass clock gate
1801	   */
1802	
1803	  val = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x02);
1804	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_GLOBAL_SOFT_RESET;  /* assert reset */
1805	  putreg32(val, YUV_BUF_REG_0x02);
1806	
1807	  val |= YUV_BUF_GLOBAL_SOFT_RESET;   /* deassert reset */
1808	  val |= YUV_BUF_GLOBAL_CLK_GATE;     /* bypass clock gate */
1809	  putreg32(val, YUV_BUF_REG_0x02);
1810	
1811	  g_dvp_module_enabled = true;
1812	
1813	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1814	         "[camera] DVP module clock enabled: CLK_EN=0x%08lX INT_EN=0x%08lX\n",
1815	         (unsigned long)getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG),
1816	         (unsigned long)getreg32(CAMERA_SYS_INT_32_63_REG));
1817	
1818	  return 0;
1819	}
1820	
1821	static void dvp_module_clk_disable(void)
1822	{
1823	  uint32_t val;
1824	
1825	  if (!g_dvp_module_enabled) return;
1826	
1827	  /* Assert soft reset first */
1828	
1829	  val = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x02);
1830	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_GLOBAL_SOFT_RESET;
1831	  putreg32(val, YUV_BUF_REG_0x02);
1832	
1833	  /* Disable system interrupt for YUV_BUF */
1834	
1835	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_SYS_INT_32_63_REG);
1836	  val &= ~CAMERA_YUVB_INT_EN_BIT;
1837	  val |= g_dvp_module_saved.int_en;  /* restore saved bits */
1838	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_SYS_INT_32_63_REG);
1839	
1840	  /* Disable YUV_BUF clock */
1841	
1842	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1843	  val &= ~CAMERA_YUV_BUF_CLKEN_BIT;
1844	  val |= (g_dvp_module_saved.clk_en & CAMERA_YUV_BUF_CLKEN_BIT);
1845	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1846	
1847	  /* Disable H264 clock */
1848	
1849	  val = getreg32(CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1850	  val &= ~CAMERA_H264_CLKEN_BIT;
1851	  val |= (g_dvp_module_saved.clk_en & CAMERA_H264_CLKEN_BIT);
1852	  putreg32(val, CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG);
1853	
1854	  /* Restore global control register */
1855	
1856	  putreg32(g_dvp_module_saved.global_ctrl, YUV_BUF_REG_0x02);
1857	
1858	  g_dvp_module_enabled = false;
1859	
1860	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] DVP module clock disabled\n");
1861	}

1863	/****************************************************************************
1864	 * DVP Controller Configuration (CIS / YUV_BUF)
1865	 *
1866	 * The YUV_BUF controller at 0x48020000 captures DVP data and writes it
1867	 * to external memory via its internal DMA.  Configuration steps:
1868	 *   1. Save all register values for restore
1869	 *   2. Set resolution (x_pixel = width/8, y_pixel = height/8)
1870	 *   3. Set format (YUV mode, HW label "YUYV" — actual byte order VYUY)
1871	 *   4. Set polarity (HSYNC/VSYNC/PCLK from Kconfig)
1872	 *   5. Set frame buffer base address
1873	 *   6. Start YUV mode (set yuv_mode bit in CTRL)
1874	 *
1875	 * All register writes use field-level RMW on shared registers.
1876	 ****************************************************************************/
1877	
1878	static void dvp_ctrl_save_state(dvp_ctrl_state_t *s)
1879	{
1880	  s->ctrl       = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x04);
1881	  s->pixel      = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x05);
1882	  s->em_base    = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x08);
1883	  s->int_en     = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x09);
1884	  s->int_status = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x0a);
1885	  s->valid      = true;
1886	}
1887	
1888	static void dvp_ctrl_restore_state(const dvp_ctrl_state_t *s)
1889	{
1890	  if (!s->valid) return;
1891	
1892	  /* Disable interrupts first */
1893	
1894	  putreg32(0, YUV_BUF_REG_0x09);
1895	
1896	  /* Clear any pending interrupt status */
1897	
1898	  putreg32(YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS_MASK, YUV_BUF_REG_0x0a);
1899	
1900	  /* Restore registers in order: CTRL, PIXEL, EM_BASE, INT_EN */
1901	
1902	  putreg32(s->ctrl, YUV_BUF_REG_0x04);
1903	  putreg32(s->pixel, YUV_BUF_REG_0x05);
1904	  putreg32(s->em_base, YUV_BUF_REG_0x08);
1905	  putreg32(s->int_en, YUV_BUF_REG_0x09);
1906	}
1907	
1908	/****************************************************************************
1909	 * Name: dvp_ctrl_config
1910	 *
1911	 * Description:
1912	 *   Configure the CIS controller (YUV_BUF) for DVP capture.
1913	 *   Resolution: CAMERA_HRES x CAMERA_VRES (640x480).
1914	 *   Format: YUV mode, HW label "YUYV" (actual PSRAM byte order: VYUY).
1915	 *   Polarity: from Kconfig (CONFIG_DVP_PCLK_RISING, etc.).
1916	 *
1917	 *   The controller's internal DMA writes captured data to the address
1918	 *   in em_base_addr.
1919	 *
1920	 * Input Parameters:
1921	 *   em_base - External memory base address for frame buffer output
1922	 *
1923	 ****************************************************************************/
1924	
1925	static int dvp_ctrl_config(uint32_t em_base)
1926	{
1927	  int ret;
1928	  uint32_t val;
1929	  uint32_t x_pixel;
1930	  uint32_t y_pixel;
1931	  uint32_t frame_blk;
1932	
1933	  if (g_dvp_ctrl_configed)
1934	    {
1935	      syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[camera] DVP ctrl already configured\n");
1936	      return 0;
1937	    }
1938	
1939	  /* Enable module clock and system interrupt FIRST
1940	   * This must be done before accessing YUV_BUF registers.
1941	   */
1942	
1943	  ret = dvp_module_clk_enable();
1944	  if (ret < 0)
1945	    {
1946	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] DVP module clock enable failed: %d\n", ret);
1947	      return ret;
1948	    }
1949	
1950	  /* Save all register values for restore */
1951	
1952	  dvp_ctrl_save_state(&g_dvp_ctrl_saved);
1953	
1954	  /* Calculate pixel parameters
1955	   * x_pixel = width / 8
1956	   * y_pixel = height / 8
1957	   * frame_blk = x_pixel * y_pixel / 2 (from ARMino yuv_buf_hal.c)
1958	   */
1959	
1960	  x_pixel   = CAMERA_HRES / 8;               /* 640/8 = 80 */
1961	  y_pixel   = CAMERA_VRES / 8;               /* 480/8 = 60 */
1962	  frame_blk = x_pixel * y_pixel / 2;         /* 80*60/2 = 2400 */
1963	
1964	  /* Configure CTRL register (0x04)
1965	   * Start from saved value to preserve reserved bits.
1966	   * Then set/clear fields as needed.
1967	   */
1968	
1969	  val = g_dvp_ctrl_saved.ctrl;
1970	
1971	  /* Enable YUV mode */
1972	
1973	  val |= YUV_BUF_CTRL_YUV_MODE;
1974	
1975	  /* Set YUV format to YUYV (controller default).
1976	   * NOTE: actual byte order in PSRAM is VYUY: [V Y0 U Y1], Cr first.
1977	   * The controller format field does NOT reorder bytes - it matches
1978	   * whatever the sensor outputs.  Software conversion uses VYUY parsing.
1979	   */
1980	
1981	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_FMT_SEL_MASK;
1982	  val |= YUV_BUF_CTRL_FMT_YUYV;
1983	
1984	  /* Set PCLK edge - default is rising edge sampling.
1985	   * If CONFIG_DVP_PCLK_FALLING is set, invert to sample on falling edge.
1986	   */
1987	
1988	#ifdef CONFIG_DVP_PCLK_FALLING
1989	  val |= YUV_BUF_CTRL_VCK_EDGE;   /* sample on falling edge */
1990	#else
1991	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_VCK_EDGE;  /* sample on rising edge (default) */
1992	#endif
1993	
1994	  /* Set HSYNC polarity - default is active-high (not inverted).
1995	   * If CONFIG_DVP_HSYNC_ACTIVE_LOW is set, invert HSYNC.
1996	   */
1997	
1998	#ifdef CONFIG_DVP_HSYNC_ACTIVE_LOW
1999	  val |= YUV_BUF_CTRL_HSYNC_REV;
2000	#else
2001	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_HSYNC_REV;
2002	#endif
2003	
2004	  /* Set VSYNC polarity - default is active-high (not inverted).
2005	   * If CONFIG_DVP_VSYNC_ACTIVE_LOW is set, invert VSYNC.
2006	   */
2007	
2008	#ifdef CONFIG_DVP_VSYNC_ACTIVE_LOW
2009	  val |= YUV_BUF_CTRL_VSYNC_REV;
2010	#else
2011	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_VSYNC_REV;
2012	#endif
2013	
2014	  /* Disable H264 mode - we're doing raw YUV capture */
2015	
2016	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_H264_MODE;
2017	
2018	  /* Disable memrev and byte_rev - ARMino disables these for normal
2019	   * YUV capture mode.  Only enable in nosensor_encode mode.
2020	   */
2021	
2022	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_MEMREV;
2023	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_BYTE_REV;
2024	
2025	  /* Write CTRL register */
2026	
2027	  putreg32(val, YUV_BUF_REG_0x04);
2028	
2029	  /* Configure PIXEL register (0x05)
2030	   * bit[7:0]   = x_pixel (width/8)
2031	   * bit[15:8]  = y_pixel (height/8)
2032	   * bit[31:16] = frame_blk (total blocks)
2033	   */
2034	
2035	  val = (x_pixel & YUV_BUF_PIXEL_X_MASK) |
2036	        ((y_pixel << YUV_BUF_PIXEL_Y_POS) & YUV_BUF_PIXEL_Y_MASK) |
2037	        ((frame_blk << YUV_BUF_PIXEL_BLK_POS) & YUV_BUF_PIXEL_BLK_MASK);
2038	
2039	  putreg32(val, YUV_BUF_REG_0x05);
2040	
2041	  /* Set external memory base address (0x08) */
2042	
2043	  putreg32(em_base, YUV_BUF_REG_0x08);
2044	
2045	  /* Clear any pending interrupt status */
2046	
2047	  putreg32(YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS_MASK, YUV_BUF_REG_0x0a);
2048	
2049	  /* Start YUV mode - set bit[0] of CTRL (yuv_mode)
2050	   * From ARMino bk_yuv_buf_start(YUV_MODE) -> yuv_buf_hal_start_yuv_mode()
2051	   *   yuv_buf_ll_enable_yuv_buf_mode(hal->hw);  // bit[0] = 1
2052	   *   yuv_buf_ll_disable_h264_encode_mode(hal->hw); // bit[3] = 0
2053	   */
2054	
2055	  val = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x04);
2056	  val |= YUV_BUF_CTRL_YUV_MODE;     /* enable YUV buf mode */
2057	  val &= ~YUV_BUF_CTRL_H264_MODE;   /* disable H264 mode */
2058	  putreg32(val, YUV_BUF_REG_0x04);
2059	
2060	  g_dvp_ctrl_configed = true;
2061	
2062	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
2063	         "[camera] DVP ctrl config: %dx%d xpix=%lu ypix=%lu blk=%lu "
2064	         "em_base=0x%08lX\n",
2065	         CAMERA_HRES, CAMERA_VRES,
2066	         (unsigned long)x_pixel, (unsigned long)y_pixel,
2067	         (unsigned long)frame_blk,
2068	         (unsigned long)em_base);
2069	
2070	  return 0;
2071	}

2073	/****************************************************************************
2074	 * Name: dvp_ctrl_deconfig
2075	 *
2076	 * Description:
2077	 *   Restore all CIS controller registers to their saved values.
2078	 *   Disables interrupts and clears pending status before restore.
2079	 *
2080	 ****************************************************************************/
2081	
2082	static void dvp_ctrl_deconfig(void)
2083	{
2084	  if (!g_dvp_ctrl_configed) return;
2085	
2086	  dvp_ctrl_restore_state(&g_dvp_ctrl_saved);
2087	  g_dvp_ctrl_configed = false;
2088	
2089	  /* Disable module clock after restoring registers */
2090	
2091	  dvp_module_clk_disable();
2092	}

2130	/****************************************************************************
2131	 * Name: dvp_irq_handler
2132	 *
2133	 * Description:
2134	 *   ISR for DVP (YUV_BUF) controller interrupts.
2135	 *   Handles VSYNC falling edge (frame start) and YUV arrived (frame done).
2136	 *
2137	 ****************************************************************************/
2138	
2139	static int dvp_irq_handler(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
2140	{
2141	  uint32_t status;
2142	
2143	  /* Read interrupt status */
2144	
2145	  status = getreg32(YUV_BUF_REG_0x0a);
2146	
2147	  /* VSYNC falling edge - frame start */
2148	
2149	  if (status & YUV_BUF_INT_VSYNC_NEGE)
2150	    {
2151	      g_dvp_vsync_count++;
2152	    }
2153	
2154	  /* YUV arrived - frame data written to memory */
2155	
2156	  if (status & YUV_BUF_INT_YUV_ARV)
2157	    {
2158	      g_dvp_frame_count++;
2159	
2160	      /* Ping-pong: if streaming, advance to next buffer */
2161	
2162	      if (g_stream_active)
2163	        {
2164	          int next_buf = 1 - g_cur_buf;
2165	
2166	          if (g_ready_buf < 0 && next_buf != g_busy_buf)
2167	            {
2168	              g_ready_buf = g_cur_buf;
2169	              g_cur_buf = next_buf;
2170	              g_pingpong_count++;
2171	              putreg32((uint32_t)(uintptr_t)g_camera_buf[g_cur_buf],
2172	                       YUV_BUF_REG_0x08);
2173	            }
2174	          else
2175	            {
2176	              g_drop_count++;
2177	            }
2178	        }
2179	    }
2180	
2181	  /* Clear all pending interrupts by writing 1s */
2182	
2183	  putreg32(status & YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS_MASK, YUV_BUF_REG_0x0a);
2184	
2185	  return OK;
2186	}

2188	/****************************************************************************
2189	 * Name: dvp_irq_attach
2190	 *
2191	 * Description:
2192	 *   Attach DVP interrupt handler and enable VSYNC + YUV_ARRIVED interrupts.
2193	 *
2194	 ****************************************************************************/
2195	
2196	static int dvp_irq_attach(void)
2197	{
2198	  int ret;
2199	
2200	  if (g_dvp_irq_attached)
2201	    {
2202	      syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[camera] DVP IRQ already attached\n");
2203	      return 0;
2204	    }
2205	
2206	  /* Reset counters */
2207	
2208	  g_dvp_vsync_count = 0;
2209	  g_dvp_hsync_count = 0;
2210	  g_dvp_frame_count = 0;
2211	
2212	  /* Attach ISR */
2213	
2214	  ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_YUV_BUF, dvp_irq_handler, NULL);
2215	  if (ret < 0)
2216	    {
2217	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] irq_attach failed: %d\n", ret);
2218	      return ret;
2219	    }
2220	
2221	  /* Enable VSYNC falling edge and YUV arrived interrupts */
2222	
2223	  putreg32(YUV_BUF_INT_VSYNC_NEGE | YUV_BUF_INT_YUV_ARV,
2224	           YUV_BUF_REG_0x09);
2225	
2226	  /* Enable the IRQ in NVIC */
2227	
2228	  up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_YUV_BUF);
2229	
2230	  g_dvp_irq_attached = true;
2231	
2232	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] DVP IRQ attached (IRQ %d)\n",
2233	         BK7258_IRQ_YUV_BUF);
2234	
2235	  return 0;
2236	}

2238	/****************************************************************************
2239	 * Name: dvp_irq_detach
2240	 *
2241	 * Description:
2242	 *   Disable DVP interrupts and detach the ISR.
2243	 *
2244	 ****************************************************************************/
2245	
2246	static void dvp_irq_detach(void)
2247	{
2248	  if (!g_dvp_irq_attached) return;
2249	
2250	  /* Disable IRQ in NVIC */
2251	
2252	  up_disable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_YUV_BUF);
2253	
2254	  /* Disable all DVP interrupts */
2255	
2256	  putreg32(0, YUV_BUF_REG_0x09);
2257	
2258	  /* Clear any pending status */
2259	
2260	  putreg32(YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS_MASK, YUV_BUF_REG_0x0a);
2261	
2262	  /* Detach ISR - restore default handler */
2263	
2264	  irq_detach(BK7258_IRQ_YUV_BUF);
2265	
2266	  g_dvp_irq_attached = false;
2267	
2268	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] DVP IRQ detached\n");
2269	}

2292	  const char *rst_g_st = "n";
2293	#endif
2294	#ifdef CONFIG_CAMERA_RST_POLARITY_CONFIRMED
2295	  const char *rst_p_st = "y";
2296	#else
2297	  const char *rst_p_st = "n";
2298	#endif
2299	#ifdef CONFIG_CAMERA_PWR_CONFIRMED
2300	  const char *pwr_st = "y";
2301	#else
2302	  const char *pwr_st = "n";
2303	#endif
2304	#ifdef CONFIG_CAMERA_PWR_POLARITY_CONFIRMED
2305	  const char *pwr_p_st = "y";
2306	#else
2307	  const char *pwr_p_st = "n";
2308	#endif
2309	#ifdef CONFIG_CAMERA_MCLK_CONFIRMED
2310	  const char *mclk_st = "y";
2311	#else
2312	  const char *mclk_st = "n";
2313	#endif
2314	
2315	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
2316	         "[camera] Config: SDA=%d(net=%s role=%s) SCL=%d "
2317	         "RST=%d(gpio=%s pol=%s) PWR=%d(net=%s pol=%s) "
2318	         "MCLK=%d(conf=%s)\n",
2319	         g_cam_sda_pin, sccb_st, role_st,
2320	         g_cam_scl_pin,
2321	         g_cam_rst_pin, rst_g_st, rst_p_st,
2322	         g_cam_pwr_pin, pwr_st, pwr_p_st,
2323	         g_cam_mclk_pin, mclk_st);
2324	
2325	  /* Stage 1: 7 confirmed sentinels */
2326	
2327	#ifndef CONFIG_CAMERA_SCCB_CONFIRMED
2328	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] BLOCKER: SCCB net NOT confirmed\n"); ok = false;
2329	#endif
2330	#ifndef CONFIG_CAMERA_SDA_SCL_ROLE_CONFIRMED
2331	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] BLOCKER: SDA/SCL role NOT confirmed\n"); ok = false;
2332	#endif
2333	#ifndef CONFIG_CAMERA_RST_GPIO_CONFIRMED
2334	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] BLOCKER: RST GPIO NOT confirmed\n"); ok = false;
2335	#endif
2336	#ifndef CONFIG_CAMERA_RST_POLARITY_CONFIRMED
2337	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] BLOCKER: RST polarity NOT confirmed\n"); ok = false;
2338	#endif
2339	#ifndef CONFIG_CAMERA_PWR_CONFIRMED
2340	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] BLOCKER: PWR net NOT confirmed\n"); ok = false;
2341	#endif
2342	#ifndef CONFIG_CAMERA_PWR_POLARITY_CONFIRMED
2343	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] BLOCKER: PWR polarity NOT confirmed\n"); ok = false;
2344	#endif
2345	#ifndef CONFIG_CAMERA_MCLK_CONFIRMED
2346	  syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] BLOCKER: MCLK NOT confirmed\n"); ok = false;
2347	#endif
2348	
2349	  if (!ok)
2350	    {
2351	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
2352	             "[camera] ======== 7 BLOCKERS - no MMIO touched ========\n");
2353	      return -ENOTSUP;
2354	    }
2355	
2356	  /* Stage 2: GPIO range + uniqueness */
2357	
2358	  if (!gpio_is_valid(g_cam_sda_pin))
2359	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] SDA pin %d out of range\n", g_cam_sda_pin);
2360	      ok = false; }
2361	  if (!gpio_is_valid(g_cam_scl_pin))
2362	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] SCL pin %d out of range\n", g_cam_scl_pin);
2363	      ok = false; }
2364	  if (gpio_is_valid(g_cam_sda_pin) && gpio_is_valid(g_cam_scl_pin) &&
2365	      g_cam_sda_pin == g_cam_scl_pin)
2366	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] SDA=SCL=%d conflict\n", g_cam_sda_pin);
2367	      ok = false; }
2368	  if (g_cam_rst_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2369	      !gpio_is_valid(g_cam_rst_pin))
2370	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] RST pin %d out of range\n", g_cam_rst_pin);
2371	      ok = false; }
2372	  if (g_cam_pwr_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2373	      !gpio_is_valid(g_cam_pwr_pin))
2374	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] PWR pin %d out of range\n", g_cam_pwr_pin);
2375	      ok = false; }
2376	  if (g_cam_pwdn_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2377	      !gpio_is_valid(g_cam_pwdn_pin))
2378	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] PWDN pin %d out of range\n", g_cam_pwdn_pin);
2379	      ok = false; }
2380	  if (g_cam_mclk_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2381	      !gpio_is_valid(g_cam_mclk_pin))
2382	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] MCLK pin %d out of range\n", g_cam_mclk_pin);
2383	      ok = false; }
2384	
2385	  {
2386	    int pins[6];
2387	    int n = 0;
2388	    int i, j;
2389	
2390	    if (gpio_is_valid(g_cam_sda_pin))  pins[n++] = g_cam_sda_pin;
2391	    if (gpio_is_valid(g_cam_scl_pin))  pins[n++] = g_cam_scl_pin;
2392	    if (g_cam_rst_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2393	        gpio_is_valid(g_cam_rst_pin))  pins[n++] = g_cam_rst_pin;
2394	    if (g_cam_pwr_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2395	        gpio_is_valid(g_cam_pwr_pin))  pins[n++] = g_cam_pwr_pin;
2396	    if (g_cam_pwdn_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2397	        gpio_is_valid(g_cam_pwdn_pin)) pins[n++] = g_cam_pwdn_pin;
2398	    if (g_cam_mclk_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED &&
2399	        gpio_is_valid(g_cam_mclk_pin)) pins[n++] = g_cam_mclk_pin;
2400	
2401	    for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
2402	      for (j = i + 1; j < n; j++)
2403	        if (pins[i] == pins[j])
2404	          { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] pin %d multi-role\n", pins[i]);
2405	            ok = false; }
2406	  }
2407	
2408	  /* Stage 3: board-level reserved pin conflicts */
2409	
2410	  {
2411	    static const struct { int pin; const char *name; } rsv[] = {
2412	      { CAMERA_PIN_UART0_RX, "UART0 RX" },
2413	      { CAMERA_PIN_UART0_TX, "UART0 TX" },
2414	      { CAMERA_PIN_SWD_CLK,  "SWD CLK"  },
2415	      { CAMERA_PIN_SWD_IO,   "SWD IO"   },
2416	      { 2,  "LCD left SCLK"  },
2417	      { 3,  "LCD left CS"    },
2418	      { 4,  "LCD left MOSI"  },
2419	      { 5,  "LCD left DC"    },
2420	      { 6,  "LCD right SCLK" },
2421	      { 7,  "LCD right CS"   },
2422	      { 22, "LCD right MOSI" },
2423	      { 23, "LCD right DC"   },
2424	      { 24, "LCD right RST"  },
2425	      { 25, "LCD backlight"  },
2426	      { 45, "LCD left RST"   },
2427	      { 52, "LCD LDO_3V3_EN" },
2428	    };
2429	
2430	    static const int cpins[] = {
2431	      CONFIG_CAMERA_GPIO_SDA,
2432	      CONFIG_CAMERA_GPIO_SCL,
2433	      CONFIG_CAMERA_GPIO_RST,
2434	      CONFIG_CAMERA_GPIO_PWR_CTL,
2435	      CONFIG_CAMERA_GPIO_PWDNB,
2436	      CONFIG_CAMERA_MCLK_GPIO,
2437	    };
2438	
2439	    int i, r;
2440	    for (i = 0; i < 6; i++)
2441	      {
2442	        if (cpins[i] == CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED) continue;
2443	        for (r = 0; r < (int)(sizeof(rsv) / sizeof(rsv[0])); r++)
2444	          {
2445	            if (cpins[i] == rsv[r].pin)
2446	              {
2447	                syslog(LOG_ERR,
2448	                       "[camera] pin %d conflicts with %s\n",
2449	                       cpins[i], rsv[r].name);
2450	                ok = false;
2451	              }
2452	          }
2453	      }
2454	
2455	    /* Reject control pins (SDA/SCL/RST/PWR/MCLK) on DVP reserved range
2456	     * P29-P39.  DVP DATA pins on P29-P39 are expected and allowed.
2457	     */
2458	
2459	    for (i = 0; i < 6; i++)
2460	      {
2461	        if (cpins[i] == CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED) continue;
2462	        if (cpins[i] >= DVP_PIN_FIRST && cpins[i] <= DVP_PIN_LAST)
2463	          {
2464	            syslog(LOG_ERR,
2465	                   "[camera] control pin %d in DVP range P%d-P%d\n",
2466	                   cpins[i], DVP_PIN_FIRST, DVP_PIN_LAST);
2467	            ok = false;
2468	          }
2469	      }
2470	  }
2471	
2472	  /* Stage 4: MCLK must be P27 */
2473	
2474	#ifdef CONFIG_CAMERA_MCLK_CONFIRMED
2475	  if (g_cam_mclk_pin != CAMERA_MCLK_REQUIRED_PIN)
2476	    {
2477	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
2478	             "[camera] MCLK_GPIO=%d but code requires %d (P27)\n",
2479	             g_cam_mclk_pin, CAMERA_MCLK_REQUIRED_PIN);
2480	      ok = false;
2481	    }
2482	#endif
2483	
2484	  if (!ok)
2485	    {
2486	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
2487	             "[camera] Cannot proceed - no MMIO touched.\n");
2488	      return -ENODEV;
2489	    }
2490	
2491	  return 0;
2492	}

2498	/****************************************************************************
2499	 * Name: bk7258_camera_id
2500	 *   Phase 0: read GC2145 chip ID via SCCB.  Restores all pins on exit.
2501	 ****************************************************************************/
2502	
2503	int bk7258_camera_id(void)
2504	{
2505	  gpio_state_t sda_saved, scl_saved, rst_saved;
2506	  gpio_state_t pwr_saved, pwdn_saved;
2507	  mclk_state_t mclk_saved = { .valid = false };
2508	  int id_h = -1, id_l = -1;
2509	  uint16_t chip_id;
2510	  int ret, stop_ret;
2511	  bool sda_ok = false, scl_ok = false, rst_ok = false;
2512	  bool pwr_ok = false, pwdn_ok = false;
2513	  bool mclk_on = false;
2514	
2515	  /* ===== Config validation - NO MMIO before this ===== */
2516	
2517	  ret = camera_check_config();
2518	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
2519	
2520	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] Config OK\n");
2521	
2522	  /* ===== GPIO setup ===== */
2523	
2524	  gpio_save_state(g_cam_sda_pin, &sda_saved); sda_ok = true;
2525	  gpio_save_state(g_cam_scl_pin, &scl_saved); scl_ok = true;
2526	
2527	  gpio_release(g_cam_sda_pin);
2528	  gpio_release(g_cam_scl_pin);
2529	  up_udelay(100);
2530	
2531	  if (g_cam_rst_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED)
2532	    { gpio_save_state(g_cam_rst_pin, &rst_saved); rst_ok = true; }
2533	
2534	  camera_power_on(&pwr_saved, &pwr_ok, &pwdn_saved, &pwdn_ok);
2535	
2536	  if (g_cam_mclk_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED)
2537	    { mclk_save_state(&mclk_saved);
2538	      mclk_enable_24mhz(); mclk_on = true;
2539	      up_udelay(500); }
2540	
2541	  if (rst_ok) camera_reset();
2542	
2543	  /* ===== SCCB ID read ===== */
2544	
2545	  id_h = sccb_read_reg(GC2145_REG_ID_H);
2546	  if (id_h < 0)
2547	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] ID high read fail: %d\n", id_h);
2548	      ret = id_h; goto cleanup; }
2549	
2550	  id_l = sccb_read_reg(GC2145_REG_ID_L);
2551	  if (id_l < 0)
2552	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] ID low read fail: %d\n", id_l);
2553	      ret = id_l; goto cleanup; }
2554	
2555	  chip_id = (uint16_t)((id_h << 8) | id_l);
2556	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
2557	         "[camera] GC2145 ID: 0x%04X (0xF0=0x%02X 0xF1=0x%02X)\n",
2558	         chip_id, (uint8_t)id_h, (uint8_t)id_l);
2559	
2560	  ret = (chip_id == 0x2145) ? 0 : -ENODEV;
2561	
2562	cleanup:
2563	
2564	  /* ===== Restore ALL saved GPIO states ===== */
2565	
2566	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
2567	
2568	  if (mclk_on)     mclk_restore_state(&mclk_saved);
2569	  if (rst_ok)      gpio_restore_state(&rst_saved);
2570	  if (pwdn_ok)     gpio_restore_state(&pwdn_saved);
2571	  if (pwr_ok)      gpio_restore_state(&pwr_saved);
2572	  if (scl_ok)      gpio_restore_state(&scl_saved);
2573	  if (sda_ok)      gpio_restore_state(&sda_saved);
2574	
2575	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] Cleanup done - pins restored\n");
2576	
2577	  if (ret == 0 && stop_ret < 0) ret = stop_ret;
2578	
2579	  return ret;
2580	}

2582	/****************************************************************************
2583	 * Name: bk7258_camera_io
2584	 *   Phase 1 Step 1: configure DVP data pins (P29-P39), readback verify,
2585	 *   deconfigure, readback verify restore.
2586	 ****************************************************************************/
2587	
2588	int bk7258_camera_io(void)
2589	{
2590	  int ret, i;
2591	  uint32_t val, expected;
2592	
2593	  ret = camera_check_config();
2594	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
2595	
2596	  /* Config DVP pins */
2597	
2598	  ret = dvp_io_config();
2599	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
2600	
2601	  /* Readback verify: second_func=1, input_en=0, output_en=1(disabled) */
2602	
2603	  for (i = 0; i < DVP_PIN_COUNT; i++)
2604	    {
2605	      int pin = DVP_PIN_FIRST + i;
2606	      val = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
2607	      if (!(val & GPIO_CFG_SECOND_FUNC))
2608	        {
2609	          syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] P%d second_func not set: 0x%08X\n",
2610	                 pin, val);
2611	          ret = -EIO;
2612	          goto cleanup;
2613	        }
2614	      if (val & GPIO_CFG_INPUT_EN)
2615	        {
2616	          syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] P%d input_en still set: 0x%08X\n",
2617	                 pin, val);
2618	          ret = -EIO;
2619	          goto cleanup;
2620	        }
2621	    }
2622	
2623	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] DVP IO config readback OK (P29-P39)\n");
2624	
2625	cleanup:
2626	  /* Deconfig and verify restore */
2627	
2628	  dvp_io_deconfig();
2629	
2630	  for (i = 0; i < DVP_PIN_COUNT; i++)
2631	    {
2632	      int pin = DVP_PIN_FIRST + i;
2633	      val = getreg32(BK7258_GPIO_CFG(pin));
2634	      expected = g_dvp_state[i].cfg;
2635	      if (val != expected)
2636	        {
2637	          syslog(LOG_ERR,
2638	                 "[camera] P%d CFG restore mismatch: 0x%08X vs 0x%08X\n",
2639	                 pin, val, expected);
2640	          if (ret == 0) ret = -EIO;
2641	        }
2642	    }
2643	
2644	  if (ret == 0)
2645	    syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] DVP IO deconfig readback OK\n");
2646	
2647	  return ret;
2648	}

2650	/****************************************************************************
2651	 * Name: bk7258_camera_init
2652	 *   Phase 1 Step 2: power on, MCLK, reset, read ID, write GC2145 init
2653	 *   table (640x480), readback verify, keep MCLK/power on for
2654	 *   oscilloscope verification.
2655	 ****************************************************************************/
2656	
2657	int bk7258_camera_init(void)
2658	{
2659	  gpio_state_t sda_saved, scl_saved, rst_saved;
2660	  gpio_state_t pwr_saved, pwdn_saved;
2661	  mclk_state_t mclk_saved = { .valid = false };
2662	  int id_h, id_l;
2663	  uint16_t chip_id;
2664	  int ret, stop_ret;
2665	  bool sda_ok = false, scl_ok = false, rst_ok = false;
2666	  bool pwr_ok = false, pwdn_ok = false;
2667	  bool mclk_on = false;
2668	  bool dvp_ok = false;
2669	
2670	  /* ===== Config validation ===== */
2671	
2672	  ret = camera_check_config();
2673	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
2674	
2675	  /* ===== DVP data pin mux ===== */
2676	
2677	  ret = dvp_io_config();
2678	  if (ret < 0) return ret;
2679	  dvp_ok = true;
2680	
2681	  /* ===== SCCB pin setup ===== */
2682	
2683	  gpio_save_state(g_cam_sda_pin, &sda_saved); sda_ok = true;
2684	  gpio_save_state(g_cam_scl_pin, &scl_saved); scl_ok = true;
2685	  gpio_release(g_cam_sda_pin);
2686	  gpio_release(g_cam_scl_pin);
2687	  up_udelay(100);
2688	
2689	  /* ===== RST, power, MCLK ===== */
2690	
2691	  if (g_cam_rst_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED)
2692	    { gpio_save_state(g_cam_rst_pin, &rst_saved); rst_ok = true; }
2693	
2694	  camera_power_on(&pwr_saved, &pwr_ok, &pwdn_saved, &pwdn_ok);
2695	
2696	  if (g_cam_mclk_pin != CAMERA_GPIO_UNCONFIGURED)
2697	    { mclk_save_state(&mclk_saved);
2698	      mclk_enable_24mhz(); mclk_on = true;
2699	      up_udelay(500); }
2700	
2701	  if (rst_ok) camera_reset();
2702	
2703	  /* ===== Read chip ID ===== */
2704	
2705	  id_h = sccb_read_reg(GC2145_REG_ID_H);
2706	  if (id_h < 0)
2707	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] ID high read fail: %d\n", id_h);
2708	      ret = id_h; goto cleanup; }
2709	
2710	  id_l = sccb_read_reg(GC2145_REG_ID_L);
2711	  if (id_l < 0)
2712	    { syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] ID low read fail: %d\n", id_l);
2713	      ret = id_l; goto cleanup; }
2714	
2715	  chip_id = (uint16_t)((id_h << 8) | id_l);
2716	  if (chip_id != 0x2145)
2717	    {
2718	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] Bad ID: 0x%04X (expected 0x2145)\n",
2719	             chip_id);
2720	      ret = -ENODEV;
2721	      goto cleanup;
2722	    }
2723	
2724	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] GC2145 ID OK: 0x%04X\n", chip_id);
2725	
2726	  /* ===== Write init table ===== */
2727	
2728	  ret = gc2145_write_table(gc2145_init,
2729	                           sizeof(gc2145_init) / sizeof(gc2145_init[0]));
2730	  if (ret < 0)
2731	    {
2732	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] Init table write failed\n");
2733	      goto cleanup;
2734	    }
2735	
2736	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] Init table written (%d entries)\n",
2737	         (int)(sizeof(gc2145_init) / sizeof(gc2145_init[0])));
2738	
2739	  /* ===== Write 640x480 resolution table ===== */
2740	
2741	  ret = gc2145_write_table(gc2145_640x480,
2742	                           sizeof(gc2145_640x480) / sizeof(gc2145_640x480[0]));
2743	  if (ret < 0)
2744	    {
2745	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] 640x480 table write failed\n");
2746	      goto cleanup;
2747	    }
2748	
2749	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "[camera] 640x480 table written (%d entries)\n",
2750	         (int)(sizeof(gc2145_640x480) / sizeof(gc2145_640x480[0])));
2751	
2752	  /* ===== Readback verify: key registers ===== */
2753	
2754	  {
2755	    int val84 = sccb_read_reg(0x84);
2756	    if (val84 < 0)
2757	      {
2758	        syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] Reg 0x84 readback fail: %d\n", val84);
2759	        ret = val84;
2760	        goto cleanup;
2761	      }
2762	    if (val84 != 0x02)
2763	      {
2764	        syslog(LOG_ERR,
2765	               "[camera] Reg 0x84 mismatch: 0x%02X (expected 0x02)\n",
2766	               val84);
2767	        ret = -EIO;
2768	        goto cleanup;
2769	      }
2770	  }
2771	
2772	  {
2773	    int val97 = sccb_read_reg(0x97);
2774	    if (val97 < 0)
2775	      {
2776	        syslog(LOG_ERR, "[camera] Reg 0x97 readback fail: %d\n", val97);
2777	        ret = val97;
2778	        goto cleanup;
2779	      }
2780	    if (val97 != 0x02)
2781	      {
2782	        syslog(LOG_ERR,
2783	               "[camera] Reg 0x97 mismatch: 0x%02X (expected 0x02=HOUT hi)\n",
2784	               val97);
2785	        ret = -EIO;
2786	        goto cleanup;
2787	      }
2788	  }
2789	
2790	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
2791	         "[camera] GC2145 init complete - 640x480 VYUY\n");
2792	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
2793	         "[camera] MCLK/power left ON for oscilloscope verification\n");
2794	
2795	  /* Restore SCCB pins only - MCLK and power stay ON */
2796	
2797	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
2798	  if (scl_ok) gpio_restore_state(&scl_saved);
2799	  if (sda_ok) gpio_restore_state(&sda_saved);
2800	
2801	  return 0;
2802	
2803	cleanup:
2804	
2805	  stop_ret = sccb_stop();
2806	  if (mclk_on)     mclk_restore_state(&mclk_saved);
2807	  if (rst_ok)      gpio_restore_state(&rst_saved);

3	> 结论先行：**用"满电→带重载→跑到自动关机"的整机放电法**，直接得续航小时数，绕开串表/供电的所有坑。
4	> 适用场景：临近截止、要快出可信数字。
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 一、为什么用整机放电法（先看这段，少走弯路）
9	
10	之前试过"万用表串电池线量电流"的估算法，踩了两个坑，最终放弃：
11	
12	1. **串表 + 插 USB = 测的是充电电流，不是耗电。**
13	   两个 Type-C 口都带 5V(VBUS)，插上就给板子供电 + 给电池充电。表串在电池线上量到的是**充进电池的电流**：
14	   空闲时读 37mA、跑 `lcdtest oeye`（更耗电）反而降到 24mA——"负载越大电池电流越小"正是充电的铁证，红灯=充电灯。
15	
16	2. **能敲命令的 NSH 只在板载 CH340（Type-C）上，拔了 Type-C 就没法敲命令。**
17	   - NSH 控制台 = **UART0 = 板载 CH340**，在系统里是 **`/dev/ttyUSB*`**（ch341 驱动，115200 8N1）。
18	   - 外接的 CH343 USB-UART 适配器是 **`/dev/ttyACM*`**（cdc_acm 驱动）。
19	   - 飞线焊的"大核 log 口 / DBG UART / GPIO6-7"**不是交互 NSH**——能打开串口、但没输出、打不进字。
20	   - 死结：**要敲命令 → 必须插带 CH340 的 Type-C → 必然供电充电 → 电池不放电 → 测不了续航。**
21	
22	> 所以放弃串表估算，改用**整机放电法**：不量电流，直接计时"满电跑到关机要多久"。
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 二、SOP（照着做）
27	
28	### 1. 还原 + 充满
29	- 把万用表从电池串联里撤掉，**电池线恢复原样直连**，确认板子能正常开机。
30	- 插充电，**充到绿灯（满电）**。
31	
32	lcdtest  ### 2. 起负载：用 `camera velapet`（已实测：拔线能继续跑）
33	满电后插上出 `ttyUSB0` 的那个 Type-C，`picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0` 进 nsh，敲：
34	- **`camera velapet`** —— 摄像头 + 双屏 + LED 一起跑，重载、掉电快、是**最坏情况续航**（报告最有说服力）。
35	  **实测拔掉 Type-C 后它能继续在电池上跑**（没人脸/手势时只有"睁眼+眨眼"两种动作，会周期眨眼 = loop 仍活着，属正常）。
36	
37	> ⚠️ **不要用 `lcdtest oeye` 做放电负载**：实测拔掉 Type-C 后它跑几秒就**卡死**（前台命令，控制台一断就挂）。仅 velapet 能拔线续跑。
38	>
39	> ⚠️ 别用空闲测：1000mAh × 空闲 ~13mA ≈ 70+ 小时，3 天跑不完。**压测就要带重载**，快且是保守值。
40	
41	### 3. 关键一步：拔 Type-C，看能不能继续跑
42	起好 `camera velapet` 后**拔掉 Type-C**，盯 10 秒：
43	- **画面继续跑（周期眨眼、不重启）** → 无缝切电池，成了。**记下此刻时间 = T0（起跑）。**（已实测 velapet 走到这步 OK）
44	- **一拔就黑屏/重启** → 命令丢了，走「四、兜底」。
45	
46	### 4. 跑到关机，记时间
47	让它一直跑到**自动关机（屏灭）**。快没电时（**< 3500mV**）**红灯会闪**，是结束预警。
48	- **续航 = 关机时刻 − 起跑时刻**。
49	- 用手机拍屏幕 + 一个钟表，或每 15~30 分钟回来看一眼，别错过关机点。
50	
51	### 5. 记录进报告
52	写清"**XX 负载场景下满电续航 = N 小时 M 分**"，注明负载（`camera velapet` / `lcdtest oeye`）与电池容量（1000mAh）。
53	
54	---
55	
56	## 三、关键事实速查
57	
58	| 项 | 值 |
59	|---|---|
60	| 电池容量 | 1000 mAh |
61	| NSH 控制台 | UART0 / 板载 CH340 / `/dev/ttyUSB*` / 115200 8N1 |
62	| 外接 CH343 适配器 | `/dev/ttyACM*`（不是 NSH，是调试 log 口） |
63	| 低电红灯闪阈值 | VBAT < 3500 mV |
64	| 满电指示 | 绿灯 |
65	| 充电中指示 | 红灯 |
66	| 空闲电流（参考） | ~13 mA（约 70+ 小时，测续航太慢） |
67	| 连接命令 | `fuser -k /dev/ttyUSB0; picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0` |
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 四、兜底：如果第 3 步"一拔就重启"
72	
73	拔 Type-C 会重启 → 没法靠拔线保持负载。最稳的办法是**让板子开机自动带载跑**：
74	在开机启动脚本 `rcS` 里加一行（如 `lcdtest oeye &`），重烧一次。之后**拔掉所有 USB、纯电池上电也会自动带载放电**，只管计时到关机。
75	
76	- 改动极小、风险很低（不碰控制台 UART 配置）。
77	- 需要重编 + 用 Type-C 重烧一次固件。
78	- 如需，找 Kiro 帮忙加这一行并重烧。
79	
80	---
81	
82	## 五、电量读数说明（重要，别被误导）
83	
84	`lcdtest bat` 的电量是**纯电压换算**（raw ADC → mV → %），**没有库仑计**，所以：
85	- **带载时 % 会掉、拔载/重启会回弹**，这是**负载压降（voltage sag）**，不是真掉电。
86	  实测：满电静态 `4200mV/100%`；`camera init` 后摄像头持续供电 → `4123mV/91%`；重启关掉摄像头 → 回 `4202mV/100%`。
87	- **进度别看 %**：续航只认"**跑到自动关机的时间**"（关机=真·欠压保护 <3500mV）。
88	- 要记曲线就记 **mV**（比 % 靠谱），且注意是带载压降后的值。
89	- `camera`（无参数）会**重启板子**，测续航时别乱敲；velapet 起来后就别再碰键盘，直接拔 Type-C 计时。
90	
91	---
92	
93	## 六、本次实测记录
94	
95	| 项 | 值 |
96	|---|---|
97	| 日期 | 2026-09-16 |
98	| 电池 | 1000 mAh |
99	| 负载 | `camera velapet`（摄像头+双屏+LED，无人脸时循环睁眼/眨眼） |
100	| 满电电压 | 4200 mV（~100%，raw=6533） |
101	| **T0（满电拔 USB 起跑）** | **15:15** |
102	| **满载电流（串表实测，纯电池、拔 Type-C）** | **~138 mA（稳定 137~139mA）** |
103	| **续航估算（1000mAh ÷ 138mA）** | **≈ 7.25 小时（7h15m）— 理论上限** |
104	| 实测跑到欠压关机（预计） | ~6.5~7 小时（可用容量 <100% + 末段电流升高，会略短于上限） |
105	| T1（自动关机实测） | 待记录（≈22:00 左右应关机，跑了约 6h47m 仍在跑，与估算吻合） |
106	
107	> **两种口径**：
108	> - 快法（串表）：`续航 ≈ 1000mAh ÷ 满载电流(mA)` = 7h15m（上限）。**推荐写报告用这个**，2 分钟出。
109	> - 慢法（放电到关机）：T1−T0 实测，最真实，但要等到关机。
110	>
111	> **红灯闪 ≠ 马上没电的矛盾**：velapet 低电阈值 `VP_BAT_LOW_MV=3500mV`，它读的是**带载电压**（会被负载压低）；而 `lcdtest bat` 若插着 Type-C 读，是**充电抬高后的电压**，所以显示 83% 却已红灯闪。带载电压才是关机依据。
112	
113	### 续航总结（串表法实测，1000mAh）
114	
115	| 场景 | 说明 | 实测电流 | 续航估算(1000÷I) |
116	|---|---|---|---|
117	| **真待机（复位进 NSH、不跑命令）** | 熄屏、无摄像头/DVP | **~16 mA** | **≈ 62 h（约 2.6 天）** |
118	| 重载 `camera velapet`（运行中） | 摄像头+双屏+LED | ~138 mA | ≈ 7.25 h（7h15m） |
119	| `lcdtest oeye`（运行中） | 双屏眼神动画 | ~80 mA | ≈ 12.5 h |
120	| velapet 退出后（未彻底下电） | 摄像头/MCLK/LCD LDO 残留 | ~102 mA | —（应回落到待机） |
121	
122	> **关键发现（已纠正）：真待机很低（~16mA），问题是外设"用完没关"。**
123	> 复位进 NSH 干净待机仅 ~16mA（续航约 2.6 天，正常）。之前测到的 102mA 是**跑完 velapet 后**测的——velapet 退出只关了背光、没关摄像头电源/MCLK 和 LCD LDO_3V3，残留 ~86mA。
124	> **根因**：`bk7258_lcd_preview_deinit()` 只关背光、保留 LDO_3V3；velapet 退出路径未走摄像头下电。而 `camera id` 的清理里已有完整下电序列（PWR 置无效 + 关 MCLK 门 + `dvp_module_clk_disable`）可复用。
125	> **优化（低风险小改）**：命令退出时复用该下电序列 + 关 LCD LDO_3V3 → 用完待机从 102mA 回落到 ~16mA。更进一步启用 PM（idle WFI + 时钟门控）可再压低 16mA。
126	
127	### 关机/深睡电流怎么测（说明）
128	本板是开发板，**没有真正的软关机/PMIC 下电**，"关机"只有两种可理解的口径：
129	- **欠压保护关机**：电池放到 ~3.0–3.3V 触发保护，此时基本断电，电池线电流≈0（只剩极小漏电）。
130	- **深睡电流（需实现 PM 后才有意义）**：当前固件无深睡。若将来做了 WFI/停机深睡，测法同串表——进深睡态后读电池线电流（可能到 µA/mA 级，需用 UT181A 的 mA/µA 档提高分辨率）。
131	> 现阶段"关机电流"无独立可测态；要给"最低功耗"数，就是上表的**真待机 ~16mA**。
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 七、注意事项
136	
137	- 一次深放电（跑到欠压保护关机）对锂电无碍；但**别反复深放**，测完及时充回。
138	- 关机是电池欠压保护动作（约 3.0~3.3V 截止），属正常，不是板子坏了。
139	- 报告里注明这是**特定重载场景**续航，不是待机续航；两者差异很大，勿混。

# BK7258 Power Optimization Plan

## Context
After running `camera velapet` or `lcdtest oeye`, the BK7258 DevKit stays at ~102mA instead of returning to the ~16mA idle baseline. Root cause: command exit paths don't power off the camera sensor (MCLK + PWR_CTL) or disable the LCD LDO_3V3 (P52).

## Implementation Steps

- [x] **Step 1: Extract `camera_power_off()` function**
  - File: `board/contest_board/src/bk7258_camera.c`
  - Add static `camera_power_off()` after `camera_power_on()`
  - Disable MCLK gate (CIS_AUXS_CKEN bit9)
  - Drive PWR_CTL inactive (opposite polarity of `camera_power_on`)
  - Drive PWDNB to standby (opposite polarity)
  - Idempotent: safe to call multiple times
  - No-ops if pins are -1 (unconfigured)
  - **Acceptance**: function compiles, does not touch DVP controller/data pins

- [x] **Step 2: Update all camera command exit paths**
  - File: `board/contest_board/src/bk7258_camera.c`
  - `bk7258_camera_stop()` → replace inline MCLK/PWR code with `camera_power_off()`
  - `bk7258_camera_preview()` → `cleanup_ctrl:` label → call `camera_power_off()`
  - `bk7258_camera_velapet()` → `stop_stream:` and `cleanup_ctrl:` → call `camera_power_off()`
  - `bk7258_camera_hr()` → `stop_stream:` and `cleanup_ctrl:` → call `camera_power_off()`
  - `bk7258_camera_track()` → `stop_stream:` and `cleanup_ctrl:` → call `camera_power_off()`
  - **Acceptance**: UT181A reads ~16mA after each command exits, commands re-runnable

- [x] **Step 3: LCD LDO_3V3 off on exit**
  - File: `board/contest_board/src/bk7258_gc9d01.c`
  - `bk7258_lcd_preview_deinit()` → add SPI1 deinit + `gpio_write(LCD_PIN_LDO33_EN, 0)`
  - `lcdtest_oeye()` → add SPI1 deinit + BL off + LDO_3V3 off before return
  - `lcdtest_blink()` → add SPI1 deinit + BL off + LDO_3V3 off before return
  - **Acceptance**: UT181A reads ~16mA after lcdtest oeye/blink exits

- [x] **Step 4: Build verification**
  - `cd cmake_out/contest2026_098_board_nsh && ninja -j16` → nuttx.bin generated
  - camera_power_off() and lcd_preview_deinit() changes compiled cleanly

- [x] **Step 5: Update documentation**
  - `docs/续航压测_SOP.md` — updated power table with optimization results
  - `docs/技术报告.md` section 3.5 — added optimized exit row to power table

## Pending (requires hardware)
- **On-board verification**: UT181A串表法, velapet/hr/oeye exit → confirm ~16mA
- **Re-run test**: confirm commands work after power-off cycle
- Update docs with actual measured numbers once verified

## Key Safety Notes
- P52 (LDO_3V3 → U3 ME6211C33) supplies **only** the LCD 3.3V rail. Camera uses separate LDOs via PWR_CTL. Safe to disable after preview.
- `camera init` debug behavior (MCLK/power left ON) is NOT affected — `camera_power_off()` is only called on exit paths, not in `camera_init()`.

105	 ****************************************************************************/
106	
107	/****************************************************************************
108	 * Name: psram_putreg / psram_getreg
109	 *
110	 * Description:
111	 *   Raw 32-bit register access helpers.
112	 *
113	 ****************************************************************************/
114	
115	static inline void psram_putreg(uint32_t val, uint32_t addr)
116	{
117	  *(volatile uint32_t *)addr = val;
118	}
119	
120	static inline uint32_t psram_getreg(uint32_t addr)
121	{
122	  return *(volatile uint32_t *)addr;
123	}
124	
125	/****************************************************************************
126	 * Name: ana_write
127	 *
128	 * Description:
129	 *   Write to an analog register (0x440101xx) and poll the SPI bus
130	 *   completion bit.  The BK7258 analog registers are behind a serial
131	 *   SPI bridge; writes are NOT instantaneous and must be polled.
132	 *
133	 *   Source: Armino sys_ll.h -> sys_ll_set_analog_reg_value()
134	 *           + bk7258_audio.c -> ana_write()
135	 *
136	 *   WARNING: Every write to an address in 0x440101xx MUST go through
137	 *   this function.  A plain psram_putreg() will appear to succeed
138	 *   (the value is latched in the register) but the SPI transfer may
139	 *   not have completed, causing the analog front-end to never
140	 *   configure properly.
141	 *
142	 ****************************************************************************/
143	
144	static void ana_write(uintptr_t addr, uint32_t val)
145	{
146	  uint32_t idx = (addr - ANA_BASE) >> 2;
147	
148	  psram_putreg(val, addr);
149	
150	  while (psram_getreg(ANA_SPI_STATE_REG) & (1u << idx))
151	    {
152	    }
153	}
154	
155	/****************************************************************************
156	 * Name: ana_rmw
157	 *
158	 * Description:
159	 *   Read-modify-write a bit field in an analog register.
160	 *   Reads the current value, clears the mask at pos, sets the new
161	 *   value, and writes via ana_write() (with SPI polling).
162	 *
163	 ****************************************************************************/
164	
165	static void ana_rmw(uintptr_t addr, int pos, uint32_t mask,
166	                    uint32_t val)
167	{
168	  uint32_t reg = psram_getreg(addr);
169	
170	  reg &= ~(mask << pos);
171	  reg |= ((val & mask) << pos);
172	  ana_write(addr, reg);
173	}

177	 ****************************************************************************/
178	
179	/****************************************************************************
180	 * Name: psram_set_sf_reset
181	 *
182	 * Description:
183	 *   Set or release the PSRAM serial-flash interface reset.
184	 *   Uses read-modify-write to preserve other REG2 bits.
185	 *
186	 *   Source: Armino psram_ll_macro_def.h ->
187	 *           psram_ll_set_sf_reset_value()
188	 *
189	 ****************************************************************************/
190	
191	static void psram_set_sf_reset(uint32_t value)
192	{
193	  uint32_t reg = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REG2);
194	
195	  reg &= ~PSRAM_SF_RESET_BIT;
196	  reg |= (value & 1);
197	  psram_putreg(reg, PSRAM_LL_REG2);
198	}
199	
200	/****************************************************************************
201	 * Name: psram_set_reg2_bypass
202	 *
203	 * Description:
204	 *   Set the PSRAM bypass bit (bit[1]) in REG2, preserving other bits.
205	 *
206	 *   Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_config_init()
207	 *
208	 ****************************************************************************/
209	
210	static void psram_set_reg2_bypass(void)
211	{
212	  uint32_t val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REG2);
213	
214	  val |= (0x1 << 1);
215	  psram_putreg(val, PSRAM_LL_REG2);
216	}

218	/****************************************************************************
219	 * Name: psram_cmd_reset
220	 *
221	 * Description:
222	 *   Issue a reset command to the PSRAM chip via the command interface.
223	 *
224	 *   Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_set_cmd_reset()
225	 ****************************************************************************/
226	
227	static void psram_cmd_reset(void)
228	{
229	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_CMD_RESET, PSRAM_LL_REG8);
230	}
231	
232	/****************************************************************************
233	 * Name: psram_cmd_write
234	 *
235	 * Description:
236	 *   Write a value to a PSRAM register address via the command
237	 *   interface.  Includes a generous timeout to avoid infinite hang.
238	 *
239	 *   Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_cmd_write()
240	 ****************************************************************************/
241	
242	static int psram_cmd_write(uint32_t addr, uint32_t value)
243	{
244	  int timeout = CMD_READ_POLL_OUTER * CMD_READ_POLL_INNER;
245	
246	  psram_putreg(addr, PSRAM_LL_REG9);
247	  psram_putreg(value, PSRAM_LL_REGA);
248	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_TRIG, PSRAM_LL_REG8);
249	
250	  while ((psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REG8) & PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_TRIG) &&
251	         --timeout > 0)
252	    {
253	    }
254	
255	  if (timeout <= 0)
256	    {
257	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "psram: cmd_write timeout\n");
258	      return -ETIMEDOUT;
259	    }
260	
261	  return OK;
262	}
263	
264	/****************************************************************************
265	 * Name: psram_cmd_read
266	 *
267	 * Description:
268	 *   Read a value from a PSRAM chip register via the command interface.
269	 *   Retries up to CMD_READ_RETRIES times, with SF reset + cmd reset
270	 *   between retries.
271	 *
272	 *   Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_cmd_read()
273	 ****************************************************************************/
274	
275	static uint32_t psram_cmd_read(uint32_t addr)
276	{
277	  int retry;
278	  int outer;
279	  int inner;
280	
281	  for (retry = 0; retry < CMD_READ_RETRIES; retry++)
282	    {
283	      psram_putreg(addr, PSRAM_LL_REG9);
284	      psram_putreg(PSRAM_CMD_READ_TRIG, PSRAM_LL_REG8);
285	
286	      for (outer = 0; outer < CMD_READ_POLL_OUTER; outer++)
287	        {
288	          for (inner = 0; inner < CMD_READ_POLL_INNER; inner++)
289	            {
290	              if (!(psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REG8) &
291	                    PSRAM_CMD_READ_TRIG))
292	                {
293	                  return psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
294	                }
295	            }
296	        }
297	
298	      /* Timeout: reset SF interface and retry */
299	
300	      psram_set_sf_reset(0);
301	      psram_set_sf_reset(1);
302	      psram_cmd_reset();
303	    }
304	
305	  return 0;
306	}

308	/****************************************************************************
309	 * Name: psram_set_clk
310	 *
311	 * Description:
312	 *   Set PSRAM clock source and divider.
313	 *
314	 *   Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_set_clk()
315	 ****************************************************************************/
316	
317	static void psram_set_clk(uint32_t sel, uint32_t div)
318	{
319	  uint32_t val = psram_getreg(SYS_CPU_CLK_DIV2);
320	
321	  val &= ~(CLK_DIV2_CKSEL_PSRAM | CLK_DIV2_CKDIV_PSRAM);
322	  val |= (sel ? CLK_DIV2_CKSEL_PSRAM : 0) |
323	         (div ? CLK_DIV2_CKDIV_PSRAM : 0);
324	  psram_putreg(val, SYS_CPU_CLK_DIV2);
325	}
