327	/****************************************************************************
328	 * Private Functions — Chip-Specific Init
329	 *
330	 * Each function configures the PSRAM controller for a specific chip
331	 * type, reads and verifies the chip ID, then configures the chip's
332	 * own mode registers (MR0/MR4/MR8) for proper latency, drive
333	 * strength, and burst settings.
334	 *
335	 * Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_APS6408L_init(),
336	 *         psram_hal_APS128XXO_OB9_init(),
337	 *         psram_hal_W955D8MKY_5J_init()
338	 ****************************************************************************/
339	
340	/****************************************************************************
341	 * Name: psram_init_aps6408l
342	 *
343	 * Description:
344	 *   Init sequence for AP Memory APS6408L (8MB, ID 0x8D09).
345	 *   Configures MR0 (drive/latency) and MR4 (write latency).
346	 *
347	 ****************************************************************************/
348	
349	static int psram_init_aps6408l(uint32_t *id)
350	{
351	  uint32_t val;
352	
353	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_MODE_APS6408L, PSRAM_LL_REG4);
354	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_DRV_APS6408L, PSRAM_LL_REG5);
355	  psram_cmd_reset();
356	  up_udelay(500);
357	
358	  val = psram_cmd_read(0x00000000);
359	  if (val == 0 || val != *id)
360	    {
361	      return -1;
362	    }
363	
364	  *id = val;
365	
366	  /* MR0: set drive strength and latency */
367	
368	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
369	  val = (val & ~0x1f) | (0x4 << 2) | 0x3;
370	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000000, val);
371	
372	  /* MR4: set write latency (6 @ 120 MHz) */
373	
374	  psram_cmd_read(0x00000004);
375	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
376	  val = (val & ~(0x7 << 5)) | (0x6 << 5);
377	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000004, val);
378	
379	  return 0;
380	}
381	
382	/****************************************************************************
383	 * Name: psram_init_aps128xxo
384	 *
385	 * Description:
386	 *   Init sequence for AP Memory APS128XXO (16MB, ID 0x8D08).
387	 *   Configures MR0 (drive/latency), MR4 (write latency), and MR8
388	 *   (burst length).
389	 *
390	 ****************************************************************************/
391	
392	static int psram_init_aps128xxo(uint32_t *id)
393	{
394	  uint32_t val;
395	
396	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_MODE_APS128XXO, PSRAM_LL_REG4);
397	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_DRV_APS128XXO, PSRAM_LL_REG5);
398	  psram_cmd_reset();
399	  up_udelay(500);
400	
401	  val = psram_cmd_read(0x00000000);
402	  if (val == 0 || val != *id)
403	    {
404	      return -1;
405	    }
406	
407	  *id = val;
408	
409	  /* MR0: set drive strength and latency */
410	
411	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
412	  val = (val & ~0x1f) | (0x6 << 2) | 0x2;
413	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000000, val);
414	
415	  /* MR4: set write latency (6 @ 120 MHz) */
416	
417	  psram_cmd_read(0x00000004);
418	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
419	  val = (val & ~(0x7 << 5)) | (0x6 << 5);
420	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000004, val);
421	
422	  /* MR8: set burst length bit */
423	
424	  psram_cmd_read(0x00000008);
425	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
426	  val |= 0x40;
427	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000008, val);
428	
429	  return 0;
430	}
431	
432	/****************************************************************************
433	 * Name: psram_init_w955d8mky
434	 *
435	 * Description:
436	 *   Init sequence for Winbond W955D8MKY (4MB, ID 0x1C8F on BK7258).
437	 *   Configures drive strength via a command write to 0x01000000.
438	 *
439	 ****************************************************************************/
440	
441	static int psram_init_w955d8mky(uint32_t *id)
442	{
443	  uint32_t val;
444	  uint32_t io_drv = 0;
445	
446	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_MODE_W955D8MKY, PSRAM_LL_REG4);
447	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_DRV_W955D8MKY, PSRAM_LL_REG5);
448	  psram_cmd_reset();
449	  up_udelay(500);
450	
451	  val = psram_cmd_read(0x01000000);
452	  if (val == 0)
453	    {
454	      return -1;
455	    }
456	
457	  /* Configure drive strength */
458	
459	  val = 0x1c8f | (io_drv << 4);
460	  psram_cmd_write(0x01000000, val);
461	
462	  /* Verify */
463	
464	  psram_cmd_read(0x01000000);
465	
466	  *id = PSRAM_ID_W955D8MKY;
467	  return 0;
468	}

474	/****************************************************************************
475	 * Name: bk7258_psram_init
476	 *
477	 * Description:
478	 *   Initialize the BK7258 PSRAM controller and detect the external
479	 *   PSRAM chip.  Sets g_psram_chip_id and g_psram_size.
480	 *
481	 *   Sequence (source: Armino psram_hal_power_clk_enable +
482	 *   psram_hal_config_init):
483	 *     1. Set voltage: ana_reg13 psldo_swb=1, vpsramsel=3 (1.95V)
484	 *     2. Enable PSRAM LDO: ana_reg13 enpsram=1, wait 1ms
485	 *     3. Enable AHB PSRAM power domain: clear pwd_ahbp bit
486	 *     4. Set init clock to 80 MHz (320MHz PLL, div=1)
487	 *     5. Enable PSRAM peripheral clock (bit 19)
488	 *     6. Release SF reset + set bypass bit in REG2
489	 *     7. Auto-detect: try APS6408L -> APS128XXO -> W955D8MKY
490	 *        (each: set mode/drive, reset, read ID, configure MRs)
491	 *     8. Switch to 120 MHz default clock
492	 *
493	 *   NOTE: Cache coherency not addressed (no D-cache configured).
494	 *
495	 * Returned Value:
496	 *   OK on success (chip detected), -ENODEV if no known chip found.
497	 *
498	 ****************************************************************************/
499	
500	int bk7258_psram_init(void)
501	{
502	  uint32_t val;
503	  uint32_t id;
504	
505	  if (g_psram_init_done)
506	    {
507	      return OK;
508	    }
509	
510	  g_psram_chip_id = 0;
511	  g_psram_size = 0;
512	
513	  /* Step 1: Set PSRAM LDO voltage to 1.95V (psldo_swb=1, vpsramsel=3).
514	   * Source: Armino sys_hal_psram_psldo_vset()
515	   * Must use ana_write (read-modify-write + SPI poll), not plain MMIO.
516	   */
517	
518	  ana_rmw(SYS_ANA_REG13, 28, 0x1, 1);   /* psldo_swb = 1 */
519	  ana_rmw(SYS_ANA_REG13, 29, 0x3, 3);   /* vpsramsel = 3 */
520	
521	  /* Step 2: Enable PSRAM LDO.
522	   * Source: Armino sys_hal_psram_ldo_enable()
523	   */
524	
525	  ana_rmw(SYS_ANA_REG13, 31, 0x1, 1);   /* enpsram = 1 */
526	  up_mdelay(1);
527	
528	  /* Step 3: Enable AHB PSRAM power domain.
529	   * Source: Armino bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(AHBP_PSRAM, ON)
530	   *         -> sys_hal_module_power_ctrl()
531	   * Clear pwd_ahbp (bit 5) to power on the AHB domain.
532	   */
533	
534	  val = psram_getreg(SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP);
535	  val &= ~PWD_AHBP_BIT;
536	  psram_putreg(val, SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP);
537	
538	  /* Step 4: Set init clock to 80 MHz (320 MHz PLL, divider=1).
539	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_set_clk(PSRAM_80M)
540	   */
541	
542	  psram_set_clk(0, 1);   /* sel=0 (320MHz), div=1 */
543	
544	  /* Step 5: Enable PSRAM peripheral clock (bit 19).
545	   * Source: Armino sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up(CLK_PWR_ID_PSRAM, PWR_UP)
546	   */
547	
548	  val = psram_getreg(SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE);
549	  val |= PSRAM_CKEN_BIT;
550	  psram_putreg(val, SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE);
551	
552	  /* Step 6: Release SF reset and set bypass bit.
553	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_config_init()
554	   */
555	
556	  psram_set_sf_reset(1);
557	  psram_set_reg2_bypass();
558	
559	  up_udelay(3000);
560	
561	  /* Step 7: Auto-detect PSRAM chip type.
562	   * Try each type in sequence; first match wins.
563	   * Each init function sets mode/drive, resets, reads ID,
564	   * and configures the chip's mode registers.
565	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_config_init()
566	   */
567	
568	  id = PSRAM_ID_APS6408L;
569	  if (psram_init_aps6408l(&id) == 0)
570	    {
571	      g_psram_chip_id = id;
572	      g_psram_size = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
573	    }
574	  else
575	    {
576	      id = PSRAM_ID_APS128XXO;
577	      if (psram_init_aps128xxo(&id) == 0)
578	        {
579	          g_psram_chip_id = id;
580	          g_psram_size = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
581	        }
582	      else
583	        {
584	          id = PSRAM_ID_W955D8MKY;
585	          if (psram_init_w955d8mky(&id) == 0)
586	            {
587	              g_psram_chip_id = id;
588	              g_psram_size = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
589	            }
590	          else
591	            {
592	              syslog(LOG_ERR,
593	                     "psram: no known chip detected\n");
594	              return -ENODEV;
595	            }
596	        }
597	    }
598	
599	  /* Step 8: Switch to 120 MHz default clock.
600	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_set_default_clk()
601	   */
602	
603	  up_mdelay(1);
604	  psram_set_clk(1, 1);   /* sel=1 (480MHz), div=1 -> 120MHz */
605	
606	  g_psram_init_done = true;
607	
608	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
609	         "psram: init OK, ID=0x%04lx, size=%lu KB\n",
610	         (unsigned long)g_psram_chip_id,
611	         (unsigned long)(g_psram_size / 1024));
612	  return OK;
613	}

641	/****************************************************************************
642	 * Name: bk7258_psram_probe
643	 *
644	 * Description:
645	 *   Full S1 verification: init + ID check + single-word data path
646	 *   test on the memory-mapped window (0x60000000).
647	 *
648	 *   The ID check uses the command-register path (REG9/REG_A/REG_B).
649	 *   The data path test uses the AXI memory-mapped window.  These are
650	 *   two independent hardware paths; testing both in S1 ensures we
651	 *   don't mix up "controller works" with "data window works".
652	 *
653	 *   NOTE: Cache coherency not addressed (no D-cache configured).
654	 *
655	 * Returned Value:
656	 *   OK on success, negative errno on failure.
657	 *
658	 ****************************************************************************/
659	
660	int bk7258_psram_probe(void)
661	{
662	  volatile uint32_t *psram_base;
663	  uint32_t save;
664	  uint32_t readback;
665	  int ret;
666	
667	  /* Run full init sequence */
668	
669	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
670	  if (ret < 0)
671	    {
672	      return ret;
673	    }
674	
675	  /* Single-word data path test on memory-mapped window */
676	
677	  psram_base = (volatile uint32_t *)0x60000000;
678	
679	  /* Save original content (avoid destructive test on first word) */
680	
681	  save = *psram_base;
682	
683	  /* Write test pattern */
684	
685	  *psram_base = 0xdeadbeef;
686	  readback = *psram_base;
687	
688	  /* Restore original content */
689	
690	  *psram_base = save;
691	
692	  if (readback != 0xdeadbeef)
693	    {
694	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "psram: data path FAIL "
695	             "(wrote 0xdeadbeef, read 0x%08lx)\n",
696	             (unsigned long)readback);
697	      return -EIO;
698	    }
699	
700	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "psram: data path OK (0x60000000 verified)\n");
701	  return OK;
702	}

704	/****************************************************************************
705	 * Name: psram_check_no_heap
706	 *
707	 * Description:
708	 *   Guard for destructive tests.  If the PSRAM heap has been
709	 *   initialized its metadata lives at 0x60000000; any write to
710	 *   that region would corrupt it.  Returns -EBUSY if the heap
711	 *   is active.
712	 *
713	 ****************************************************************************/
714	
715	static int psram_check_no_heap(FAR const char *who)
716	{
717	  if (g_psram_heap != NULL)
718	    {
719	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
720	             "psram %s: heap is active, "
721	             "reboot to run destructive tests\n",
722	             who);
723	      return -EBUSY;
724	    }
725	
726	  return OK;
727	}

729	/****************************************************************************
730	 * Name: bk7258_psram_test
731	 *
732	 * Description:
733	 *   Address-in-address destructive test over the PSRAM window.
734	 *   Writes each 32-bit address's own address as the value, then
735	 *   reads back and verifies.  Reports errors, throughput, and
736	 *   boundary checks.
737	 *
738	 *   WARNING: This is a destructive test.  All data in the tested
739	 *   range will be overwritten.
740	 *
741	 * Input Parameters:
742	 *   size_bytes - Number of bytes to test (rounded down to 4-byte
743	 *                alignment).  If 0, uses g_psram_size.
744	 *
745	 * Returned Value:
746	 *   OK on success (zero errors), -EIO if any mismatch found.
747	 *
748	 ****************************************************************************/
749	
750	int bk7258_psram_test(uint32_t size_bytes)
751	{
752	  volatile uint32_t *base = (volatile uint32_t *)0x60000000;
753	  volatile uint32_t *last;
754	  uint32_t errors = 0;
755	  uint32_t first_bad = 0;
756	  uint32_t first_exp = 0;
757	  uint32_t first_got = 0;
758	  uint32_t save_last;
759	  uint32_t i;
760	  uint32_t nwords;
761	  clock_t t_start;
762	  clock_t t_wr;
763	  clock_t t_rd;
764	  uint32_t wr_kbps_x10;
765	  uint32_t rd_kbps_x10;
766	  int ret;
767	
768	  ret = psram_check_no_heap("test");
769	  if (ret < 0)
770	    {
771	      return ret;
772	    }
773	
774	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
775	  if (ret < 0)
776	    {
777	      return ret;
778	    }
779	
780	  if (size_bytes == 0)
781	    {
782	      size_bytes = g_psram_size;
783	    }
784	
785	  if (size_bytes > g_psram_size)
786	    {
787	      size_bytes = g_psram_size;
788	    }
789	
790	  nwords = size_bytes / 4;
791	
792	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
793	         "psram test: range 0x%08lx - 0x%08lx (%lu KB, destructive)\n",
794	         (unsigned long)0x60000000,
795	         (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + size_bytes - 1),
796	         (unsigned long)(size_bytes / 1024));
797	
798	  /* Write phase: each word gets its own byte address */
799	
800	  t_start = clock_systime_ticks();
801	
802	  for (i = 0; i < nwords; i++)
803	    {
804	      base[i] = (uint32_t)(0x60000000 + i * 4);
805	
806	      /* Progress every 1 MB */
807	
808	      if ((i & 0x3ffff) == 0 && i > 0)
809	        {
810	          syslog(LOG_INFO, "  wrote %lu MB\n",
811	                 (unsigned long)(i * 4 / (1024 * 1024)));
812	        }
813	    }
814	
815	  t_wr = clock_systime_ticks() - t_start;
816	
817	  /* Read-and-verify phase */
818	
819	  t_start = clock_systime_ticks();
820	
821	  for (i = 0; i < nwords; i++)
822	    {
823	      uint32_t expected = (uint32_t)(0x60000000 + i * 4);
824	      uint32_t actual = base[i];
825	
826	      if (actual != expected)
827	        {
828	          if (errors == 0)
829	            {
830	              first_bad = 0x60000000 + i * 4;
831	              first_exp = expected;
832	              first_got = actual;
833	            }
834	
835	          errors++;
836	
837	          /* Print first few errors in detail */
838	
839	          if (errors <= 5)
840	            {
841	              syslog(LOG_ERR,
842	                     "  MISMATCH @ 0x%08lx: "
843	                     "expected 0x%08lx, got 0x%08lx\n",
844	                     (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + i * 4),
845	                     (unsigned long)expected,
846	                     (unsigned long)actual);
847	            }
848	        }
849	
850	      /* Progress every 1 MB */
851	
852	      if ((i & 0x3ffff) == 0 && i > 0)
853	        {
854	          syslog(LOG_INFO, "  verified %lu MB\n",
855	                 (unsigned long)(i * 4 / (1024 * 1024)));
856	        }
857	    }
858	
859	  t_rd = clock_systime_ticks() - t_start;
860	
861	  /* KB/s with 1 decimal (integer math: value * 10 / 1024).
862	   * size_bytes * 1000 stays < 2^32 for sizes up to 4 MB per
863	   * phase; for larger sizes the intermediate is still safe
864	   * up to ~16 MB (16M * 1000 = 16G < 2^34, fits uint64_t).
865	   */
866	
867	  if (t_wr > 0)
868	    {
869	      wr_kbps_x10 = (uint32_t)((uint64_t)size_bytes * 1000
870	                     / (uint64_t)t_wr / 1024);
871	    }
872	  else
873	    {
874	      wr_kbps_x10 = 0;
875	    }
876	
877	  if (t_rd > 0)
878	    {
879	      rd_kbps_x10 = (uint32_t)((uint64_t)size_bytes * 1000
880	                     / (uint64_t)t_rd / 1024);
881	    }
882	  else
883	    {
884	      rd_kbps_x10 = 0;
885	    }
886	
887	  /* Boundary check: last word */
888	
889	  last = (volatile uint32_t *)(0x60000000 + g_psram_size - 4);
890	  save_last = *last;
891	  *last = 0xcafebabe;
892	
893	  if (*last != 0xcafebabe)
894	    {
895	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "  BOUNDARY FAIL @ 0x%08lx: "
896	             "wrote 0xcafebabe, read 0x%08lx\n",
897	             (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + g_psram_size - 4),
898	             (unsigned long)*last);
899	      errors++;
900	    }
901	
902	  *last = save_last;
903	
904	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
905	         "psram test: %lu words, %lu errors, "
906	         "%lu.%lu / %lu.%lu KB/s (wr/rd), "
907	         "%lu.%02lu s total\n",
908	         (unsigned long)nwords,
909	         (unsigned long)errors,
910	         (unsigned long)(wr_kbps_x10 / 10),
911	         (unsigned long)(wr_kbps_x10 % 10),
912	         (unsigned long)(rd_kbps_x10 / 10),
913	         (unsigned long)(rd_kbps_x10 % 10),
914	         (unsigned long)((t_wr + t_rd) / TICK_PER_SEC),
915	         (unsigned long)((t_wr + t_rd) % TICK_PER_SEC *
916	                         100 / TICK_PER_SEC));
917	
918	  if (errors > 0)
919	    {
920	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
921	             "psram test: first error @ 0x%08lx "
922	             "(expected 0x%08lx, got 0x%08lx)\n",
923	             (unsigned long)first_bad,
924	             (unsigned long)first_exp,
925	             (unsigned long)first_got);
926	      return -EIO;
927	    }
928	
929	  return OK;
930	}

932	/****************************************************************************
933	 * Name: bk7258_psram_alias
934	 *
935	 * Description:
936	 *   Address alias detection.  Writes distinct patterns at offsets
937	 *   0, 4MB, 8MB, and 16MB-4KB, then re-reads offset 0 to check
938	 *   for aliasing (address wraparound).
939	 *
940	 *   Independent of chip ID — verifies actual usable capacity.
941	 *
942	 * Returned Value:
943	 *   OK if no aliasing detected, -EIO if aliasing found.
944	 *
945	 ****************************************************************************/
946	
947	int bk7258_psram_alias(void)
948	{
949	  volatile uint32_t *base = (volatile uint32_t *)0x60000000;
950	  uint32_t save0;
951	  uint32_t readback;
952	  int ret;
953	  int aliased = 0;
954	
955	  ret = psram_check_no_heap("alias");
956	  if (ret < 0)
957	    {
958	      return ret;
959	    }
960	
961	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
962	  if (ret < 0)
963	    {
964	      return ret;
965	    }
966	
967	  save0 = base[0];
968	
969	  /* Write unique patterns at key offsets */
970	
971	  base[0] = 0xaaaaaaaa;
972	
973	  /* 4 MB offset */
974	
975	  base[0x400000 / 4] = 0x11111111;
976	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
977	         "  wrote 0x11111111 @ 0x%08lx (4 MB)\n",
978	         (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + 0x400000));
979	
980	  /* 8 MB offset */
981	
982	  base[0x800000 / 4] = 0x22222222;
983	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
984	         "  wrote 0x22222222 @ 0x%08lx (8 MB)\n",
985	         (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + 0x800000));
986	
987	  /* 16 MB - 4 KB offset (only meaningful if >= 16MB) */
988	
989	  if (g_psram_size >= 16 * 1024 * 1024)
990	    {
991	      base[(16 * 1024 * 1024 - 4096) / 4] = 0x33333333;
992	      syslog(LOG_INFO,
993	             "  wrote 0x33333333 @ 0x%08lx (16MB-4K)\n",
994	             (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + 16 * 1024 * 1024 - 4096));
995	    }
996	
997	  /* Re-read offset 0 — if it changed, aliasing occurred */
998	
999	  readback = base[0];
1000	
1001	  if (readback != 0xaaaaaaaa)
1002	    {
1003	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
1004	             "psram alias: FAIL — offset 0 changed from "
1005	             "0xaaaaaaaa to 0x%08lx (aliasing!)\n",
1006	             (unsigned long)readback);
1007	      aliased = 1;
1008	    }
1009	
1010	  /* Now check if writing at 8MB clobbers offset 0
1011	   * (would indicate 8MB wraparound)
1012	   */
1013	
1014	  base[0] = 0xbbbbbbbb;
1015	  readback = base[0x800000 / 4];
1016	
1017	  if (readback == 0xbbbbbbbb)
1018	    {
1019	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
1020	             "psram alias: 8 MB offset mirrors offset 0 "
1021	             "(real capacity <= 8 MB)\n");
1022	      aliased = 1;
1023	    }
1024	
1025	  /* Restore */
1026	
1027	  base[0] = save0;
1028	
1029	  if (!aliased)
1030	    {
1031	      syslog(LOG_INFO,
1032	             "psram alias: OK — no aliasing detected "
1033	             "(%lu MB usable)\n",
1034	             (unsigned long)(g_psram_size / (1024 * 1024)));
1035	    }
1036	
1037	  return aliased ? -EIO : OK;
1038	}

1040	/****************************************************************************
1041	 * Name: bk7258_psram_width
1042	 *
1043	 * Description:
1044	 *   Access width test: verifies 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit
1045	 *   read/write to the PSRAM window.  Some controllers only
1046	 *   support word access; this test catches that early.
1047	 *
1048	 *   Uses the first 16 bytes of PSRAM (non-destructive to the
1049	 *   rest).
1050	 *
1051	 * Returned Value:
1052	 *   OK if all widths pass, -EIO if any width fails.
1053	 *
1054	 ****************************************************************************/
1055	
1056	int bk7258_psram_width(void)
1057	{
1058	  volatile uint8_t  *base8  = (volatile uint8_t  *)0x60000000;
1059	  volatile uint16_t *base16 = (volatile uint16_t *)0x60000000;
1060	  volatile uint32_t *base32 = (volatile uint32_t *)0x60000000;
1061	  uint32_t save[4];
1062	  int failures = 0;
1063	  int ret;
1064	
1065	  ret = psram_check_no_heap("width");
1066	  if (ret < 0)
1067	    {
1068	      return ret;
1069	    }
1070	
1071	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
1072	  if (ret < 0)
1073	    {
1074	      return ret;
1075	    }
1076	
1077	  /* Save first 16 bytes */
1078	
1079	  save[0] = base32[0];
1080	  save[1] = base32[1];
1081	  save[2] = base32[2];
1082	  save[3] = base32[3];
1083	
1084	  /* Test 32-bit access */
1085	
1086	  base32[0] = 0xdeadbeef;
1087	  base32[1] = 0xcafebabe;
1088	  if (base32[0] != 0xdeadbeef || base32[1] != 0xcafebabe)
1089	    {
1090	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "  32-bit: FAIL (wrote dead/cafe, "
1091	             "read 0x%08x/0x%08x)\n",
1092	             (unsigned)base32[0], (unsigned)base32[1]);
1093	      failures++;
1094	    }
1095	  else
1096	    {
1097	      syslog(LOG_INFO, "  32-bit: OK\n");
1098	    }
1099	
1100	  /* Test 16-bit access (critical for RGB565 framebuffer) */
1101	
1102	  base16[0] = 0x1234;
1103	  base16[1] = 0x5678;
1104	  base16[2] = 0x9abc;
1105	  base16[3] = 0xdef0;
1106	  if (base16[0] != 0x1234 || base16[1] != 0x5678 ||
1107	      base16[2] != 0x9abc || base16[3] != 0xdef0)
1108	    {
1109	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "  16-bit: FAIL (read 0x%04x/0x%04x/"
1110	             "0x%04x/0x%04x)\n",
1111	             (unsigned)base16[0], (unsigned)base16[1],
1112	             (unsigned)base16[2], (unsigned)base16[3]);
1113	      failures++;
1114	    }
1115	  else
1116	    {
1117	      syslog(LOG_INFO, "  16-bit: OK (RGB565 framebuffer safe)\n");
1118	    }
1119	
1120	  /* Test 8-bit access */
1121	
1122	  base8[0] = 0xaa;
1123	  base8[1] = 0x55;
1124	  base8[2] = 0xff;
1125	  base8[3] = 0x00;
1126	  if (base8[0] != 0xaa || base8[1] != 0x55 ||
1127	      base8[2] != 0xff || base8[3] != 0x00)
1128	    {
1129	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "  8-bit:  FAIL (read 0x%02x/0x%02x/"
1130	             "0x%02x/0x%02x)\n",
1131	             (unsigned)base8[0], (unsigned)base8[1],
1132	             (unsigned)base8[2], (unsigned)base8[3]);
1133	      failures++;
1134	    }
1135	  else
1136	    {
1137	      syslog(LOG_INFO, "  8-bit:  OK\n");
1138	    }
1139	
1140	  /* Restore */
1141	
1142	  base32[0] = save[0];
1143	  base32[1] = save[1];
1144	  base32[2] = save[2];
1145	  base32[3] = save[3];
1146	
1147	  if (failures > 0)
1148	    {
1149	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
1150	             "psram width: %d width(s) FAILED\n", failures);
1151	      return -EIO;
1152	    }
1153	
1154	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1155	         "psram width: all widths OK (8/16/32-bit)\n");
1156	  return OK;
1157	}

1159	/****************************************************************************
1160	 * Name: bk7258_psram_heap_init
1161	 *
1162	 * Description:
1163	 *   Initialize a standalone heap over the PSRAM data window
1164	 *   (0x60000000, g_psram_size bytes).  Uses NuttX mm_initialize()
1165	 *   to create a private heap that does NOT merge with the main
1166	 *   SRAM heap.
1167	 *
1168	 *   Idempotent: calling when g_psram_heap != NULL is a no-op.
1169	 *   Internally ensures the PSRAM controller is initialized.
1170	 *
1171	 * Returned Value:
1172	 *   OK on success, negative errno on failure.
1173	 *
1174	 ****************************************************************************/
1175	
1176	int bk7258_psram_heap_init(void)
1177	{
1178	  int ret;
1179	
1180	  if (g_psram_heap != NULL)
1181	    {
1182	      return OK;
1183	    }
1184	
1185	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
1186	  if (ret < 0)
1187	    {
1188	      return ret;
1189	    }
1190	
1191	  g_psram_heap = mm_initialize("psram",
1192	                                (FAR void *)0x60000000,
1193	                                g_psram_size);
1194	  if (g_psram_heap == NULL)
1195	    {
1196	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "psram heap: mm_initialize failed\n");
1197	      return -ENOMEM;
1198	    }
1199	
1200	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
1201	         "psram heap: ready, base=0x60000000, size=%lu KB\n",
1202	         (unsigned long)(g_psram_size / 1024));
1203	  return OK;
1204	}

1213	 *
1214	 ****************************************************************************/

1217	{

1219	    {
1220	      return NULL;

1235	{

1261	 * Name: bk7258_psram_meminfo
1262	 *
1263	 * Description:
1264	 *   Fill `info` with PSRAM heap statistics.  Equivalent to
1265	 *   mallinfo() but for the PSRAM heap only.

1270	{
1271	  if (info == NULL)
1272	    {
1273	      return;
1274	    }
1275	
1276	  if (g_psram_heap == NULL)
1277	    {

1285	/****************************************************************************
1286	 * Name: bk7258_psram_memalign
1287	 *
1288	 * Description:
1289	 *   Allocate `size` bytes from the PSRAM heap with `alignment`
1290	 *   byte alignment.  Required for DMA targets (DVP, SPI) that
1291	 *   need 32/64-byte aligned buffers.
1292	 *
1293	 *   D-cache note (2026-08): the current defconfig does NOT enable
1294	 *   CONFIG_ARMV8M_DCACHE, so no cache maintenance is needed.
1295	 *   If D-cache is enabled in the future, every buffer written by
1296	 *   DMA must be cache-invalidated before the CPU reads it
1297	 *   (arm_dcache_invalidate / up_invalidate_dcache).
1298	 *   Without this the CPU will read stale cache lines instead of
1299	 *   the DMA data — a data-corruption bug that is very hard to
1300	 *   diagnose after the fact.
1301	 *
1302	 ****************************************************************************/
1303	
1304	FAR void *bk7258_psram_memalign(size_t alignment, size_t size)
1305	{
1306	  if (g_psram_heap == NULL)
1307	    {
1308	      return NULL;
1309	    }
1310	
1311	  /* Reject alignment == 0 and non-power-of-two alignment.
1312	   *
1313	   * mm_memalign() only rejects non-powers of two: its check
1314	   * ((alignment & -alignment) != alignment) lets 0 through, and the
1315	   * subsequent DEBUGASSERT(((uintptr_t)ptr) % alignment == 0) then
1316	   * divides by zero.  Filter it here so a bad caller gets NULL
1317	   * instead of an assertion or an undefined-behaviour trap.
1318	   */
1319	
1320	  if (alignment == 0 || (alignment & (alignment - 1)) != 0)
1321	    {
1322	      syslog(LOG_ERR,
1323	             "psram heap: invalid alignment %zu "
1324	             "(must be a non-zero power of two)\n",
1325	             alignment);
1326	      return NULL;
1327	    }
1328	
1329	  return mm_memalign(g_psram_heap, alignment, size);
1330	}

# BK7258 Power Optimization Round 2: PSRAM Deinit

## Context
Round 1 added `camera_power_off()` (MCLK/PWR/PWDN) + LCD LDO_3V3 off, but exit current barely dropped (~94mA after velapet, ~110mA after hr). Root cause: **PSRAM is never powered off**. `bk7258_psram_init()` enables LDO + AHB power domain + clock, and `g_psram_init_done` guard prevents re-init but nothing ever deinits.

## Key Findings

**PSRAM init sequence** (bk7258_psram.c):
1. `SYS_ANA_REG13` (0x44010134): enpsram=bit31, psldo_swb=bit28, vpsramsel=bit29 — via `ana_write` (SPI-polled RMW)
2. `SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP` (0x44010040): clear PWD_AHBP bit5 to power AHB domain
3. `SYS_CPU_CLK_DIV2` (0x44010024): PSRAM clock sel/div
4. `SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE` (0x44010030): PSRAM_CKEN bit19
5. Auto-detect chip, configure mode registers
6. Set `g_psram_init_done = true`

**Camera PSRAM usage** (bk7258_camera.c):
- `camera_framebuf_alloc()` (line 1742): calls `bk7258_psram_init()`, maps buffers at 0x60000000
- `camera_framebuf_free()` (line 1771): clears pointers + `g_framebuf_allocated = false`, does NOT deinit PSRAM
- `camera_framebuf_free()` only called from `camera_stop()` (line 2900)
- velapet/hr/track/preview exit paths: call `camera_power_off()` but NOT `camera_framebuf_free()`

**LCD PSRAM usage** (bk7258_gc9d01.c):
- Only `lcdtest chunk psram` path (line 5076): calls `bk7258_psram_init()`, no deinit

**Command registration**: NuttX builtin apps in `app/camera/camera_main.c` and `app/lcdtest/lcdtest_main.c`

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Add `camera pwrdump` debug command
**Purpose**: Dump key power registers to confirm PSRAM is the culprit before implementing deinit.

- **File: `board/contest_board/src/bk7258_camera.c`**
  - Add `bk7258_camera_pwrdump()` function that reads and prints:
    - `0x44010030` (SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE) — bit19 PSRAM_CKEN
    - `0x44010040` (SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP) — bit5 PWD_AHBP
    - `0x44010034` (CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG) — bit9 CIS_AUXS
    - `0x44010024` (SYS_CPU_CLK_DIV2) — PSRAM clock
    - `0x44010134` (SYS_ANA_REG13) — PSRAM LDO bits
    - `0x48020008` (YUV_BUF_REG_0x08) — EM_BASE_ADDR
  - Use `getreg32()` for all reads (direct MMIO, no SPI poll needed for reads)

- **File: `board/contest_board/src/bk7258_camera.h`**
  - Add `int bk7258_camera_pwrdump(void);` declaration

- **File: `app/camera/camera_main.c`**
  - Add `"pwrdump"` subcommand dispatch

**Acceptance**: `camera pwrdump` prints register values. Run before/after velapet → diff shows PSRAM bits.

### Step 2: Implement `bk7258_psram_deinit()`
**File: `nuttx/arch/arm/src/bk7258/bk7258_psram.c`**

Strict reverse of init, with idempotent guard:
```c
void bk7258_psram_deinit(void)
{
  uint32_t val;

  if (!g_psram_init_done)
    return;

  /* 1. Disable PSRAM peripheral clock (bit19) */
  val = psram_getreg(SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE);
  val &= ~PSRAM_CKEN_BIT;
  psram_putreg(val, SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE);

  /* 2. Disable PSRAM LDO (ana_reg13 enpsram=0) */
  ana_rmw(SYS_ANA_REG13, 31, 0x1, 0);  /* enpsram = 0 */

  /* 3. Power off AHB domain (set pwd_ahbp bit5) */
  val = psram_getreg(SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP);
  val |= PWD_AHBP_BIT;
  psram_putreg(val, SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP);

  /* 4. Clear init guard for re-init */
  g_psram_init_done = false;

  syslog(LOG_INFO, "psram: deinit — clock off, LDO off, AHB off\n");
}
```

**File: `nuttx/arch/arm/src/bk7258/bk7258_psram.h`**
- Add `void bk7258_psram_deinit(void);` declaration

**Acceptance**: compiles, `camera pwrdump` after deinit shows bit19=0, bit5=1, enpsram=0.

### Step 3: Call deinit from camera/LCD exit paths
**File: `board/contest_board/src/bk7258_camera.c`**

Add `camera_framebuf_free()` + `bk7258_psram_deinit()` to all exit paths that currently only call `camera_power_off()`:

- `bk7258_camera_preview()`: `cleanup_ctrl:` → add after `camera_power_off()`
- `bk7258_camera_track()`: `stop_stream:` and `cleanup_ctrl:` → add after `camera_power_off()`
- `bk7258_camera_velapet()`: `stop_stream:` and `cleanup_ctrl:` → add after `camera_power_off()`
- `bk7258_camera_hr()`: `stop_stream:` and `cleanup_ctrl:` → add after `camera_power_off()`

Pattern for each exit label:
```c
  camera_power_off();
  camera_framebuf_free();
  bk7258_psram_deinit();
```

**File: `board/contest_board/src/bk7258_gc9d01.c`**
- In `lcdtest_chunk()` after the psram test path: add `bk7258_psram_deinit()` when `use_psram` was true

**Acceptance**: After velapet/hr exit, `camera pwrdump` shows PSRAM off. Commands re-run correctly (PSRAM re-inits on demand).

### Step 4: Build + On-board verification
- Build: `cd cmake_out/contest2026_098_board_nsh && ninja -j16` (with ccache in PATH)
- **串表法验证**:
  1. reset → NSH → `camera pwrdump` → record baseline
  2. `camera velapet` → Enter exit → `camera pwrdump` → confirm PSRAM bits off
  3. 拔 Type-C → UT181A 读数应回落到 ~16mA
  4. `camera velapet` 第二遍 → 确认摄像头能重新出图
  5. `camera hr` 退出后同样回到 ~16mA
  6. `lcdtest oeye` 退出后回到 ~16mA
- Update `docs/续航压测_SOP.md` and `docs/技术报告.md` with actual measured numbers

### Step 5: Clean up
- Keep `camera pwrdump` as debug-only command (useful for future power debugging)
- Or remove if user prefers

## Safety Notes
- AHB power domain (PWD_AHBP bit5): confirmed only used by PSRAM. Safe to disable.
- PSRAM LDO (ana_reg13): only supplies PSRAM. Safe to disable.
- `g_psram_init_done = false` ensures next `bk7258_psram_init()` runs full sequence including LDO + AHB + clock + chip detect.
- `camera_framebuf_free()` clears pointers so no stale 0x60xxxxxx references remain after PSRAM is off.
- `g_framebuf_allocated = false` ensures next command re-allocates framebuf (which triggers PSRAM re-init).

 * Description:

 *   current after command exit.  Compares PSRAM, camera, and LCD domains.

int bk7258_camera_pwrdump(void)
{
  uint32_t dev_clk   = getreg32(0x44010030);  /* SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE */
  uint32_t pwr_wake  = getreg32(0x44010040);  /* SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP */
  uint32_t cam_clk   = getreg32(0x44010034);  /* CAMERA_CLK_EN_REG */
  uint32_t clk_div2  = getreg32(0x44010024);  /* SYS_CPU_CLK_DIV2 */
  uint32_t ana13     = getreg32(0x44010134);  /* SYS_ANA_REG13 */
  uint32_t yuv_glob  = getreg32(0x48020008);  /* YUV_BUF global ctrl */

  syslog(LOG_INFO,
         "[pwrdump] 0x44010030 DEV_CLK     = 0x%08lx  "
         "PSRAM_CKEN(bit19)=%lu  SPI1_CKEN(bit9)=%lu\n",
         (unsigned long)dev_clk,
         (unsigned long)((dev_clk >> 19) & 1),
         (unsigned long)((dev_clk >> 9) & 1));

  syslog(LOG_INFO,
         "[pwrdump] 0x44010040 PWR_WAKEUP  = 0x%08lx  "
         "PWD_AHBP(bit5)=%lu (0=on,1=off)\n",
         (unsigned long)pwr_wake,
         (unsigned long)((pwr_wake >> 5) & 1));

  syslog(LOG_INFO,
         "[pwrdump] 0x44010034 CAM_CLK_EN  = 0x%08lx  "
         "CIS_AUXS(bit9)=%lu  H264(bit0)=%lu  YUV_BUF(bit3)=%lu\n",
         (unsigned long)cam_clk,
         (unsigned long)((cam_clk >> 9) & 1),
         (unsigned long)((cam_clk >> 0) & 1),

  syslog(LOG_INFO,
         "[pwrdump] 0x44010024 CLK_DIV2    = 0x%08lx  "
         "PSRAM_CKSEL(bit5)=%lu  PSRAM_CKDIV(bit4)=%lu\n",
         (unsigned long)clk_div2,
         (unsigned long)((clk_div2 >> 5) & 1),
         (unsigned long)((clk_div2 >> 4) & 1));

  syslog(LOG_INFO,
         "[pwrdump] 0x44010134 ANA_REG13   = 0x%08lx  "
         "enpsram(bit31)=%lu  psldo_swb(bit28)=%lu  vpsramsel=%lu\n",
         (unsigned long)ana13,
